Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

providers.name: Cajal Technologies
providers.description: Cajal Technologies (Cajal) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (W26) company scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. Its multi-agent system, Tau, collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean, deploying AI mathematicians across high-impact applied domains starting with quantum computing and finance. Tau verifies compiled binaries with mathematical certainty down to the machine level. Cajal also partners with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems through datasets, evals, and RL environments, and open-sources tooling such as Talos, a Wasm interpreter written in Lean designed for reasoning.

providers.name: Optivolt Labs
providers.description: Optivolt Labs (operating as Optivolt) is a Burlingame, California solar technology company building intelligent home solar systems with power electronics embedded directly inside each panel. Its patented Balancer device shuffles power from stronger to weaker zones within a panel to keep energy flowing in shaded and non-ideal conditions, delivering up to 50% more annual energy and improved shaded performance versus conventional panels. The product line includes 450W N-type mono half-cut panels, universal battery and inverter compatibility, and a real-time monitoring app for tracking energy and savings. Optivolt is a Techstars-backed hardware company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: SiMa
providers.description: SiMa.ai is a Silicon Valley machine-learning semiconductor company building a co-optimized hardware and software platform for physical AI at the edge. Its MLSoC (Machine Learning System-on-Chip) family — including the Modalix line delivering roughly 50 TOPS under 10 watts in multiple form factors — targets drones, robotics, automotive, industrial, retail, government, and healthcare. The developer experience centers on the Palette software suite and an agentic development environment that compiles and deploys computer-vision and multimodal models onto SiMa silicon, backed by a Developer Center, a model browser, a Hugging Face model hub (simaai), and a community forum. SiMa.ai ships downloadable SDK/CLI tooling and evaluation hardware (Modalix DevKit) rather than a hosted public HTTP API.

providers.name: Ali Tech
providers.description: Ali Tech (operating as Xaim) is an AI infrastructure platform that gives startups and AI-driven businesses affordable, predictable compute for running AI workloads. Instead of token-based pricing, Xaim sells reserved processing capacity so teams can reduce processing costs without modifying their existing AI models. The platform is delivered as APIs through an Azure API Management developer portal, and advertises three products - a Compute API for running existing AI models cost effectively, an Insights API for real-time performance-optimization signals, and an Automation API for automating and scaling AI processes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Appwrite GraphQL
providers.description: Appwrite GraphQL is a powerful API layer that exposes the full Appwrite backend-as-a-service platform through a GraphQL interface, allowing developers to query and mutate any resource type including databases, storage, users, and functions. It mirrors the complete Appwrite REST API (except OAuth) with GraphQL advantages such as selection sets and query batching, enabling precise data fetching and multiple operations in a single request.

providers.name: Clone
providers.description: Clone Robotics develops musculoskeletal, intelligent humanoid androids and robotic hands built on Myofiber, its artificial-muscle technology pioneered in 2021, driven by water-based hydraulics and biomimetic joints. Its flagship Clone Alpha is a full-body biomimetic humanoid with synthetic organs; the Clone Hand is its foundational dexterous-manipulation platform. The developer surface is a first-party Python client (clone_client) exposing a high-level gRPC (proto3) API to directly control the Clone Robot over the local network — actuating muscles via impulses/pulses/pressures, driving pinch and hydra valves, managing the water-pump pressure source, streaming IMU/pose/joint telemetry, and configuring cameras. There is no public HTTP/REST API or hosted endpoint; control is LAN-scoped gRPC discovered over zeroconf/mDNS by robot name or IP. Co-founded 2021 by Dhanush Radhakrishna and Lukasz Kozlik.

providers.name: Udacity
providers.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

providers.name: Hadrian
providers.description: Hadrian (Hadrian Automation) is a Los Angeles-area precision-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power, building software-driven, AI-powered factories that produce high-tolerance machined components for the aerospace and defense industrial base — including parts for rockets, satellites, jets, drones, and missiles. The company's core software stack is Opus, described as a full-stack, AI-powered Factory Autonomy platform that interprets legacy engineering designs, automates CNC machining, inspection, tool-path optimization, adaptive programming, scheduling, and quality assurance, and enables new operators to be productive in 30 days or less. Hadrian operates multiple factories — Factory 2 (F2) and Factory X (FX) in Torrance, California, and Factory 3 (F3) in Mesa, Arizona — and offers three commercial models: precision component manufacturing, Manufacturing-as-a-Service (dedicated automation cells for a single customer), and Factories-as-a-Service (turnkey factory design and operation). Customers and partners include major aerospace and defense primes such as Lockheed Martin. Hadrian has also launched an additive manufacturing division to expand U.S. defense production capacity. The Opus platform is internal-only — Hadrian sells finished precision parts and factory capacity, not software access — and there is no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release for Opus or any Hadrian system.

providers.name: Projectx
providers.description: ProjectX is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building Infinity (InfinityOS), a cloud operating system designed for AI agents. Infinity lets agents and humans orchestrate GPU workloads through a chat interface rather than traditional APIs, running multiple Windows and Linux applications — such as Blender, VS Code, DaVinci Resolve, Unreal Engine, and Isaac Sim — simultaneously, each on its own independent compute and GPU inside a single shared browser-based workspace with sub-minute cold starts. A public API, developer docs, status page, changelog, and blog are announced as coming soon; no programmatic API surface is published yet.

providers.name: Achronix Semiconductor
providers.description: Achronix Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company specializing in high-performance FPGA (field-programmable gate array) products and embedded FPGA (eFPGA) intellectual property. Its portfolio includes the Speedster7t family of standalone FPGAs, Speedcore eFPGA IP for system-on-chip integration, VectorPath PCIe accelerator cards, and the ACE design tools suite for synthesis, verification, and optimization. Achronix technology targets AI/ML inference, 5G/6G networking, data-center compute acceleration, automotive, SmartNICs, and test-and-measurement workloads. The company is privately held and backed by investors including Battery Ventures. It exposes no public web/REST API or developer API portal; its developer surface is a hardware support portal, product documentation, datasheets, and design tools.

providers.name: ams OSRAM
providers.description: ams OSRAM (ams-OSRAM AG) is a global leader in innovative optical solutions, designing and manufacturing intelligent sensors, emitters, and light-based semiconductors. Formed from the 2020 combination of ams AG (Austria) and OSRAM (Germany), the company builds LEDs, VCSEL and edge-emitting lasers, CMOS image sensors, ambient light and proximity sensors, direct time-of-flight (dToF) sensors, photodiodes, and LED/VCSEL driver ICs. Its sensing, illumination, and visualization technologies serve automotive and mobility (headlamps, interior lighting, ADAS), industrial automation and robotics, medical and healthcare devices, mobile and wearable devices, computing, and general lighting. Headquartered in Premstaetten, Austria and Munich, Germany, ams OSRAM employs roughly 18,500 people across 25 R&D sites and holds over 12,000 patents. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of iconiq-capital and enriched from ams OSRAM public web pages; the company exposes product/design support and a download center rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Anker Innovations
providers.description: Anker Innovations is a global consumer-electronics company headquartered in Shenzhen, China, known for its Anker charging and power products, Soundcore audio, eufy smart-home and security devices, Nebula projectors, and Anker SOLIX portable power and solar storage. Through the Anker Open Platform (developer.anker.com) the company exposes a developer surface that lets partners integrate and control Anker devices from their own applications via API and SDK, gated behind an Open Platform login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and is being enriched with the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Aurora Networks
providers.description: Aurora Networks is the broadband and access networks brand of Vistance Networks, Inc. (Nasdaq: VISN), the company CommScope renamed itself to in January 2026 after divesting its Connectivity and Cable Solutions segment to Amphenol. Aurora Networks builds end-to-end access network infrastructure for global cable and broadband service providers: HFC and PON access systems, cable headend optics platforms, CMTS and CCAP gear, Distributed Access Architecture (DAA) devices, optical hubs, nodes and passives, RF and RFoG equipment, and video processing, security and delivery systems. Its ServAssure NXT family adds network performance management, alarm handling and service assurance software on top of that hardware estate. The brand originates with Aurora Networks, Inc., founded in Santa Clara, California in 1999 as a pure-play optical transport supplier to cable operators, backed by Battery Ventures among ten investors across roughly $60M raised, and acquired by Pace plc for $323M in 2013 before passing through ARRIS and CommScope. Aurora Networks is a network equipment vendor rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable API specification. Product and integration documentation, including the ServAssure NXT web service and message-bus integration surfaces, sits behind authenticated customer support portals.

providers.name: C-Infinity
providers.description: C-Infinity is a Mountain View, California company founded in 2023 that builds foundational AI for mechanical design and manufacturing — AI that reasons about geometry, motion, spatial constraints, and production logic. Its platform, AutoAssembler, connects directly to existing CAD and PLM environments to automate assembly process planning, accelerate engineering change order (ECO) reviews, and generate production-ready assembly work instructions, compressing work that historically took weeks into minutes. The product is described by the company as API-first, with an integration layer that connects upstream to engineering systems and downstream to production, but as of July 2026 C-Infinity publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition — the AutoAssembler application is gated behind a request-a-demo flow and integration is arranged directly with the company. C-Infinity raised a $16M round in April 2026 led by Canaan Partners, with participation from Inventus Capital, Bee Partners, and Radius Capital, and reports deployments across Global Fortune 100 manufacturers as well as small and mid-sized enterprises.

providers.name: Cognichip
providers.description: Cognichip is an AI-first semiconductor company revolutionizing the way chips are designed. Its core technology, Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI), is built on what the company describes as the world's first physics-informed foundation AI model tailored for chip design, positioning ACI as a new scaling factor for semiconductors. ACI aims to understand, learn, and solve chip design problems with designer-level cognitive abilities, reducing design effort by roughly 75% and cutting completion time in half to address the industry bottleneck where chip development can take three to five years. Founded by semiconductor and AI veterans including CEO Faraj Aalaei and CTO Ehsan Kamalinejad, the company is backed by Lux Capital, Mayfield, and Seligman Ventures, has Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan on its board, and was named to Fast Company's World's Most Innovative Companies of 2026. Added to the API Evangelist network and enriched by the pipeline; the company publishes a marketing and corporate presence today with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Jays
providers.description: JAYS is a Swedish consumer audio brand founded in 2006 by Jens and Johan, headquartered in Sweden and owned by the Northbaze Group AB. It designs and sells wireless and wired headphones, true-wireless earbuds, Bluetooth and multiroom speakers, and audio accessories, sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at jaysheadphones.com. JAYS publishes no first-party developer API; its only machine-accessible surface is the Shopify-provided agent-commerce layer: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint, Customer Account OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, and an llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio/commitment lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Luminal
providers.description: Luminal is an AI inference-optimization company that compiles machine-learning models ahead-of-time into optimized native code for GPUs and ASICs, aiming to deliver the fastest, highest-throughput inference available. Its core product is an open-source, high-performance general-purpose inference compiler written in Rust (the "luminal" crate), built around static computation graphs, a compile-time-checked GraphTensor API, composable neural-network modules, and pluggable graph compilers. Luminal ships two deployment paths: Luminal Cloud, a managed serverless inference service with automatic scaling, and licensed on-prem deployment with dedicated support and custom optimization. The company is backed by Felicis.

providers.name: MaxLinear
providers.description: MaxLinear, Inc. (NASDAQ: MXL) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Carlsbad, California that designs radio-frequency (RF), high-performance analog, and mixed-signal communications systems-on-chip (SoCs) for critical network infrastructure, the connected home, and industrial and multi-market applications. Its products integrate RF, analog, mixed-signal, digital signal processing, security engines, data compression, networking, and power management into single chips that power cable and fiber broadband modems, Wi-Fi 6/7 and wireline home routers, optical transceivers, 4G/5G base-station and backhaul infrastructure, and high-speed data-center interconnects. MaxLinear exposes developer surface primarily as hardware/firmware SDKs and C APIs (for example the Panther Storage Acceleration SDK and the MxL890x Raw Acceleration API) delivered with its silicon, along with design tools, simulation models, and a technical documentation library — it does not publish a public web/REST API. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Mubit
providers.description: Mubit is a temporary storage and logistics service based in Guadalajara, Mexico, offering on-demand collection, climate-controlled warehousing, digital photo inventory, and delivery for both individuals and businesses. Customers pay only for the space they use, with free pickup and drop-off, optional professional packing, and 24/7 CCTV-monitored facilities across three warehouses (Colli, Tijera, and Casuarina). Backed by 500 Global and Techstars, the company reports 4,000+ customers and a 4.9-star Google rating, and operates a mobile/web customer portal at clientes.mubit.co for scheduling pickups and deliveries and viewing stored items. Mubit publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Sunday Robotics
providers.description: Sunday Robotics is a consumer robotics company building Memo, an autonomous home robot that handles household chores such as clearing dishes, loading the dishwasher, pulling espresso shots, and folding laundry. The robot is trained on human demonstrations captured with the company's proprietary Skill Capture Glove and runs on the ACT family of robot foundation models. Founded as a physical-AI company and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Sunday is pre-launch with a beta program opening in late 2026. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this record captures its public web and security surface only.

providers.name: Vital Lyfe
providers.description: Vital Lyfe is a Torrance, California hardware company building portable water purification technology designed to scale where infrastructure cannot reach. Its flagship product, Access, is a portable watermaker that converts naturally occurring water, including saltwater, into clean drinking water through a simple place-a-hose, press-start, hydrate workflow. The company sells the Access device and branded gear through a direct-to-consumer Shopify storefront and publishes a mission, team, careers, and journal. It was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass, Vital Lyfe is a consumer-hardware and e-commerce brand with no public API, SDK, or developer program surface.

providers.name: Medivis
providers.description: Medivis is a medical technology company building AI-powered augmented reality solutions for surgery and medical education. Its flagship product, SurgicalAR, is an FDA 510(k)-cleared platform that runs on Microsoft HoloLens 2 and transforms 2D medical imaging (CT and MRI) into interactive 3D holographic visualizations for surgical planning and navigation, including FDA-cleared systems for spine and cranial procedures. Medivis also offers AnatomyX, an AR platform for anatomy and medical education. The company reports deployment across 40+ institutions and use in 2,000+ surgeries. Medivis is a Microsoft technology partner and a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Medivis publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its software surface is delivered as HoloLens and iOS applications for clinical and educational users.

providers.name: Mira
providers.description: Mira is a San Francisco-based consumer hardware startup building AI-powered smart glasses positioned as an always-on "second brain." Founded in 2024 by Harvard builders AnhPhu Nguyen and Caine Ardayfio (rebranded from Halo), the camera-free glasses pair a dual-waveguide display, microphone, and iOS companion app to deliver live transcription, real-time translation across 60+ languages, hands-free AI assistance, and searchable memory of everyday conversations. Mira raised a $6.6M seed round led by General Catalyst and began shipping its first devices in January 2026. It is a privacy-first consumer wearable with an iOS companion app and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Modular Robotics
providers.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot. The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: W. R. Grace
providers.description: W. R. Grace & Co. is a global producer of specialty chemicals and specialty materials, providing catalysts and process technologies to refining, petrochemical, and other manufacturers. Grace operates in two segments: Catalysts Technologies (fluid catalytic cracking catalysts, additives, and process technologies) and Materials Technologies (silica-based engineered materials for pharmaceutical, food, coatings, and industrial applications). Grace's Fine Chemical Manufacturing Services division provides active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) development and manufacturing for the pharmaceutical industry. W. R. Grace does not offer a public developer API for software integration.

providers.name: Carbon
providers.description: Carbon is a digital manufacturing company that builds an integrated 3D printing platform combining Digital Light Synthesis (DLS) printing hardware, advanced photopolymer resins, and cloud-connected computational design software. Its technology enables production-scale additive manufacturing of end-use polymer parts across automotive, medical, dental, consumer goods, and industrial applications, with the Design Engine tool for lattice and part design and the Carbon Academy knowledge base for operational guidance. Carbon is a frontier-tech portfolio company backed by GV. As of this profile Carbon exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or event surface; enrichment is limited to verified company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Hidrate
providers.description: HidrateSpark is the world's smartest water bottle brand, tracking daily water intake with a Bluetooth-connected sensor puck that glows to remind you to drink and syncs to the HidrateSpark hydration app, Fitbit, and Apple Watch. The company (originally Hidrate, Inc., a Techstars-backed startup) sells its smart bottles and accessories through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at hidratespark.com. It does not publish a first-party developer or product API; the only machine-facing surface is the Shopify platform layer — OIDC/OAuth customer accounts and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-commerce endpoints that let buyer-approved AI shopping agents browse and check out.

providers.name: Owl Labs
providers.description: Owl Labs is a Boston-based video conferencing hardware and software company building smart devices for hybrid meetings. Its flagship Meeting Owl line is a 360-degree AI-powered camera, microphone, and speaker that automatically focuses on whoever is speaking, alongside accessories such as the Owl Bar, Whiteboard Owl, and Expansion Mic. The Nest is its cloud fleet-management platform for provisioning, updating, and monitoring deployed devices across an organization. Owl Labs sells to enterprises, schools, and distributed teams, and publishes an annual State of Hybrid Work report. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and Playground Global. Owl Labs does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Reframe
providers.description: Reframe (usereframe.ai) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, founded in 2025 by Bryan Zin (previously a Product Design Engineer on the iPhone team at Apple) and Eric Wiener, building an AI-native hardware procurement platform. Reframe automates the manual procurement process in hardware supply chains: instead of emails and spreadsheets, AI agents handle purchase orders, supplier follow-ups, and part tracking for both COTS and custom-manufactured components, with Slack and Gmail integrations for team workflows. This API Evangelist profile tracks Reframe as a company in the network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Versuni
providers.description: Versuni is a global domestic-appliances company headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands, formed when Philips Domestic Appliances was carved out and acquired by Hillhouse Investment in 2021. With more than 130 years of heritage, roughly 6,400 employees and a presence in over 100 countries, Versuni designs and sells cooking, coffee, garment-care, floor-care and climate-care products under brands including Philips, Saeco, Gaggia, Preethi, Senseo and L'OR Barista. Its connected appliances are supported by the consumer HomeID app (formerly NutriU). Versuni publishes no public developer API program; its public API-adjacent surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt and a responsible-disclosure program.

providers.name: 1X Technologies
providers.description: 1X Technologies (formerly Halodi Robotics) is a Norwegian-American humanoid robotics company building general-purpose bipedal robots designed to live and work alongside people. Founded in 2014 in Norway by Bernt Øyvind Børnich, the company is now headquartered in Palo Alto, California with R&D and manufacturing presence in Moss, Norway and a new vertically integrated NEO factory in Hayward, California. 1X is backed by the OpenAI Startup Fund, EQT Ventures, Tiger Global, Samsung NEXT, and others through Series A2 ($23.5M, 2023), Series B ($100M, 2024), and a $1B raise reported in 2025. Its commercial robots are EVE — a wheeled upper-humanoid deployed in industrial and security settings since 2022 — and NEO, a bipedal home humanoid that began pre-orders October 28, 2025 at $20,000 (or $499/month) with consumer deliveries in 2026. 1X also acquired Kind Humanoid (Jan 2025) and announced a partnership to deploy up to 10,000 NEO robots into EQT portfolio company factories and warehouses between 2026 and 2030. Unlike most humanoid robotics vendors, 1X publishes meaningful open-source artifacts: the EVE ROS2 API (custom WholeBodyTrajectory and DrivingCommand message types) and the halodi-messages package on GitHub under Apache-2.0, plus the 1X World Model Challenge with 100+ hours of vector-quantized EVE observations and GENIE baseline models released on Hugging Face. There is no public REST/HTTP developer API or hosted developer portal — the developer surface is ROS2 messages, robot models in URDF, and the world-model dataset/model artifacts.

providers.name: Camfer
providers.description: Camfer is a Y Combinator-backed startup (S24) building an AI mechanical engineer — an AI-powered CAD tool that plugs into SolidWorks and lets engineers generate parametric designs from natural language prompts and images. Its camfy text-to-CAD model produces editable feature-tree geometry, automates repetitive modeling tasks, answers questions about a model without manual feature-tree navigation, and gives real-time design feedback. The product is a downloadable desktop application (currently in invite-only beta), not a public API; the company is backed by Y Combinator, Next47, Bloomberg Beta, Octave Fund, and the founders of Dropbox, Airtable, and Clari.

providers.name: Classiq
providers.description: Classiq Technologies is a Tel Aviv, Israel headquartered enterprise quantum software company founded in 2020 by Nir Minerbi (CEO), Amir Naveh (CPO), and Dr. Yehuda Naveh (CTO), positioning itself as a high-level quantum algorithm design platform that lets organizations build, scale, and deploy quantum algorithms across any hardware or simulator without writing low-level gate code. Its flagship offering centers on Qmod, an intuitive quantum modeling language, and a hardware-aware synthesis engine that compiles functional quantum models into optimized circuits with constraint-driven optimization, transpilation, and execution session management across cloud quantum providers including AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, GCP, IBM Quantum, IonQ, OQC, Alice and Bob, and C12. The platform is delivered through the Classiq Studio web IDE at platform.classiq.io, a public Python SDK (`pip install classiq`) currently at version 1.14.0 covering synthesis, execution, analysis, and application libraries for chemistry (QSP), finance (IQAE), and quantum machine learning (QSVM, QML), plus an AI-assisted natural language interface for algorithm design. Classiq publishes the largest open quantum algorithm library on GitHub at github.com/Classiq/classiq-library (2,000+ stars, Jupyter Notebook, MIT license) with reference implementations across optimization, linear solvers, quantum machine learning, chemistry, finance, logistics, cybersecurity, and physical systems. Customers include Microsoft, AWS, NVIDIA, HSBC, Citibank, BMW, and Rolls-Royce; the company is SOC 2 and GDPR compliant. Classiq has raised over $200M including a $110M Series C in May 2025 with backers such as AMD Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures, IonQ, Bank Leumi, Mirae Asset Capital, and SoftBank. Classiq's developer surface is the Python SDK and Qmod language — there is no public REST API or OpenAPI specification; the Mintlify-hosted `docs.classiq.io/api-reference/openapi.json` endpoint currently returns the default Mintlify Plant Store placeholder rather than a real API contract.

providers.name: Provenmetal
providers.description: ProvenMetal is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building fast-turn, American-made printed circuit board (PCB) assembly. The company lets customers upload a Gerber file, automatically infers the board specification, and returns instant quoting for a 7-day standard turnaround with no expedite fees. ProvenMetal automates the traditional manufacturing bottlenecks — part procurement, design for manufacturability (DFM) review, and assembly — and performs 100% X-ray inspection of every board (AI-assisted, cited at 99.8% confidence) before shipment, including the inspection data with each order. It is a domestic B2B PCB manufacturing service aimed at reshoring electronics production, operated out of San Francisco. As of this profile ProvenMetal exposes a customer ordering portal at order.provenmetal.com but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Albemarle
providers.description: Albemarle Corporation is a global specialty chemicals company and leading provider of lithium, bromine, and other essential elements. Operating from its global headquarters in Charlotte, NC, Albemarle serves customers in approximately 70 countries with world-class hard-rock and brine lithium resources, state-of-the-art lithium conversion facilities, advanced lithium material and process development, bromine production facilities, and the US's only producing lithium resource in Silver Peak, NV. The company serves critical markets including electric vehicle batteries, energy storage, flame retardants, pharmaceutical ingredients, catalysts, and specialty chemicals, employing approximately 7,800 people and holding over 1,500 active patents worldwide.

providers.name: Tile (thetileapp)
providers.description: Tile is a consumer Bluetooth-tracker company whose Tile Mate, Pro, Slim, and Sticker devices help people find everyday items such as keys, wallets, bags, and phones, backed by the crowd-sourced Tile "Find" network that anonymously relays location when another Tile user passes a lost item. Founded in 2012, Tile was acquired by Life360 in 2021 and now operates as part of the Life360 family-safety platform. Tile publishes consumer apps for iOS and Android and a support and legal surface, but does not offer an official public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; only third-party community libraries wrap its private app API. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web and security-program surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Aitomatic
providers.description: Aitomatic, Inc. (Palo Alto, CA) builds DanaOS, an operating system for industrial AI. DanaOS is a governed, neurosymbolic, self-improving platform that runs autonomous AI agents inside a customer's own boundary — for semiconductor fabs, building and process operations, energy grids, and heavy industry. It combines neural flexibility with symbolic precision: a Sector Ontology encodes domain expertise as executable knowledge, Small Specialist Agents (SSAs) reason over it in a See-Think-Act-Reflect loop, and a governance substrate (the Dana Ontologist) verifies every action against ontology and policy before it commits — all deployable on-prem and air-gapped. Aitomatic is a founding member of the AI Alliance and publishes the open-source Dana agent-native language, the OpenSSA framework, and SemiKong, the first open-source semiconductor-industry LLM. Founded by Christopher Nguyen (CEO).

providers.name: Dyndrite
providers.description: Dyndrite develops GPU-accelerated software for digital and additive manufacturing, focused on laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and other metal 3D-printing processes. Its platform streamlines build preparation, materials development, process qualification, and production automation for industrial manufacturers, machine builders (OEMs), and software vendors. Products include Dyndrite LPBF Pro for end users and the Application Development Kit (ADK) for machine makers, exposing low-level toolpathing control (Vector and Raster Toolpathing APIs) plus a scriptable Python geometry engine. Dyndrite is backed by Amplify Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an AI/ML and manufacturing automation company. It does not currently publish a public web/REST API, OpenAPI definition, or self-service developer portal; its APIs are embedded scripting and integration interfaces delivered inside its desktop software and ADK.

providers.name: MosaicML
providers.description: MosaicML was a San Francisco-based foundation model training company founded in 2021 by Naveen Rao and Hanlin Tang to make large-scale model training faster and cheaper through algorithmic and systems efficiency. Databricks acquired MosaicML in July 2023 for approximately $1.3 billion and folded the team and platform into Databricks Mosaic AI Research. The MosaicML training platform is now delivered as Databricks Mosaic AI Training (pretraining and finetuning), and the original mosaicml.com domain redirects to the Databricks Mosaic Research microsite. MosaicML's surviving open-source artifacts include Composer (a PyTorch training library with built-in speedup recipes), Streaming (a cloud-native dataset format for efficient distributed training), LLM Foundry (the training code behind Databricks' DBRX foundation model), the Diffusion training stack, and the MCLI command line and Python SDK that orchestrate Pretraining and Finetuning jobs against the managed training service. The Mosaic AI Training service itself is accessed exclusively through the MCLI command line, the mosaicml-cli Python SDK, and Databricks workspace integrations — there is no publicly published REST OpenAPI surface for the training control plane. Commercial access requires a Databricks account; pricing is consumption-based via Databricks DBU billing rather than an independent MosaicML pricing page.

providers.name: Polaron
providers.description: Polaron is a London-based AI software company that builds "the intelligence layer for materials science." Its platform applies machine learning to microscopy and image data to automate microstructure analysis, connecting process, structure, and performance so materials engineering teams can characterise, design, and manufacture materials faster and with less uncertainty. The platform centers on three core model families: Segmentation (identifying and measuring microstructural features), Reconstruction (converting 2D micrographs into 3D representations), and Design (optimising microstructural parameters). It is applied across batteries, metals and alloys, composites, ceramics, additive manufacturing, and pharmaceuticals, spanning R&D, quality and qualification, and modelling and simulation workflows. Polaron is backed by Speedinvest and research institutions including Imperial College London, Manchester, Oxford, and Cambridge.

providers.name: Rabbit
providers.description: Rabbit Inc. is a consumer technology company building AI-powered devices, best known for the Rabbit R1, a $199 handheld AI companion with industrial design by Teenage Engineering. The R1 runs rabbitOS and centers on a Large Action Model (LAM) that automates tasks across operating systems and applications (DLAM), alongside features like the Magic Camera, voice recording with transcription, and vibe-coded "creations." Rabbit is a portfolio company of a16z. As of this profile, Rabbit is a consumer hardware and device company with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site, support center, blog, and newsroom.

providers.name: Condor Energy
providers.description: Condor Energy is an AI-powered energy management operating system for enterprise energy procurement, built for industrial companies, retailers, and data center operators who buy electricity at scale. The platform aggregates consumption data, PPAs, solar, batteries, and live market data into real-time dashboards; models load against market dynamics to execute hedging strategies and produce board-ready price-risk reporting; and analyzes granular load data to find flexibility opportunities and evaluate ROI on solar, battery, EV-charging, and hybrid investments. Founded in 2026 by former electricity traders and energy physicists, the Paris-based company is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company. No public API, developer portal, or SDK is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Imajin
providers.description: Imajin is an Indonesian online manufacturing marketplace (the "Indonesia Manufacturing Hub") that connects buyers with vetted manufacturers and machine shops through a project-based workflow: post a project, receive quotes, and track production through to delivery. It brokers rapid 3D printing and prototyping, high-precision mold and die making, SPM and custom part fabrication, mass production (stamping, plastics, and fabrication), CNC milling and turning at machining centers, and broader manufacturing projects. The platform offers an instant-quote tool, real-time project notifications, integrated company profiles, team and project management, and up-front payment handling for suppliers. Imajin is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)
providers.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a leading American technology integrator providing full life cycle services and solutions in the technical, engineering, and enterprise information technology markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC serves the U.S. federal government with approximately $7.4 billion in annual revenues. The company delivers IT modernization, cloud computing, digital transformation, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and data analytics solutions primarily for defense, intelligence, and civilian government customers. SAIC's open source presence is at github.com/saic-oss with DevSecOps tools including Anvil (CI/CD container) and terraform modules for Kubernetes sandboxes.

providers.name: Agility Robotics
providers.description: Agility Robotics is a Salem, Oregon humanoid robotics company building industrial bipedal robots for warehouse and factory automation. Founded in 2015 as a spin-out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Laboratory, its flagship product is Digit — described as the first humanoid robot in commercial production deployment — and Arc, the cloud-based automation platform that operates Digit fleets, provides real-time visibility, manages task assignments, and connects Digit to existing warehouse automation including AMRs, WMS, and WES systems. Digit has commercial deployments and pilots with Amazon, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre, with an expanded NVIDIA partnership for foundation-model and simulation tooling. Agility operates RoboFab, a humanoid robot factory in Salem, OR with capacity to produce 10,000 robots annually. Digit has surpassed 100,000 totes moved in commercial deployment at a single Georgia facility. Agility Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Digit or Arc; integration is performed by Agility's solutions team and partners through a gated low-level JSON-over-WebSocket API and pysdk delivered with the robot. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (JFrog, Bazel, Fluent Bit, Kubernetes Cluster API) plus an archived documentation repo for the earlier Cassie research platform.

providers.name: COMSOL
providers.description: COMSOL is a Swedish-American engineering software company best known for COMSOL Multiphysics, a desktop platform for physics-based simulation. The platform exposes a unified COMSOL API that powers the GUI, the Application Builder (Java-based Method Editor), LiveLink for MATLAB, LiveLink for Excel, and the LiveLink family of CAD/CAE interfacing products (SOLIDWORKS, Inventor, AutoCAD, Revit, Solid Edge, CATIA V5, MATLAB, Simulink, Excel). COMSOL is primarily licensed desktop software with web deployment via COMSOL Server and standalone applications via COMSOL Compiler. There is no public web REST API and no public GitHub SDK organization; programmatic surfaces are the Java API, the MATLAB LiveLink interface, and the module-specific LiveLink integrations bundled with the licensed product.

providers.name: FANUC
providers.description: FANUC Corporation is a Japanese multinational headquartered in Oshino, Yamanashi at the base of Mount Fuji, and is one of the world's largest suppliers of factory automation, industrial robots, and CNC (computer numerical control) systems. Founded in 1972 after spinning out of Fujitsu's numerical control division (originated 1955) under Seiuemon Inaba, FANUC pioneered commercial NC and CNC technology and by the early 1980s held roughly half of the global CNC market. The company operates three primary business segments: FA (CNC systems, servo motors, lasers, and PMC controls for machine tools), Robot (industrial arms from the LR Mate and M-series through the heavy-payload M-2000iA, plus the CRX collaborative robot family), and ROBOMACHINE (ROBODRILL machining centers, ROBOCUT wire EDM, and ROBOSHOT all-electric injection molding machines). FANUC's primary developer surface is FOCAS (FANUC Open CNC API Specification), a licensed C/C++ library (fwlib32.dll) used by machine builders and MES/OEE vendors to read CNC state over Ethernet, plus KAREL and Teach Pendant (TP) programming on the robot controllers and a published ROS 2 driver for the CRX collaborative arms. FANUC does not operate a public REST developer portal or publish OpenAPI specifications; integrations are partner-driven through MTConnect adapters, OPC UA servers, FIELD system edge apps, and the FANUC America customer/training portals.

providers.name: KUKA
providers.description: KUKA AG is a German industrial automation company headquartered in Augsburg, Bavaria, founded in 1898 and majority-owned by China's Midea Group since 2016. KUKA designs and manufactures industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), production cells, controllers, and the software stack that drives them. Its product portfolio spans six-axis articulated robots (KR series), sensitive collaborative robots (LBR iiwa, LBR iisy), mobile platforms (KMR iiwa, KMP), and palletizing/welding/CNC cells, controlled by the KR C4 and KR C5 / KR C5 micro controller generations. The robot software stack centers on KUKA System Software (KSS/VSS) for KR C4-class hardware, the newer iiQKA.OS / iiQKA.OS2 operating system for KR C5, and the KUKA Robot Language (KRL) for motion programming, with extension surfaces including KUKA.RobotSensorInterface (RSI), KUKA.EthernetKRL, KUKA.PLC mxAutomation for external PLC control, KUKA.OPC UA, and KUKA.AppTech / iiQKA App Builder for option packages. Engineering and simulation are delivered through iiQWorks (iiQWorks.Sim, iiQWorks.App Builder, iiQWorks.Copilot) and KUKA.Sim, while operational software includes KUKA Xpert (documentation/cloud), KUKA iiQoT (condition monitoring), and KUKA Connect / my.KUKA customer portals. KUKA does not publish a first-party public REST/OpenAPI developer API or an official GitHub organization for its robot control stack; integration is performed through proprietary protocols (RSI, EthernetKRL, mxAutomation, OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) and SDKs distributed via the iiQKA Creator portal and KUKA Xpert. A meaningful body of open-source KUKA integration code lives in the community-maintained kroshu GitHub organization (ROS 2 drivers, external-control SDK, URDF robot descriptions) and the roboticsapi / openkuka projects. KUKA serves automotive, electronics, battery, metal, consumer goods, healthcare, aerospace, and e-commerce logistics customers, and through its Swisslog subsidiary extends into warehouse and intralogistics automation.

providers.name: Segway-Ninebot
providers.description: Segway-Ninebot is a global personal-transportation and robotics company, formed when Ninebot acquired Segway in 2015. It designs and manufactures electric kickscooters (the world's top-selling e-kickscooter brand, 13M+ units sold across 100+ countries), self-balancing personal transporters, e-bikes, and — through its Robotics division — RMP mobile-robot chassis and delivery/service robots (Nova Carter, NVIDIA Isaac-powered developer kits). Backed by HongShan. Its public developer surface is limited to Segway Robotics' open-source ROS / NVIDIA Isaac integration packages on GitHub; no first-party REST or OpenAPI product API is currently published.

providers.name: NinjaBlocks
providers.description: Ninja Blocks Inc was an Australian Internet-of-Things startup (founded 2012, backed by 500 Global / 500 Startups) behind the Ninja Block and Ninja Sphere home-automation hubs. It offered a cloud-connected platform with a RESTful API (base https://api.ninja.is/rest/v0/) for reading sensor data and controlling actuators, plus first-party client libraries for Node.js, PHP, Ruby, Lua and Arduino, a `ninja-toolbelt` CLI, and OAuth-based authentication. The company ceased operation and its web and API hosts are no longer online; this profile preserves the surviving first-party open-source client libraries and API tooling published to npm and GitHub. Added to the API Evangelist network from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from public package registries and the github.com/ninjablocks organization.

providers.name: Phasecraft
providers.description: Phasecraft is a quantum algorithms company building software that combines classical and quantum computing to solve real-world problems in materials discovery, advanced biochemistry, and optimization. Its algorithms are engineered to run efficiently across multiple quantum hardware platforms, and its published results include scalable approaches to the Fermi-Hubbard model and QAOA-based optimization. Founded by Profs. Ashley Montanaro (CEO) and Toby Cubitt (CTO), the company operates from London, Bristol, and Washington DC, and is backed by Playground Global. Phasecraft exposes no public developer API; its programmatic surface is limited to open research code on GitHub and two interactive web tools (a materials database and an optimization graph library).

providers.name: Quantum Machines
providers.description: Quantum Machines is a Tel Aviv, Israel-based quantum control company that builds the Quantum Orchestration Platform (QOP) — a unified hardware and software stack for controlling quantum processors at the pulse level. Its hardware portfolio centers on the OPX+ and OPX1000 controllers, which are built around a custom Pulse Processing Unit (PPU) architecture that executes classical control and real-time feedback alongside arbitrary waveform generation, with sub-microsecond classical-quantum round trips and 160 ns active reset latency. The platform is programmed in QUA, the company's domain-specific pulse-level language, exposed to developers through the qm-qua Python SDK and an extensive open-source ecosystem under the qua-platform GitHub organization (QUAlibrate, QUAM, qua-libs, py-qua-tools, qua-dashboards). Quantum Machines also ships peripheral hardware including the Octave up/down converter (to 18 GHz), QDAC-II ultra-low-noise DACs, QSwitch, QBox, and the QCage/QBoard/QFilter cryogenic line. The platform is qubit-modality agnostic, supporting superconducting, semiconductor spin, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and color-center systems, and is used by university labs (MIT, Caltech, Harvard, Princeton, Weizmann) and quantum startups (Alice & Bob, Diraq, EeroQ). Quantum Machines has partnered with NVIDIA on the DGX Quantum hybrid quantum-classical compute platform and acquired the Delft-based QHarbor Bioscience team as a European R&D hub. Quantum Machines does not currently publish a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or self-service developer signup; the QOP control surface is reached exclusively via the qm-qua Python SDK against an OPX/OPX1000 controller (hardware or qm-saas cloud simulator).

providers.name: MEQ Solutions
providers.description: MEQ Solutions is an Australian agrifood technology company delivering what it calls the world's only end-to-end measurement of red meat quality and yield. Its integrated hardware-and-software suite — MEQ Probe, MEQ Camera, MEQ Live, and MEQ Insights — gives producers, feedlots, processors, brands, retailers, and food-service operators objective, real-time carcass and eating-quality data. Deployed across Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and Brazil, MEQ has completed over 10 million scans across 60+ deployments and reports a demonstrated 10x ROI. The company is backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API surface is currently published; the meqinsights.com portal is a customer login.

providers.name: Teserac
providers.description: Teserac is an AI-native infrastructure intelligence company building Neuron™, a unified platform for data center observability, intelligence, and workflow automation. Neuron ingests telemetry from every system in a facility and correlates it across existing DCIM, BMS, EPMS, and ITSM platforms into a single intelligence layer, surfacing anomalies before they become incidents to protect SLAs and shrink MTTR. Its proprietary Neuron Connect™ technology auto-discovers and configures devices and supports protocols including SNMP, OPC-UA, MQTT, Redfish, REST APIs, and Niagara/Tridium. Teserac is backed by Mayfield. As of this profile the company exposes a marketing site and an authenticated product demo (neuron.demo.teserac.ai) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Tozuda
providers.description: Tozuda is a Philadelphia-based safety technology company that makes mechanical, non-electronic head impact indicators for helmets. The patented indicator changes from clear to red when a helmet sustains force exceeding a set G-force threshold, making hidden helmet damage visible to workers, athletes, and safety inspectors across ANSI, DOT, EN, CSA, CPSC, and SNELL helmet types. Tozuda is a Techstars portfolio company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Ai Fabrik
providers.description: AI Fabrik is an infrastructure company building an edge inference delivery network for high-performance AI tokens. Incubated within Gruve and led by founder Tarun Raisoni alongside Swati Deshpande and Tanuj Mohan, the company has deconstructed the traditional data center model and rebuilt every layer for real-time AI, delivering distributed inference close to users and cloud providers with sub-20ms latency, cost efficiency, and built-in compliance. AI Fabrik is deploying five initial production sites with 6,000+ B300 GPUs launching in 2026, backed by Mayfield, Xora (Temasek), Acclimate Ventures, and Cisco Investments.

providers.name: Aiko Solar
providers.description: Aiko Solar (Zhejiang Aiko Solar Energy Co.) is a solar photovoltaic manufacturer specializing in high-efficiency solar cells and modules, best known for its ABC (All Back Contact) module technology for residential, commercial, industrial, and utility-scale applications. A BloombergNEF Tier 1 manufacturer, the company reports 200 GW+ accumulative cell and module shipments and mass-production cell efficiency around 25%. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer or API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Anthro Energy
providers.description: Anthro Energy is a battery materials company based in Alameda, California, developing next-generation electrolyte technology for lithium-ion and next-gen battery cells. Its flagship Proteus platform is a drop-in electrolyte that increases energy density, improves safety, and adds mechanical integrity without requiring changes to existing gigafactory manufacturing infrastructure, and is compatible with a wide range of anodes, separators, and cathodes. Spun out of research at Stanford, Anthro Energy is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures and Ultratech Capital. It is a physical-materials company with no public API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and market discovery.

providers.name: Ayar Labs
providers.description: Ayar Labs is a silicon-photonics company that develops co-packaged optics (CPO) and optical I/O technology to replace copper interconnects with light. Its products, including the TeraPHY optical engine and SuperNova external light source, connect thousands of GPUs across racks to deliver the bandwidth density and energy efficiency required by hyperscale AI infrastructure. Ayar Labs is backed by Insight Partners and Playground Global. It ships hardware and optical-interconnect technology rather than a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Boldr
providers.description: Boldr is a Techstars-backed consumer hardware company building energy-saving smart home climate control devices. Its two products are Kelvin, a smart infrared heater, and Klima, a smart thermostat controller for mini-split air conditioners that also monitors appliance health so units last longer with fewer issues. Both devices are managed through the Boldr mobile app, which lets homeowners control climate settings remotely and track energy usage to lower utility bills. Boldr also runs Boldr Pro, a program for HVAC contractors. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted online store at shopboldr.com and does not currently publish a first-party developer API; its only public machine-readable surface is the Shopify Customer Account OIDC discovery served at the storefront host.

providers.name: Cashify
providers.description: Cashify is an Indian re-commerce platform for buying, selling, and repairing used and refurbished consumer electronics — smartphones, laptops, tablets, and other gadgets. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Gurugram, the company provides instant online price quotes, free doorstep pickup with on-the-spot payment for devices sold to it, and sells certified refurbished devices backed by warranty. Alongside its consumer website and mobile apps, Cashify operates a network of physical retail stores across India, runs device repair services, and offers a partner program for retailers. It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners among other investors. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead and has been enriched with identity and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: CelLink
providers.description: CelLink (CelLink Technologies / CelLink Corporation) manufactures large-format, high-conductance flexible circuits that consolidate power, data, and sensing into thin, lightweight layers, replacing traditional wire harnesses and busbars. Its product lines are Battery Pack Interconnect, Flex Harness, and Data Center power delivery, serving automotive, aerospace, industrial, data center, and grid-storage electrification markets. Founded by CEO Kevin Coakley and VP Engineering Malcolm Brown, the company is headquartered in San Carlos, California, with sites in Georgetown, Texas; Wixom, Michigan; Hamburg, Germany; and Shanghai, China. CelLink circuits have been in electric-vehicle production since 2020. CelLink is a hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Chemify
providers.description: Chemify is a Glasgow-based programmable-chemistry company, spun out of the University of Glasgow in 2022 by chemist Lee Cronin, that digitizes the creation of molecules through what it calls "Chemputation." The platform fuses AI/ML-driven molecular design, a universal chemical programming language, and robotic synthesis so pharmaceutical, biotech, and industrial partners can move from a novel concept to a makeable compound end to end. In 2025 Chemify opened its first Chemifarm, a fully automated chemistry facility in Glasgow's Maryhill district that pairs its molecular-design engine with industrial-scale robotic synthesis, and closed a $50M Series B co-led by Wing Venture Capital and Insight Partners, with backing from DCVC. Chemify does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; engagement runs through its partner program.

providers.name: Chipstack
providers.description: Chipstack is an AI-driven semiconductor verification company that uses agentic AI to automate chip design verification, one of the most time-consuming stages of building a complex chip (often 60% or more of total development effort). Its product suite is a set of specialized AI agents — a Mental Model AI Agent, a Formal AI Agent, a Unit Simulation AI Agent, and a UVM AI Agent — that read design intent and generate, run, and reason about verification tasks to shift that work earlier in the design cycle and cut the time and resources it takes to tape out. Founded and based across Seattle, WA and San Jose, CA, and backed by Khosla Ventures, Chipstack is an enterprise, demo-request product rather than a public developer platform: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or developer portal. In 2026 the company announced it is joining Cadence. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: E-Peas
providers.description: e-peas is a Belgian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2014 in Louvain-la-Neuve that designs power management integrated circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting, enabling battery-free and battery-assisted IoT devices to power themselves from ambient energy. Its flagship Ambient Energy Manager (AEM) family harvests from photovoltaic (light), thermal, vibration/piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid multi-source inputs, and the company also develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers for autonomous data acquisition. e-peas positions itself as a pioneer of the "Ambient IoT" concept serving smart buildings, industrial IoT, consumer electronics, and wearables, with an ecosystem of 30+ partners including Panasonic, TDK, Vishay, and Silicon Labs. This is a hardware/silicon company that does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: ECOVACS Robotics
providers.description: ECOVACS Robotics is a global home service robotics company founded in 1998 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, that designs, manufactures, and sells AI-powered autonomous cleaning devices for consumer and commercial use. Its product families include DEEBOT robotic vacuum and mopping robots, WINBOT window-cleaning robots, GOAT robotic lawn mowers, ULTRAMARINE pool-cleaning robots, and the DEEBOT PRO commercial line, all managed through the ECOVACS HOME mobile app. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; as of this enrichment pass ECOVACS publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface — this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Ergatta
providers.description: Ergatta is a connected-fitness company that makes game-based home rowing machines, pairing WaterRower-derived water-resistance hardware handcrafted in Rhode Island with a gamified software platform of interactive challenges (Endeavor, Meteor, Wavelength), live and on-demand races, scenic rows, coached classes, and custom workouts. Ergatta sells the Luxe and Lite rowers plus upgrade kits for existing WaterRower and Concept2 machines, delivered through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront with a membership subscription. Ergatta does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web surface and identity for network discovery.

providers.name: Fractile
providers.description: Fractile is a UK-based semiconductor startup, founded in 2022 and headquartered in London with an engineering base in Bristol, designing a new class of AI inference processors. Its architecture physically interleaves memory and compute to overcome the memory-bandwidth bottleneck that limits large language model inference, targeting frontier model serving up to 25x faster and at roughly 1/10th the cost of existing hardware. The company takes a full-stack approach spanning transistor-level circuit design through cloud inference server logic, and in May 2026 raised $220M to build the next generation of inference hardware. Backers include Accel and Felicis. Led by founder and CEO Walter Goodwin, Fractile is a hardware/compute company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Fuchsia
providers.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Iconbuild
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. (iconbuild.com) is an Austin, Texas construction technologies company using large-scale robotics, advanced materials, and software to build homes and structures. ICON develops the Vulcan and Phoenix 3D-printing robots, proprietary Lavacrete and CarbonX building materials, and design/build tooling (including its CODEX architectural catalog and ICON Prime), and has printed communities across the US as well as researched off-world construction with NASA (Project Olympus). Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a physical construction / building-technology company; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no API artifacts were harvested.

providers.name: In Focus Systems
providers.description: In Focus Systems, Inc. (later InFocus Corporation, and today marketed as InFocus) is an audiovisual technology company founded in 1986 in Oregon by Steve Hix and Paul Gulick, both formerly of Tektronix. The company pioneered LCD projection panels and is credited with inventing the digital projector, going public on NASDAQ (ticker INFS) in December 1990. It grew into a leading maker of DLP and LCD projectors, interactive flat-panel displays, DVLED video walls, and collaboration hardware for business, education, installation, and home markets. In Focus Systems was an early Battery Ventures investment (since exited). The InFocus business was acquired by Image Holdings Corp. in 2009 and operates today as a privately held subsidiary headquartered in the Portland, Oregon area. It is a hardware and audiovisual solutions company and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Jiobit
providers.description: Jiobit is a real-time GPS tracking device company owned by Life360, based in San Mateo, California. Its lightweight (18g) wearable tracker is designed for kids, pets, seniors, and adults, combining LPWA CatM1 cellular, GPS, WiFi, and BLE for location accuracy of 1-50 feet, up to 30 days of battery life, geofence and SOS/911 emergency alerts, and tamper-proof, government-level encryption. Jiobit is a consumer hardware and mobile-app product sold direct-to-consumer with a monthly connectivity subscription; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Kandou
providers.description: Kandou (Kandou AI) is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2011 by Amin Shokrollahi and headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland. It designs high-speed, energy-efficient chip-to-chip interconnect technology built on its proprietary Copper MIMO / Chord Signaling architecture, which turns noise in copper channels into usable bandwidth for massively scalable AI systems. Products include the Glasswing chiplet interconnect IP, the Regli PCIe retimer, the Matterhorn USB4 retimer, the Zetti PCIe switch, and AI Fabric memory/networking platforms. Chord signaling has been adopted into JEDEC and OIF industry specifications. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners across multiple rounds, Kandou raised a $225M round in March 2026 led by Maverick Silicon with strategic participation from SoftBank, Synopsys, Cadence, and Alchip. This is a hardware/semiconductor IP company with no public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Marshall
providers.description: Marshall is a Swedish-British consumer audio brand, part of Marshall Group AB, known for its iconic guitar amplifiers and a modern line of Bluetooth speakers, wireless headphones, and earbuds. Built on more than 60 years of live-music heritage, Marshall sells direct-to-consumer through marshall.com across amps, home and portable speakers, and personal audio. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer portfolio company of HongShan. Marshall publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Mesodyne
providers.description: Mesodyne is an MIT-founded engineering and manufacturing company (established 2018) that builds the LightCell, a patented thermophotovoltaic power generator which converts liquid and gaseous fuels — gasoline, diesel, propane, jet fuel, and hydrogen — directly into silent electricity with more than ten times the energy density of batteries. Designed for military, tactical, drone, and off-grid use, it operates day or night across extreme environments with low heat and emissions signatures and no routine maintenance. Mesodyne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures the company identity and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Movandi
providers.description: Movandi is an RF semiconductor company founded by former Broadcom executives (CEO Maryam Rofougaran and CTO Reza Rofougaran) that designs 5G mmWave chipsets, RF front ends, phased-array antenna modules, 5G smart repeaters, and beamforming software for terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. Based in Irvine, California and backed by Sierra Ventures, the company holds 130+ patents covering millimeter wave semiconductor, system, and software technologies spanning 5G, fixed wireless, and satellite connectivity. Movandi is a hardware/semiconductor vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Nanotronics
providers.description: Nanotronics (rebranded to CubeFabs in 2025) builds AI-driven inspection, process-control, and automation systems for advanced industrial manufacturing, with a focus on semiconductors, data centers, EV/automotive, and aerospace/defense. Its "AI factory" platform combines optical imaging, machine learning, and robotics to improve manufacturing precision, yields, and cost efficiency for customers including Hologic, Broadcom, Coherent, and Standard BioTools. Surfaced as a founders-fund portfolio company; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: nlyte
providers.description: nlyte is an enterprise Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) software provider, now part of Carrier, that helps organizations discover, model, and manage physical and virtual data-center assets, capacity, power, cooling, connectivity, and operational workflows across facilities. Nlyte products expose REST APIs (including the NgageAPI / Ngauge web service) plus a portfolio of pre-built bi-directional connectors for CMDB, ITSM, service desk, virtualization, and building-management systems. The API is delivered to customers through the Nlyte customer portal rather than a public developer program, so there is no open developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or self-serve sign-up.

providers.name: NovaSparks
providers.description: NovaSparks builds ultra-low-latency FPGA market data solutions for banks, trading firms, and electronic markets. Its NovaTick ticker plant, delivered as a hardware appliance or PCIe card, normalizes and distributes real-time feeds across global equities, options (OPRA), and other asset classes with deterministic nanosecond latency. Integration is via a proprietary ultra-low-latency C++ Software API and the NovaSparks Wire Format (NSWF), a normalized message protocol whose full specification is provided to banks and trading firms under NDA rather than published publicly. NovaSparks is now part of Exegy. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech.

providers.name: Omnitron Sensors
providers.description: Omnitron Sensors designs advanced MEMS (micro electro mechanical systems) sensors using innovative 3D manufacturing techniques, aiming to deliver high-performance, low-cost sensing with major gains in precision and reliability. Its technology targets AI data centers, autonomous systems and vehicles, environmental and climate monitoring, and extended reality (XR) devices. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, the company is a hardware/semiconductor business with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: One Five
providers.description: One Five (styled one.five) is a sustainable packaging technology company based in Holm, Germany that pairs an AI-driven decision platform, Quartermaster, with ready-to-use recyclable and compostable packaging products. The Quartermaster platform embeds product-market-fit and material analysis into packaging development to accelerate material scouting and packing trials, helping consumer brands cut R&D spend, improve customer acquisition efficiency, and meet emerging packaging regulations while reducing environmental impact. One Five ships flexible sustainable packaging for categories such as dishwasher tablets and gummies through partners including Bluemorph and Glassleaf, and is backed by Speedinvest. The company offers no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: oneNav
providers.description: oneNav is a fabless GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) semiconductor company building the next generation of mobile positioning. Its L5-direct receiver acquires and tracks on the modern L5 satellite band without legacy L1 aiding, delivering higher location accuracy in urban canyons and far greater resilience to GPS jamming and spoofing, in half the RF size, power and cost of hybrid L1+L5 solutions. Founded in 2019 (Steve Poizner, Paul McBurney) with offices in Sunnyvale, CA and Tampere, Finland, oneNav targets smartphones, wearables, IoT trackers, defense and emergency services. It is backed by GV, Norwest Venture Partners and GSR Ventures. oneNav is a hardware/silicon company and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Polycom
providers.description: Polycom, Inc. was a pioneer of unified communications and video conferencing, known for its RealPresence video collaboration platform, SoundStation conference phones, and Group Series and HDX room video endpoints. Polycom merged with Plantronics in 2018 to form Poly, which HP acquired in 2022; the polycom.com domain now redirects to HP's Poly product line. For developers, Polycom exposed the RealPresence Platform REST API (via the RealPresence Resource Manager and Distributed Media Application, later branded Clariti) along with device REST APIs on its VideoOS endpoints, enabling programmatic conference control, scheduling, provisioning, resource monitoring, and billing integration. Developer resources are now consolidated under HP's Poly developer portal.

providers.name: Quantum Circuits
providers.description: Quantum Circuits, Inc. is a quantum computing hardware company (a Yale University spinout) building superconducting quantum systems with built-in error detection. Its dual-rail cavity qubits pair Quantum Error Detection (QED), Real-Time Control Flow (RTCF), and Error Detection Handling (EDH), and its Aqumen Seeker QPU (introduced November 2024) targets stable, repeatable, fault-tolerant quantum computation. The company engages early users through a Strategic Quantum Release (SQR) program that includes a simulator and access to Aqumen Seeker systems, rather than a public self-serve API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Schrödinger
providers.description: Schrödinger is a New York-headquartered (NASDAQ: SDGR) computational science company that develops a physics-based and AI-driven molecular simulation platform used across drug discovery and materials science.
