Its flagship desktop modeling environment is Maestro (MS Maestro for materials science), which integrates a deep stack of computational tools — Glide (docking), FEP+ (free energy perturbation), Desmond (molecular dynamics), Jaguar (quantum chemistry), Prime (protein structure prediction), BioLuminate (biologics), LigPrep, QikProp, SiteMap, and WaterMap — together with the Schrödinger-maintained PyMOL visualization system. LiveDesign is the cloud-native enterprise design lab where chemists, biologists, and program teams collaborate on molecules, run computational workflows, and integrate experimental data; it exposes a snap-in API framework for connecting in-house and third-party tooling. The Schrödinger Python API (current release 2026-1) is the primary developer surface, providing programmatic access to molecular structures, Maestro automation, jobcontrol, Glide, FEP+, Desmond, Jaguar, MacroModel, Prime, BioLuminate, and LiveDesign integration (login, export, dataset and column management). Schrödinger also ships KNIME extensions, command-line drivers for every computational product, and maintains a meaningful open-source footprint on GitHub — including PyMOL, maeparser, coordgenlibs, sketcher, gpusimilarity, csmiles, and the fixed-data-table-2 React component. The business has two segments — software licensing to global pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and a co-developed and proprietary drug discovery pipeline. There is no public developer signup or self-serve REST API; access to the platform, Python API, and LiveDesign is gated through commercial licensing and the my.schrodinger.com customer portal.

providers.name: Tensordyne
providers.description: Tensordyne (formerly Recogni) builds next-generation AI inference systems from the foundation up — a proprietary logarithmic-math architecture cast into custom 3nm silicon, compute hardware, scale-up interconnect, and system software. Its flagship Napier platform targets the fastest, lowest-cost, most energy-efficient generative AI inference for hyperscaler and neocloud data centers, delivering 608 PFLOPS dense compute per rack in an air-cooled 30 kW pod and supporting MoE models, agentic workloads, and 4K video generation. The stack integrates with PyTorch, Triton, vLLM, and Kubernetes; a developer SDK is announced as coming soon. Backed by Mayfield, Bosch Ventures, Toyota Ventures, GreatPoint Ventures, and Plug and Play, the company has raised more than $211M and operates from Sunnyvale, California and Munich, Germany.

providers.name: TRIDITIVE
providers.description: TRIDITIVE is an automated additive manufacturing company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Meres, Asturias, Spain, with offices in Hartford, Connecticut and London. It builds the AMCELL family of automated industrial 3D printing machines (Amcell 1300, 4300, 8300, Bulkam), the Traced traceability system, and the EVAM Software platform for additive manufacturing workflow management, digital warehousing, and on-demand production of polymer and metal parts. A Techstars portfolio company, TRIDITIVE publishes no public API, developer portal, or client SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: versatile.ai
providers.description: Versatile is a construction-technology company building AI-powered crane intelligence for jobsites, primarily serving steel erectors and general contractors. Its CraneView hardware device attaches to a crane's hook block and passively captures operational data, which the Control Center software turns into real-time insight on pace, progress, productivity, and delays without asking crews to change how they work. The company is backed by Insight Partners. As of this profile Versatile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Vita Inclinata
providers.description: Vita Inclinata Technologies is a Colorado-based hardware company that builds physics-based load stabilization systems for helicopter hoists and construction cranes, eliminating the dangerous spin and sway of suspended loads. Its ecosystem spans Vita Aerospace (helicopter and rescue hoist stabilization), Vita Industrial (crane and construction load control), Air Rescue Systems (hoist training and products), and the Vita Rescue System used in military MEDEVAC operations. The company is Techstars-backed. It was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network; as a physical-hardware manufacturer it currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: CubeSmart
providers.description: CubeSmart (NYSE CUBE) is a self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust (REIT) and the third-largest owner and operator of self-storage properties in the United States. As of December 31, 2024 the company owns 631 self-storage properties across 25 states and Washington DC, containing approximately 45.8 million rentable square feet, and operates a third-party management platform that pushes the total managed network well past 1,300 properties. Headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, CubeSmart originated as U-Store-It Trust (founded July 2004, IPO October 2004) and rebranded to CubeSmart on September 14, 2011. The company is a component of the S&P 400. CubeSmart does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal — its public technology footprint is limited to the consumer cubesmart.com booking/account site and the CubeSmart mobile apps for iOS and Android.

providers.name: Photoneo
providers.description: Photoneo is a Slovak (Bratislava, founded 2013) machine-vision company and a global pioneer of high-resolution structured-light 3D measurement. Its flagship products are the PhoXi 3D Scanner family and the MotionCam-3D, a parallel structured-light camera that captures moving scenes in real-time 3D, together with AI-enabled software such as Bin Picking Studio, Locator, and Palletizing for robotic automation. Rather than a hosted web/REST API, Photoneo exposes a developer surface through the PhoXi Control software and its official C++, C#, and Python device APIs, GenICam/GigE Vision standard connectivity, TCP/IP robot interfaces (UR, ABB, FANUC, Staubli, Mitsubishi, Kawasaki, Yaskawa), and a set of BSD-licensed example repositories on GitHub. Documentation lives in the Photoneo Knowledge Base (docs.photoneo.com) and the 3D scanning wiki. Photoneo (now part of the Brightpick Group) was acquired by Zebra Technologies.

providers.name: MKS Instruments
providers.description: MKS Instruments is a global provider of foundational technology solutions for semiconductor manufacturing, electronics and packaging, and specialty industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans vacuum and gas delivery systems, photonics, lasers, optics, motion control, and process control. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified at the corporate level; technical integration is typically handled through product-level documentation, sales engineering, and partner channels.

providers.name: NextSilicon
providers.description: NextSilicon is a deep-tech compute company building intelligent, software-defined acceleration hardware for high-performance computing, AI, and vector-database workloads. Its flagship Maverick-2 is a dataflow accelerator built on the Intelligent Compute Architecture (ICA) that reconfigures itself at runtime, and its Arbel product is a server-class RISC-V CPU core on TSMC process. A developer toolchain supports C/C++, FORTRAN, OpenMP, and Kokkos, with planned CUDA and HIP/ROCm paths, letting teams run existing code faster without rewrites or vendor lock-in. NextSilicon publishes no public web API, SDK registry package, or open developer portal; its documentation site is gated, so this profile captures company identity, its GitHub organization (largely upstream compiler/Kokkos forks), and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Xperi
providers.description: Xperi Inc. (NYSE: XPER) is an entertainment technology company whose licensed technologies power audio, video, and media discovery experiences across connected cars, consumer electronics, pay-TV, and streaming media platforms. Its brands include DTS immersive audio, HD Radio digital broadcast radio, IMAX Enhanced certification, and the TiVo video platform. Xperi ships its technologies to automakers, device makers, and video providers through commercial licensing and integration programs rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal or API documentation was found, though its TiVo engineering organization maintains an open-source presence on GitHub.

providers.name: Celus
providers.description: CELUS GmbH is a Munich-based electronics design automation company building an AI-driven, cloud design platform that automates the early stages of printed circuit board (PCB) engineering. The CELUS Design Platform turns high-level product requirements into schematics, part selections and layout-ready outputs in minutes rather than days by combining AI-powered component search with its proprietary CUBO component knowledge base, then handing off EDA-compatible files to tools like Altium and KiCad. Founded by Alexander and Tobias Pohl and backed by Earlybird and Speedinvest, CELUS targets hardware engineers and manufacturers pursuing digital transformation of the electronics design workflow. The platform is a closed SaaS product accessed through app.celus.io; as of this enrichment pass CELUS publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: DeepSight Technology
providers.description: DeepSight Technology is a medical-imaging company reinventing diagnostic ultrasound. It is building a semiconductor-based ultrasound sensor and imaging platform (including its NeedleVue technology) to deliver a step-change in ultrasound performance, making this safe, non-invasive, radiation-free, low-cost imaging modality far more usable across clinical applications. The company is a hardware and medical-device business backed by Wing Venture Capital and Deerfield; it is added to the API Evangelist network as a Wing portfolio lead. It does not currently publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Instabeat
providers.description: Instabeat is a San Francisco based swimming technology company that builds a heart-rate monitoring device integrated directly into swim goggles, giving swimmers real-time, color-coded effort feedback (heart-rate zones), automatic stroke detection, lap counting, pace, distance and rest-interval tracking without a chest strap or wrist watch. Paired with the Instabeat mobile app and myinstabeat.com, it delivers data-driven training insights so swimmers can adjust workouts in the water rather than after the session. The company sells the device through a Shopify storefront and has tested the product with 250+ swimmers across 56 countries. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer or API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Intellitech
providers.description: Intellitech Corporation is a semiconductor test and design-for-test company based in Rochester, New Hampshire, specializing in IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG) boundary-scan technology. Its products include the Eclipse boundary-scan test development environment, the Scan Executive production test platform, and concurrent JTAG hardware testers such as the PT100 and JAF Pro, used for printed circuit board (PCB) testing, in-system FLASH programming, and FPGA configuration. Intellitech is an early Battery Ventures ("Battery Ventures I") portfolio company in the semiconductor sector. The company publishes product, legal, and customer-account pages on its website but does not expose a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or MCP surface.

providers.name: INURU
providers.description: INURU (Inuru GmbH) is a Berlin-based printed-electronics company that manufactures ultra-thin, flexible printed OLED lighting for smart packaging, labels, apparel, and medical products. Its core product, the Elf (Embeddable Luminous Film), combines an inkjet-printed OLED, a power source, and a microchip into a paper-thin, waterproof film that can glow in any shape and respond to touch, motion, or sound. Founded in 2016, Inuru operates the automated "Dragon Factory" OLED production line in Wildau and works with brands such as Coca-Cola and Marvel on interactive, sustainable smart-packaging and medication-adherence labels. This is a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network; Inuru is a hardware and smart-packaging manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: zincfive
providers.description: ZincFive is a power solutions company that manufactures nickel-zinc (NiZn) battery technology for mission-critical and backup power applications, including data center UPS systems, AI dynamic power, and grid storage. Its product line covers BC Series UPS battery cabinets, NiZn retrofit kits, monobloc batteries, and cylindrical cells, positioned as non-flammable, high-power-density, and highly recyclable alternatives to lead-acid batteries. ZincFive publishes technical documents, papers, and industry insights reports, but does not expose a public developer API or SDK surface.

providers.name: Alta Resource Technologies
providers.description: Alta Resource Technologies is a Colorado-based deep-tech company reinventing how critical minerals are sourced. It uses advanced biochemistry — customizable, engineered proteins licensed from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and co-developed with researchers at Pennsylvania State University — to selectively separate high-purity rare earth elements and other strategic metals from low-grade ores, mining tailings, and electronic-waste streams such as end-of-life hard disk drives. The protein-based platform binds target elements out of complex, low-concentration solutions with high selectivity while dramatically reducing the environmental footprint of conventional mining and refining, strengthening U.S. and allied critical-mineral supply chains. Alta emerged from stealth in January 2025 and expanded its Series Seed to $10M, backed by DCVC, Voyager Ventures, In-Q-Tel, and Orion Industrial Ventures. As a materials-science and biochemistry company, Alta does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this API Evangelist profile carries its identity and website properties only.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ara
providers.description: Ara is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising network that finances, installs, and operates rich-media displays across mobility, municipal, parking, and retail settings. It describes itself as the largest U.S. owner-operator of rideshare and taxi car-top digital billboards, running a long-term partnership with Uber alongside in-car, storefront, and parking/municipal kiosk screens. Ara owns the hardware and content-management operations under a subscription model so partners avoid cap-ex and operational overhead. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/enrichment lead.

providers.name: August Home
providers.description: August Home is a consumer smart-home and access-control brand best known for its retrofit August Smart Lock, Smart Lock Pro, Wi-Fi Smart Lock, Smart Keypad, Doorbell Cam, and the August Connect Wi-Fi Bridge. Founded in San Francisco and acquired by ASSA ABLOY, August products are now sold and supported alongside the Yale Home brand and operated through the shared Yale Access mobile app. August does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; programmatic access to August locks is reached through the private mobile/app API or via third-party universal-access platforms such as Seam, and integrations exist with Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Airbnb, and Yale. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Blixt
providers.description: BL!XT (Blixt) is a Swedish deep-tech company building intelligent, programmable power infrastructure that turns electrical distribution from analog systems into digitally controlled, software-defined platforms. Its products include ZERO, a solid-state current-control switchgear for circuit-level protection, monitoring, and automation; X-VERTER, a software-defined voltage conversion system with integrated energy storage; and THE ZONE, an AI-driven software intelligence layer that coordinates connected distribution devices for real-time analysis, failure prediction, and load balancing. BL!XT serves data centers, industrial manufacturing, maritime vessels, grid providers, and defense. Headquartered in Kista, Sweden and backed by Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Bright View Technologies
providers.description: BrightView Technologies, Inc. is a Durham, North Carolina optical film company specializing in computational optics and the design and manufacture of Micro Lens Array (MLA) solutions that shape, diffuse, and manage light. Founded in 2002 on intellectual property licensed from Duke University, the company engineers precision optical films and micro-optical structures used in automotive displays, head-up displays, and LiDAR; consumer and mini/micro-LED displays (gain enhancement and LED-hiding films); LED and architectural lighting (beam shaping and diffusion); and augmented- and virtual-reality beam-shaping optics. BrightView is a hardware and materials manufacturer serving OEMs and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead of Battery Ventures and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Greentoe
providers.description: Greentoe is a name-your-price e-commerce marketplace where shoppers make an offer on brand-new electronics, cameras, TVs and home theater, appliances, baby gear, watches, and optics, and manufacturer-authorized retailers compete to fulfill the order at the buyer's price. Built to bring the negotiation model of big-ticket purchases online, Greentoe reports more than $100M saved by its customers, backs every order with manufacturer warranties and a 30-day return policy, and is backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator. Greentoe operates as a consumer-facing web application and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ICON
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. is an Austin, Texas construction-technology company building large-scale robotic 3D printing systems, materials, and software to make home building faster, more affordable, and more resilient. Its flagship Titan 3D construction printer, orchestrated by the proprietary BuildOS software that translates architectural designs into robotic tool paths and manages material flow, can print the wall system of a 2,500 sq. ft. home in under seven days. ICON operates a Design + Build division delivering 3D-printed homes and communities, a Technology division selling its printers and building systems to other builders, the CODEX digital home design catalog, and ICON Prime. The company is privately held and backed by investors including Bond Capital and Pantera Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a venture-portfolio lead; ICON publishes a marketing and product presence but no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Koobz
providers.description: Koobz is a Ventura, California additive-manufacturing company rebuilding the footwear supply chain around on-demand 3D printing. Its "gigafactory" prints circular-ready, mono-material foamed-TPU shoes to order, so brands carry zero inventory and face no minimum order quantities: a consumer buys on the brand's own storefront, the order and personalization specs sync to the Koobz factory, the shoe is printed in Ventura and dropshipped direct to the customer in days. The company markets 10x faster concept-to-market cycles (4-6 weeks, no tooling), custom cushioning and foot-scanning personalization, and a KoobzWeave toolpath-as-textile upper pattern engine. Its mono-material architecture is positioned for Extended Producer Responsibility regimes such as California SB 707, since a single-polymer shoe yields premium TPU on take-back rather than mixed waste. Koobz has raised $7.2M and is backed by Uncork Capital. It describes its factory as API-driven and its order intake as an API sync from brand storefronts, but as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definition; integration appears to run through its partner ("Partner With Us") channel.

providers.name: Lumos Helmet
providers.description: Lumos (Lumos Helmet) is a consumer hardware company that designs and manufactures smart bike helmets and connected bike lights with integrated safety features such as turn signals, brake lights, and high-visibility LED lighting. Its product line spans commuter, e-bike, and kids' helmets plus standalone smart bike lights, controlled through companion iOS and Android mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Lumos sells direct-to-consumer through an online store; it does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed no programmatic API surface and captured the company's identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Motorola
providers.description: Motorola (motorola.com) is the consumer mobile-device brand operated by Motorola Mobility, a Lenovo company, producing Android smartphones (moto g, moto edge, and razr foldable lines), tablets, and accessories sold worldwide. It was originally added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio stub. On review, the consumer brand publishes no open public REST/HTTP API developer portal: the historical developer.motorola.com Moto Mods hardware SDK (for the modular Moto Z) is no longer reachable, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or well-known discovery surface was found. Enterprise and public-safety APIs are offered separately by Motorola Solutions, Inc. (docs.motorolasolutions.com), a distinct company, under a gated partner Application Developer Program.

providers.name: Nodal Industries
providers.description: Nodal Industries, operating as Nodal Security, is a network security company and 500 Global portfolio startup that makes Numa, a plug-and-play network security appliance providing protective oversight of every connected device on a home or small-office network. Rather than per-device antivirus software, Numa works at the network layer, intercepting malicious traffic before it reaches devices using real-time threat intelligence powered by Suricata, with automatic updates and minimal setup. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or event surface.

providers.name: Osmo
providers.description: Osmo (Tangible Play) makes hands-on, screen-interactive learning games for iPad and Fire tablet that pair a physical reflector base placed over the device camera with digital games spanning math, coding, spelling, drawing, and problem-solving for children. Backed by Accel and GV, Osmo is a consumer educational-technology brand that sells hardware kits and companion apps direct to families and schools. As of this enrichment pass it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Preemadonna
providers.description: Preemadonna is a consumer hardware and software company best known for the Nailbot, a compact inkjet nail-art printer that prints custom designs onto fingernails, press-ons, gel, or bare nails in about five seconds. Backed by Version One Ventures, the company is building a creative-expression platform that pairs smart hardware with AI-powered design tools, consumables, and a creator marketplace, delivered through companion iOS and Android apps. The company holds 10+ utility patents. Preemadonna currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public web, support, and policy footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prophetic
providers.description: Prophetic is a San Francisco-based neurotechnology startup, incorporated in January 2023, building the world's first wearable device for stabilizing lucid dreams. Its "Halo" headband pairs EEG sensing with targeted transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) to noninvasively stimulate the prefrontal cortex, driven by an in-house AI model, Morpheus-1, that takes brain activity as its prompt and generates shaped ultrasonic waveforms as output. Backed by BoxGroup and a16z's Scout Fund, Prophetic sells its neuromodulation headbands direct-to-consumer. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Prophetic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic integration surface — it is a consumer hardware and wellness company.

providers.name: Quandela
providers.description: Quandela is a Paris-region (Massy, France) photonic quantum computing company building modular, scalable, and energy-efficient quantum systems driven by deterministic single-photon sources. Its hardware lineup includes Ascella (its first deployed cloud-accessible system), Belenos (a 12-qubit second-generation machine), Canopus (its latest state-of-the-art system), and Mosaiq (its flagship prototyping platform), alongside Prometheus single-photon sources and the Entropy quantum random number generator. Quandela develops Perceval, an open-source Python framework for programming photonic quantum computers, distributed via PyPI as perceval-quandela, and operates a cloud platform at cloud.quandela.com where users authenticate with a token and submit jobs to simulators and QPUs (e.g. "sim:altair", "qpu:altair") through Perceval's RemoteProcessor. The company also runs a Quantum Acceleration Program for enterprise pilots in cybersecurity, pharma, chemistry, logistics, finance, energy, and aerospace. There is no public REST/HTTP OpenAPI specification — the cloud surface is abstracted entirely behind the Perceval Python SDK and its companion perceval-interop bridges to Qiskit, QuTiP, cQASM, and myQLM.

providers.name: Senra Systems
providers.description: Senra Systems is an aerospace wire harness manufacturer based in Redondo Beach, California, that unites design, data, and production under one roof. The company builds complex electrical wire harnesses for aerospace and defense programs, spanning wire harness design and engineering support, prototype through full-rate production, component selection and supply chain optimization, and precision automation in a 15,000 square foot smart-manufacturing facility. Senra positions itself as delivering harnesses at roughly four times the speed of traditional vendors while maintaining aerospace-grade quality and certifications. Senra Systems is backed by Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 8VC, and General Catalyst. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Simplifyber
providers.description: Simplifyber is a sustainable footwear and materials technology company that manufactures shoe uppers and other components using a proprietary fiber-molding process. By casting products directly from a liquid, cellulose-based material it eliminates the spinning, weaving, and knitting steps and much of the cutting and sewing of traditional shoemaking, which it says lowers the CO2 emissions of a shoe upper by roughly 33x versus conventional methods. Its flagship Moon Shoe was developed with the fashion brand Ganni. Simplifyber is a Techstars-backed startup. It operates as a consumer and industrial manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Tennibot
providers.description: Tennibot builds AI-powered ball machines and autonomous ball collectors for tennis, pickleball, and padel. Its flagship Partner ball machine and Rover ball collector use computer vision and robotics to deliver realistic drills and eliminate manual ball pickup, controlled through the Tennibot mobile app for iOS and Android. The company, based in Auburn, Alabama and backed by Techstars, sells direct-to-consumer hardware; it ships a companion mobile app but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; no external API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Axalta Coating Systems
providers.description: Axalta Coating Systems is a global supplier of liquid and powder coatings for transportation and industrial end-markets, operating through Performance Coatings (refinish and industrial) and Mobility Coatings (light vehicle and commercial vehicle) segments. Brands include Cromax, Spies Hecker, Standox, Imron, and Voltatex. In July 2024 Axalta acquired The CoverFlexx Group from Transtar Holding for $285 million to expand its economy-tier aftermarket coverage in North America. In November 2025 Axalta announced a $17 billion all-stock merger of equals with AkzoNobel that is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027, forming a coatings company with dual headquarters in Amsterdam and Philadelphia.

providers.name: Carnot Fleet
providers.description: Carnot Fleet (Carnotfleet) is a Seoul-based cold-chain technology company that converts non-refrigerated vehicles into temperature-controlled units in under 30 minutes using modular insulation panels and proprietary solid-state thermoelectric heat pumps, spanning frozen, chilled, and ambient ranges with humidity control. Its Adaptive Thermal Control System (ATCS) is an AI-based autonomous control platform delivering cloud-connected temperature monitoring at 10-second intervals. Carnot Fleet surfaces its capabilities through the CF Mobile Application, the CF Portal, and CF APIs that let customers integrate the ATCS into existing logistics solutions to detect, analyze, prevent, and discover cold-chain data points and reduce post-harvest to pre-retail loss across the supply chain.

providers.name: Apoha
providers.description: Apoha is a deep-tech molecular-science company teaching machines to understand matter at the molecular level. Its Liquid State sensory-intelligence platform captures dynamic molecular fingerprints, measuring the biophysical behavior of molecules under stress from minimal sample amounts, to unlock a new fundamental data class for AI. Its first commercial product, VIBE (Variations in Inter-facial Behaviour Under Excitation), predicts how drugs, foods, and materials will behave in the real world, serving pharmaceutical, biotech, food-and-beverage, and materials-science R&D. Based in San Francisco and London, Apoha emerged from stealth in 2026 with $36M in funding led by Singular, alongside Draper Associates, Redalpine, Seedcamp, Wilbe, and Nucleus.

providers.name: Arago
providers.description: Arago (Arago Computing SAS) is a Paris-based deeptech semiconductor startup, founded in 2024 by Nicolas Muller, Ambroise Muller, and Eliott Sarrey, building energy-efficient AI accelerators powered by light rather than electricity. Its photonic processor, codenamed JEF, uses a proprietary multi-physics computing core that encodes values with lasers instead of thousands of transistor switches, targeting 10x to 30x reductions in energy and cost overhead for AI workloads at equivalent performance to leading GPUs. Arago pairs the hardware with a full software stack called CARLOTA, which abstracts the complexities of photonic computing and exposes a programmable interface compatible with mainstream AI frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, while remaining fabbable using standard semiconductor processes. The company operates across France, North America, and Israel, and in July 2025 raised an oversubscribed $26 million seed round co-led by Earlybird, Protagonist, and Visionaries Tomorrow, with backing from executives and investors tied to Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, Uber, PayPal, and Hugging Face. Arago was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Earlybird; as an early-stage hardware company it does not yet publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Dynamics
providers.description: Dynamics Inc designs and manufactures battery-powered interactive payment cards that work with existing point-of-sale and card infrastructure. Its "Computer-in-a-Card" technology embeds a microprocessor, buttons, and a rewritable magnetic stripe into a standard-size card, enabling programmable multi-account cards, hidden card numbers, and on-card loyalty for banks, merchants, and consumers. The company is a fintech hardware manufacturer backed by Bain Capital Ventures. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this repository tracks its identity and public security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lightberry
providers.description: Lightberry is a San Francisco robotics software company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) that builds conversational AI "personality" software for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its platform lets a robot listen, speak, see its surroundings, and act on natural-language instruction without the owner writing any code, emphasizing emotional intelligence, contextual awareness, and autonomy rather than a simple speech-to-text voice pipeline. Lightberry ships pre-installed on robots sold through its partnership with Unitree, and the company runs a manufacturer-compatibility program with robot makers including Fourier, Booster Robotics, and High Torque. Its published documentation today covers device setup (power-on, WiFi provisioning, starting a conversation) plus an MCP architecture note describing a Model Context Protocol server that routes tool calls to individual Lightberry devices, which each expose a REST endpoint. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: Novo Space
providers.description: Novo Space develops high-performance, radiation-tolerant, modular electronics for the most ambitious space missions. Founded by Rodrigo Diez (CEO) and Facundo Jorge (CTO), the company builds SpaceVPX single-board computers, mass memory and GPU boards, tailored subsystems, and radiation-tolerant FPGA IP cores (SpaceWire, SpaceFibre, Ethernet/TCP-IP, CCSDS, NAND controllers, floating-point units) that let satellite and spacecraft builders reuse qualified hardware instead of re-engineering every mission. Customers and partners include Maxar, MIT, Thales Alenia Space, BAE Systems, Leonardo DRS, Mitsubishi, the US Air Force, Nvidia, Ansys, and Microchip. Novo Space is a space-computing hardware provider and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Omate
providers.description: Omate designs and manufactures Wearable-as-a-Service (WaaS) safety solutions built around cellular-connected smartwatches for people who need protection — seniors, children, and lone workers. Its devices (such as the O6L Pro line, marketed under the Omahome brand) combine GPS location tracking, SOS calling, fall detection, and two-way voice into a managed hardware-plus-service offering sold direct to consumers and through partners. Omate is a hardware and connected-device company; as of this profile it exposes no public developer program, API, or SDK. This entry was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with an identity and domain-security pass.

providers.name: Arena AI
providers.description: Arena AI (now operating as Arena Physica) is a New York-headquartered applied-research company building what it calls "electromagnetic superintelligence." Its flagship product, Atlas, is an AI-powered hardware-engineering platform that pairs general intelligence with deterministic physics models to accelerate the design, verification, and debugging of electronic and RF hardware. Atlas ingests telemetry, schematics, CAD files, and firmware, then connects via API or MCP (Model Context Protocol) to engineering toolchains such as Jira, GitHub, Altium, Cadence, and SPICE simulators, and to test equipment from vendors like Keysight and Tektronix. Atlas RF Studio, the company's RF design tool, is currently in beta. The company operates from New York City (HQ), San Francisco, and Los Angeles.

providers.name: Astrus
providers.description: Astrus is an AI-powered microchip design company automating the physical layout of analog circuits. Founded in 2022 by Brad Moon (CEO) and Zeyi Wang (CTO) and based in Toronto and Waterloo, Canada, Astrus applies deep reinforcement learning — inspired by AlphaGo-style self-play — to generate thousands of manufacturable analog chip layouts in seconds, targeting high-speed SERDES interconnects used in data-center GPUs. The platform lets circuit designers submit a schematic and receive optimized layouts in minutes rather than the weeks of manual transistor-by-transistor placement that analog EDA traditionally requires. Astrus raised $8M in seed funding led by Khosla Ventures with participation from Pradeep Sindhu, 1517 Fund, Drive Capital and Alumni Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a Khosla Ventures portfolio company; Astrus publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: clounix
providers.description: Clounix (云合智网, Yunhe Zhiwang) is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Shanghai, with additional offices in Hangzhou, Nanjing, Beijing, and Chengdu. It designs high-end networking and communication silicon — high-performance programmable Ethernet switch chips, DPUs (Data Processing Units), and SmartNIC intelligent network cards — along with cloud-native infrastructure hardware and customized software for data centers and 5G networks. Its switch platforms run the open-source SONiC network operating system, and the company maintains a public GitHub organization with SONiC/SAI networking software. Clounix is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It currently publishes no public developer-facing API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Exowatt
providers.description: Exowatt is a clean-energy technology company redefining power generation for the AI era. Its flagship Exowatt P3 is a modular, dispatchable solar-thermal energy platform that captures solar energy with proprietary Fresnel lenses and heat exchangers, stores it in a high-efficiency heat battery, and dispatches electricity on demand via a proprietary heat engine, delivering up to 24 hours of dispatchable baseload power. The systems are factory-built in the USA from abundant, low-cost materials without rare-earth minerals, and are aimed at energy-intensive customers such as AI data centers and utilities. Backed by a16z and Felicis, Exowatt is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Hermeus
providers.description: Hermeus is an American aerospace and defense company building rapidly reusable high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft for national-security missions in partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the company applies a hardware-rich, rapid design-build-test approach to move quickly from concept to flight. Its programs include Quarterhorse, a reusable high-speed flight-test aircraft; Darkhorse, a multi-mission reusable hypersonic uncrewed aerial system (UAS); and Chimera, a hybrid turbine-based combined-cycle engine that transitions from turbojet takeoff through supersonic flight into hypersonic acceleration. Hermeus is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile tracks the company's public web, security, and corporate properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Heron Power
providers.description: Heron Power is an industrial power-electronics company modernizing the electrical grid with solid-state transformers and integrated power conversion systems. Founded by former Tesla executive Drew Baglino, the company builds Heron Link products that combine a solid-state transformer with a power supply or inverter for two markets: data centers (AI and hyperscale power delivery, including 800 VDC datacenter architectures) and solar-and-storage renewable energy systems. Heron Power targets the grid infrastructure bottlenecks of the clean-energy transition, replacing century-old passive transformer technology with dense, controllable, software-defined power hardware. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Breakthrough Energy. Heron Power is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence.

providers.name: JMEM
providers.description: JMEM (Jmem Tek) is an upstream semiconductor company specializing in Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) solutions for quantum-resilient cybersecurity. The company designs hardware security intellectual property and provides IC design services, offering products such as JRoot, JPUF, JCrypt, and JShield, along with Zanker, described as the world's first PUF-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC) chip. Its NIST-aligned, quantum-safe encryption and hardware-anchored identity authentication protect chips against counterfeiting and unauthorized modification across UAV, automotive, surveillance, and fintech applications. JMEM is a portfolio company of 500 Global, added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public web presence; it publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Upscale AI
providers.description: Upscale AI is a pure-play AI networking infrastructure company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, founded by industry veterans from Palo Alto Networks, Marvell, Cisco, and Google and led by CEO Barun Kar. The company builds a full-stack, open-standards AI fabric spanning silicon, systems, and software — its SkyHammer scale-up ASIC architecture and NVIDIA Spectrum-X/SONiC-based scale-out Ethernet systems connect accelerators, memory, and storage for large-scale AI training and inference. Backed by Mayfield among others (Premji Invest, NVIDIA, Salesforce Ventures, Temasek, Tiger Global), it has raised $500M total at a $2B valuation. The company publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface surface beyond a Webflow-served llms.txt; it sells networking hardware and software evaluated by hyperscalers and neoclouds.

providers.name: VSORA
providers.description: VSORA is a French fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Meudon-La-Foret, France, that designs high-performance AI inference chips. Its Jotunn 8 data-center inference chip (3200 Tflops fp8, 288 GB HBM, built on TSMC 5nm) targets cost- and energy-efficient large-scale AI inference, and its Tyr family (Tyr 2, Tyr 4) targets edge AI and on-device processing. VSORA is a Partech portfolio company and publishes no public web API or developer portal as of July 2026.

providers.name: Apptronik
providers.description: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas-based humanoid robotics company founded in 2016 as a spinout from the Human Centered Robotics Lab at the University of Texas at Austin. Co-founded by Jeff Cardenas (CEO), Dr. Nick Paine (CTO), and Dr. Luis Sentis (scientific advisor), the company designs and manufactures Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot standing 5'8", weighing 160 lbs, capable of lifting 55 lbs, and running for roughly 4 hours on a swappable battery. Apollo targets warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics applications including trailer unloading, case picking, palletization, machine tending, and workcell delivery. Apptronik has commercial pilot programs and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz (automotive manufacturing logistics), GXO Logistics (multi-phase R&D in U.S. distribution centers), Jabil (supply-chain partner helping scale production and an internal Apollo deployment), and Google DeepMind (Apollo integrates Gemini Robotics vision-language-action models). The company previously built NASA's Valkyrie humanoid and ten-plus other research robots. As of February 2026 Apptronik had raised more than $935M (including a $520M Series A-X extension) at a reported $5B valuation, with investors including B Capital, Google, and Mercedes-Benz. The company sells/leases Apollo to enterprise customers via a direct contact-sales motion and ships a proprietary "point-and-click" control suite for deploying solutions; there is no public developer portal, no published REST/AsyncAPI/gRPC API, no public SDK, no open-source release, and no public GitHub repositories under the `apptronik` org.

providers.name: Path Robotics
providers.description: Path Robotics is a Columbus, Ohio autonomous welding robotics company founded in 2018 by brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (CEO and CTO) out of Case Western Reserve University. The company builds AI-powered intelligent welding cells that automate metal fabrication for defense shipyards, utility and energy infrastructure, data centers, and heavy industry. Its core technology is Obsidian, a physical-AI reinforcement-learning agent trained inside Path's proprietary Weld World Model on tens of millions of welded inches; Obsidian runs at the edge of each cell and makes real-time, seam-by-seam welding decisions using a sensor stack of two cameras plus four lasers that deliver sub-millimeter 360-degree awareness around the torch. Path markets the cells with a CapEx-free consumption model and reports 97%+ first-pass yield, 4x productivity, and 30% lower welding costs across customers including HII (America's largest military shipbuilder), Saronic, LAD Services, Tycrop, Mine Rite Technologies, and Millerbernd. In April 2026 Path announced Rove, a mobile welding system mounted on a quadruped platform, extending its addressable geometry beyond fixed-cell applications. The company has raised approximately $271M across Seed through Series D from Drive Capital, Matter Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Addition, and Yamaha Motor Ventures, with the most recent $100M Series D closing in October 2024. Path Robotics has no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; its GitHub organization contains roughly 50 repositories that are almost entirely upstream open-source forks (ROS, protobuf, abseil, ceres-solver, pytorch3d, etc.) used as internal build dependencies rather than published developer artifacts. Revenue is earned through welding-cell deployments, services, and the consumable weld-output model — not API monetization.

providers.name: 21 Market
providers.description: 21 Market is the API Evangelist network profile for 주식회사 21세기전파상 (21st Century Electronics Shop Co., Ltd.), a South Korean consumer-electronics resale company that operates the Repercent (리퍼센트) service at repercent.com. Repercent buys used smartphones and mobile devices — iPhone, Galaxy, tablets, and laptops — from individual sellers, providing instant online price quotes, fast payment, and a simple pickup/logistics flow for secondhand device trade-in. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company and was surfaced into the network as a venture portfolio lead. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation surface; this profile captures verified company identity, its live web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Alterego
providers.description: Alterego is a Boston-based startup, spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 2025, building a near-telepathic silent-speech interface: a minimal, non-invasive wearable that detects the faint neuromuscular signals produced when a person internally verbalizes words, letting them interact with AI and computers without typing, tapping, or speaking aloud. Its "Silent Sense" technology responds only to intentional internal speech, keeping private thoughts private while enabling hands-free, screen-free messaging, queries, and information access. The company is pre-launch, backed by investors including Canaan, Granite Ventures, Mayfield, Rembrandt Venture Partners, and Cisco Investments. As of this profile Alterego publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Armstrong Robotics
providers.description: Armstrong Robotics is building general-purpose robots for commercial kitchens, beginning with autonomous dishwashing systems that load, run, and unload dishware without human intervention. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company is an early-stage robotics startup focused on kitchen labor automation. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead awaiting a public API surface, and this profile carries only the identity and domain-security signals that could be verified from its public website.

providers.name: B2X
providers.description: B2X is a Munich-founded hardware lifecycle orchestration company that manages the complete service journey of electronic devices for global brands and operators — from warehousing, staging and onsite deployment through customer support, maintenance and repair, returns management, refurbishment and recycling. Its proprietary B2XONE platform combines ONE Connect (self-service customer portals with track & trace and appointment booking), ONE Service (operations management for repair, warehouse, inventory and logistics) and ONE Analytics (real-time KPIs and predictive insights), delivered through a network of 155+ certified service partners across 25+ countries. B2X serves mobile and consumer electronics, retail automation, B2B/enterprise and mission-critical segments. As of this profile, B2X does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: BigScreen
providers.description: Bigscreen is a social virtual-reality company founded in 2014 by Darshan Shankar. Its flagship Bigscreen app lets people watch movies, mirror their Windows PC desktop, play games, and hang out with friends inside shared virtual rooms across major VR platforms. In 2023 the company shipped the Bigscreen Beyond, an ultra-compact, custom-fit OLED PC-VR headset, followed by the Beyond 2 line. Bigscreen is a consumer VR hardware and software company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors; it does not currently operate a public developer program or REST API. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Cowboy Space
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation builds space-based infrastructure for artificial-intelligence computing. Its flagship program, Stampede, is a constellation of solar-powered GPU data centers in Low Earth Orbit that integrate the rocket's upper stage with the satellite to form a megawatt-class data center with active thermal management and integrated compute. The company positions orbital compute as an alternative to terrestrial data centers, whose grid-connection lead times in major US markets can run five to seven years or more, arguing that Earth's energy grid cannot keep pace with AI demand. Cowboy Space is an early-stage aerospace and AI-infrastructure startup backed by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital; it currently publishes a corporate and careers presence with no public developer API.

providers.name: Cowboy Space Corporation
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation is a space infrastructure company building orbital data centers to address Earth's power constraints on artificial intelligence. Its Stampede satellite constellation places megawatt-class, GPU-equipped data centers in Low Earth Orbit powered by abundant solar energy, integrating the compute payload directly into the rocket's upper stage to maximize capacity and sidestep the multi-year terrestrial grid-connection delays that constrain traditional data centers. The company is an early-stage, venture-backed lead (backed by IVP); it currently publishes a corporate marketing site and careers portal but no developer portal, public API, or technical documentation.

providers.name: De-Ice
providers.description: De-Ice Technologies is a Somerville, Massachusetts deep-tech aviation startup building a chemical-free aircraft de-icing system that replaces conventional glycol spray with electrically heated strips applied to aircraft surfaces, removing snow and ice prior to takeoff. The technology eliminates weather-related departure delays, cuts glycol spraying costs, and reduces CO₂ emissions from idling fuel burn and chemical production. Named to Time's Best Inventions of 2024, De-Ice counts Air Canada as its launch customer and is backed by Techstars. This is a physical-hardware aviation company and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Fishbit
providers.description: Fishbit is a smart-aquarium management company whose platform pairs a mobile app (iOS/Android) with connected hardware — the Fishbit Monitor, which tracks water parameters such as pH, temperature, and salinity in real time, and the Fishbit Controller, which wirelessly automates aquarium equipment. Hobbyists and reef keepers use the system to remotely monitor tank conditions and automate lighting, pumps, and dosing. The company sells its monitoring and control hardware through an online store and ran a device-manufacturer partner program (e.g. RapidLED Corona integration). No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a connected-hardware / IoT lead.

providers.name: NGL Energy Partners
providers.description: NGL Energy Partners LP is a diversified midstream master limited partnership providing transportation, storage, blending, and marketing services for crude oil, natural gas liquids, refined products, and water solutions to producers and end-users across the energy industry. The company is publicly traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol NGL and operates three primary business units: Crude Oil Logistics, Water Solutions, and NGL Liquids.

providers.name: NuStar Energy
providers.description: NuStar Energy is one of the largest independent liquids terminal and pipeline operators in the United States, transporting and storing crude oil, refined products, and renewable fuels. NuStar does not currently publish public APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: Opalcamera
providers.description: Opal Electronics is an original hardware company based in California specializing in the design and engineering of premium webcams and creator-focused camera devices. Its products include the Opal C1, a professional-grade webcam built around a large image sensor and DSLR-style optics, and the Opal Tadpole, an ultra-compact clip-on webcam for laptops, paired with the Opal Composer desktop software that adds virtual-camera, scene, and streaming controls. The company is backed by Kindred Ventures. Opal runs a consumer hardware business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner platform; this profile captures its public web presence and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Porotech
providers.description: Porotech (Poro Technologies Ltd) is a Cambridge University deep-tech spinout, founded in 2018 by Dr. Tongtong Zhu, Dr. Yingjun Liu, and Professor Rachel Oliver, that develops gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor materials and MicroLED display technology. Its proprietary PoroGaN porous-InGaN epitaxy enables full-color MicroLED production on 4-to-12-inch wafers using a single material system, and its Dynamic Pixel Tuning (DPT) technology generates any visible color from a single LED chip. Porotech supplies epitaxy, micro displays, and light-engine products for AR/VR/MR applications, and has established mass-production partnerships with Foxconn, PSMC (Powerchip), and GIS. The company is backed by Speedinvest. Porotech is a hardware and semiconductor manufacturer and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event/streaming surface; this record is maintained for company-level discovery within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Prototyping.io
providers.description: Prototyping.io is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building AI-driven autonomous manufacturing for mechanical parts. The platform converts CAD designs into finished physical parts by automating design-for-manufacturability analysis, manufacturability evaluation, production planning, machine execution, and quality control across CNC machining, sheet metal, 3D printing, injection molding, extrusion, and die casting. Founded by Revanth Bodepudi (CEO) and Prerit Oberai (CTO) in the San Francisco Bay Area, it targets hardware teams in robotics, AI infrastructure, energy, automotive, and defense, aiming to cut hardware iteration cycles from weeks to days with no minimum order quantities and tight tolerances. The company is in early-access/waitlist stage and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Seeqc
providers.description: Seeqc is developing the first digital quantum computing platform for businesses, integrating all core functions of a quantum computer - qubits together with classical control logic - onto a single superconducting chip operating at millikelvin temperatures. Founded in 2019 and holding over 115 patents, the company combines classical and quantum technologies to address the efficiency, stability, and cost challenges endemic to scalable quantum computing, and also offers superconducting chip foundry services. As a quantum-hardware and foundry company, Seeqc currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: The Bot Company
providers.description: The Bot Company is a San Francisco robotics startup founded in 2024 by Kyle Vogt, the co-founder and former CEO of Cruise, building a helpful general-purpose robot for every home to automate everyday household chores. Its team draws from Tesla, Cruise, OpenAI, Google, and Pixar, and the company has raised roughly $301M (reportedly valued near $2B) from investors including Spark Capital and SV Angel. As of this profile the company operates a marketing and careers site only and publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Visibl Semiconductors
providers.description: Visibl Semiconductors builds an AI-enabled coordination layer for custom chip design teams, positioning itself as "the first coordination layer for chip design." Its platform continuously monitors specifications against implementation to detect drift early, investigates issues by assembling evidence bundles, and proposes fixes through AI agents that require human approval before any change is deployed. The company frames this as a faster path to custom silicon and is backed by Y Combinator. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Westmag
providers.description: Western Magnetics (Westmag) designs and manufactures brushless DC (BLDC) drone motors and robot actuators in South San Francisco, California. Built and scaled in America and NDAA-compliant from day one, Westmag is a vertically integrated motor company spanning design, manufacturing, and supply chain — producing high-volume BLDC drone motors for Group 1, 2, and 3 UAS platforms (20-100mm stators, Kv 100-3,000, outrunner and inrunner) and integrated actuators for humanoid and mobile robots (torque 1-150Nm, 24-48V, gearing 6:1-12:1). Founded by David Hansen (CEO) and Jordan Sanders (COO) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Menlo Ventures, and NFDG. This is a hardware company; it currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Zipline
providers.description: Zipline is a South San Francisco–headquartered autonomous logistics company operating the world's largest commercial drone delivery network, with more than two million customer deliveries flown across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan. Zipline designs, builds, and operates two end-to-end aircraft platforms: Platform 1 (P1, "Sparrow"), a long-range fixed-wing aircraft that launches from a catapult, parachutes payloads from altitude, and is used primarily for national-scale healthcare logistics — delivering blood products, vaccines, medicines, and lab samples to hospitals and clinics — and Platform 2 (P2), a short-range hybrid VTOL aircraft with an autonomous tethered "droid" delivery vehicle that lowers packages from a hovering aircraft directly to a designated point on the ground, enabling precision quick-commerce delivery from restaurants, retailers, pharmacies, and hospitals. Zipline's customer roster includes Walmart, OhioHealth, Michigan Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic Florida, MultiCare, Sweetgreen, GNC, Jet's Pizza, the governments of Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, and Kenya, and Japan's Toyota Tsusho, with the P2 platform actively scaling across the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex, Pea Ridge (AR), and expanding into Houston and Phoenix in 2026. The company also operates one of the largest civil autonomous aviation stacks in the world — proprietary detect-and-avoid, route planning, weather, fleet operations, and flight-control software — and in 2025 received the first-ever FAA Part 135 BVLOS (beyond-visual-line-of-sight) operational approval permitting drone package delivery without visual observers. Zipline is a privately held company; its revenue model is drone-as-a-service contracts with healthcare systems, retailers, restaurant brands, and governments. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, GitHub organization, status page, changelog, or self-service developer portal — integrations with customer systems (order management, EHR, WMS, dispatch) are delivered as managed enterprise integrations rather than as a public programmable API.

providers.name: houmo
providers.description: HOUMO.AI (后摩智能) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 that develops compute-in-memory (CIM / storage-and-computation integrated) edge AI chips for running large language models and other AI workloads on endpoint devices. Its products include the MOMAGIC (H30) series processors, LIQING M.2 modules, and Limou (LM 5050 / LM 5070 / LM 30) AI acceleration cards, paired with the Houmo Avenue software toolchain (PyTorch / TensorFlow / ONNX, CUDA-style front end) for model quantization, compilation, and deployment. The company targets edge inference, autonomous driving, embodied robotics, and intelligent mobile devices, and runs a developer community with documentation and downloads. This profile is a hardware / AI-chip vendor with a developer toolchain rather than a public web API provider; no REST/OpenAPI, OAuth, or hosted API surface was found.

providers.name: Infleqtion
providers.description: Infleqtion is a Louisville/Boulder, Colorado quantum-technology company — formerly ColdQuanta — that builds neutral-atom quantum computers, precision atomic clocks, and quantum sensors for governments, corporations, and research institutions. Its computing portfolio spans Sqale (a full-stack, fault-tolerant neutral-atom quantum computer), Quantum Cores (ready-to-use neutral-atom systems for laboratories), and Superstaq, an open-source quantum software platform with proprietary cross-layer optimization that compiles Qiskit, Cirq, and OpenQASM circuits down to hardware-native operations and routes them across heterogeneous quantum backends. Infleqtion's sensing portfolio includes the Tiqker optical atomic clock, Quantum Spectrum (Rydberg atomic spectrum sensing), and inertial sensors for GPS-denied positioning. The company was founded in 2007 as ColdQuanta, rebranded to Infleqtion in November 2022 after absorbing the Super.tech quantum-software acquisition, and became Infleqtion, Inc. (NASDAQ: INFQ) in January 2026. Superstaq (qiskit-superstaq, cirq-superstaq, general-superstaq) is the only developer-facing public surface; the hardware and sensing businesses are sold via direct engagement and government contracts rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Physicsx
providers.description: PhysicsX is an AI-native engineering software company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in London (Shoreditch) with an office in New York, building a platform that embeds physics AI directly into industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows. The platform unifies simulation, physics AI, data, and engineering applications into a single foundation, pairing fast AI-driven physics inference (Deep Physics Models) with numerical simulation to compress development cycles and expand the design space engineers can explore. It integrates with industry-standard CAE/CAD tooling (ANSYS, CATIA, Siemens NX, OpenFOAM, Siemens Star-CCM+), runs cloud-agnostically across AWS and Azure plus hybrid and on-premises deployments, and serves aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy and renewables. Born out of Formula One, PhysicsX has raised roughly $489M across five rounds from investors including General Catalyst, Atomico, Temasek, NVIDIA, Siemens, and Applied Materials. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: BRINC
providers.description: BRINC builds a connected ecosystem of drones, software, and services purpose-built for public safety in the United States. Its Drone as First Responder (DFR) systems — the Guardian and Responder outdoor drones, the Lemur 2 indoor tactical drone, and the throwable BRINC Ball — pair with LiveOps teleoperations software (livestreaming, two-way comms, evidence management) to put a camera overhead within seconds of a 911 call. BRINC reports deployments across 900+ public safety agencies in all 50 states, sub-70-second average drone arrival times, and a recent $125M funding round. The company also runs its Safeguard upgrade-and-repair program and grant/DFR playbook services. BRINC exposes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface as of this profile; this entry is enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: OctoAI
providers.description: OctoAI (formerly OctoML) was a Seattle-based AI inference platform founded in 2019 as a University of Washington Allen School spin-out of the Apache TVM project. The company originally focused on machine-learning model optimization and compilation across CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators, and in June 2023 launched a generative-AI SaaS inference platform that served open-source foundation models (Llama 2, Mixtral, SDXL, Stable Diffusion, Whisper) behind OpenAI-style REST APIs with Python and TypeScript SDKs. In January 2024 OctoML formally rebranded to OctoAI and in April 2024 unveiled OctoStack, a self-contained generative-AI production stack for deploying models inside customer VPC and on-premises environments across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and AWS Inferentia. NVIDIA acquired OctoAI in September 2024 for a reported $165M (down from a 2021 peak valuation of ~$900M), with CEO Luis Ceze and key staff joining NVIDIA. OctoAI sent customers a "Wind down of OctoAI Services" notice and terminated all hosted endpoints, accounts, and SDK access on 31 October 2024. The octo.ai domain now 301-redirects to nvidia.com and no public OctoAI product, API, dashboard, or developer portal remains; the technology has been absorbed into NVIDIA's internal AI inference stack and is not separately purchasable. This catalog entry is a historical record of the former OctoAI developer surface and the GitHub artifacts that remain.

providers.name: Prewitt Ridge
providers.description: Prewitt Ridge builds SysGit, "the collaboration layer for complex hardware" — an enterprise platform that applies software development practices to systems engineering. SysGit provides Git-based version control for requirements and system models, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) workflows, AI-assisted systems engineering automation, and SysMLv2 compliance for open-standards adherence. The platform targets defense and aerospace teams, with customers including the US Air Force, GTRI, Leidos, and Anduril. Prewitt Ridge is a Techstars-backed company added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or .well-known documents.

providers.name: Cloudistics (Fungible)
providers.description: Cloudistics was a composable, hyperconverged cloud infrastructure software company whose platform managed applications, virtual machines, storage, and networking across on-premises datacenters via a REST API and an official Python client (with the ccli command-line tool). Fungible acquired the Cloudistics software team and assets in September 2020 to build DPU-powered hyperdisaggregated infrastructure, and Microsoft acquired Fungible in January 2023 to bolster Azure datacenter networking and storage. As independent companies both are now defunct: the primary product domains are parked, the public GitHub organization has been emptied, and the PyPI package has been removed. The one surviving public developer surface is the read-only Cloudistics API Python Client documentation hosted on Read the Docs. This profile is retained as a historical API Evangelist network record.

providers.name: ShelterLogic Group
providers.description: ShelterLogic Group is the world leader in shade, shelter, storage, and outdoor lifestyle products with over 70 years of industry experience. Launched in 1991, ShelterLogic develops tough, affordable shelter solutions for everyday consumers and commercial customers. The company operates three manufacturing facilities in the US and China and maintains worldwide distribution. The ShelterLogic brand portfolio includes ShelterLogic, SOJAG, Arrow Storage Products, Quik Shade, CAMP&GO, RIO Beach, and licensed brands including Tommy Bahama, Margaritaville, Life is Good, and Scotts Miracle-Gro. As a B2C manufacturer and retailer, ShelterLogic does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Carpenter Technology
providers.description: Carpenter Technology Corporation is a U.S.-based producer and distributor of premium specialty alloys — including titanium alloys, powder metals, high-temperature stainless steels, tool steels, and soft magnetic alloys — serving the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, and industrial end markets. The company supports customers through technical product resources such as its Alloy Finder, alloy technical data sheets, conversion tables, and a member-only Customer Portal for order and account self-service, but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Extra Space Storage
providers.description: Extra Space Storage Inc. is a fully integrated, self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust (REIT) and one of the largest operators of self-storage properties in the United States. The company owns, operates, and manages thousands of self-storage facilities across the country, offering storage units, vehicle storage, and business storage solutions. Extra Space Storage does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Mirana Toys
providers.description: Mirana Toys (Mirana Innovations Pvt Ltd) is an India-based smart-toy company and OEM/ODM manufacturer of electronic toys — RC cars, monster trucks, drones, educational toys, and AI/AR toys. It pairs its consumer products with the Mirana smart app (iOS and Android), a mobile gaming platform that lets kids and adults control and play with Mirana toys over Bluetooth. As an OEM partner it offers in-house PCB/PCBA design and SMT assembly, tooling and mold design, mobile app development, compliance support (ASTM, EN-71, RoHS, ISO, SMETA), and global logistics for toy brands and retailers. Backed by Accel. The company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and support center but no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Aclarity Water
providers.description: Aclarity, Inc. (Aclarity Water) is a Medway, Massachusetts cleantech company that designs and manufactures on-site PFAS destruction technology. Its flagship Aclarity Octa system uses electrochemical oxidation to break the carbon-fluorine bond in per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), destroying these "forever chemicals" at landfills, centralized waste-treatment facilities, industrial sites (laundry, pulp and paper, automotive), municipal and industrial wastewater, drinking-water treatment, and AFFF-contaminated aviation sites. Aclarity is a portfolio company of DCVC. It is a physical water-treatment hardware and services business with no public developer API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company intelligence.

providers.name: Auradine (Velaura AI)
providers.description: Auradine, Inc. is a Silicon Valley semiconductor and infrastructure company founded in 2022, in 2026 rebranded as Velaura AI, Inc. The company designs ultra-low-power compute solutions for data center, edge, and physical AI applications, anchored by its Titan Core silicon design and IP platform that reduces the power required for AI compute while maintaining performance. Its Teraflux product line delivers high-efficiency Bitcoin mining hardware (3nm ASICs, air- and hydro-cooled miners, containers, and fleet management software) deployed by leading Bitcoin data center operators. Auradine raised over $300 million across its funding rounds, including a $153M Series C, and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Auradine/Velaura AI publishes no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Ayr Energy
providers.description: Ayr Energy is a power grid equipment manufacturer founded in 2024 and headquartered in Mountain View, California, backed by General Catalyst. The company designs and builds custom-engineered electrical infrastructure - power, distribution, and special-purpose transformers, high-voltage circuit breakers, and medium-voltage switchgear - for renewable energy, data center, utility, industrial, and oil & gas customers. Ayr operates six manufacturing facilities across India (Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu) and emphasizes accelerated delivery of grid hardware in months rather than years. Ayr Energy does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Biren Technology
providers.description: Biren Technology (Shanghai Biren Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company that designs general-purpose GPUs (GPGPUs) for AI training, inference, and high-performance computing. Its flagship BR100-series accelerators are programmed through BIRENSUPA, a CUDA-like software platform that bundles the BRCC compiler, a hardware abstraction layer, deep-learning and general-compute acceleration libraries, and a developer toolchain with support for PyTorch, TensorFlow, and PaddlePaddle. Biren distributes its drivers, SDK, and documentation through its developer.birentech.com developer community rather than a public web/REST API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Calamu Technologies
providers.description: Calamu Technologies is a data-first cybersecurity company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Clinton, New Jersey. Its flagship product, Calamu Protect (Data Harbor), is a cyber vault for backup and recovery data that uses a patented process to fragment and scatter data across multiple storage locations, rendering it valueless ("Digital Sludge") to attackers even if breached and instantly reassembling it for authorized applications and users. Calamu integrates with enterprise backup platforms including Veeam, Veritas NetBackup, Dell EMC, Nutanix, Wasabi, and StarWind, and exposes an S3-compatible storage interface for data protection. The company is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Claros
providers.description: Claros is a data center power delivery company reimagining how energy moves from chip to grid for AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. Based in Torrance, California with an office in McLean, Virginia, the company builds two hardware-and-software product lines: an Integrated Voltage Regulator (IVR) that targets the roughly 40 percent of chip power lost to heat at the point of delivery, and a Power Gateway that manages broader data center power distribution where 30 to 50 percent of power is lost to transmission, conversion, and cooling. Claros is an early-stage hardware company backed by General Catalyst and Red Cell Partners; its founding team collectively holds 286 patents and has brought more than 80 gigawatts of projects to market.
