Co-founded by Talmon Firestone (CEO) and Dr. Tom Wallace-Smith (CTO), the company applies compact, modular fusion to near-term problems: large-scale medical isotope production to address the global isotope shortage affecting cancer diagnosis and treatment, spent fission fuel analysis, neutronics research, industrial neutron irradiation and accelerated lifetime testing, materials-damage testing, nuclear-waste burnup, and hybrid fission/fusion power. It is a Speedinvest deep-tech portfolio company. Astral Systems is a hardware/deep-tech provider and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Astro Mechanica
providers.description: Astro Mechanica is a San Francisco aerospace company, founded in 2021 by Ian Brooke, reinventing supersonic flight for a new jet age. Its flagship Duality electric combined-cycle engine is engineered to stay efficient from takeoff through Mach 3+ by reconfiguring between turbofan, turbojet, and ramjet modes using a hybrid turboelectric architecture. The company designs engines, airframes, and flight systems in-house, has been selected to develop an engine for the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, and is backed by a16z, Lowercarbon Capital, and Y Combinator. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As an aerospace hardware manufacturer, Astro Mechanica publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web and identity surface only.

providers.name: Ateios
providers.description: Ateios Systems is an Indianapolis-based advanced battery manufacturer that produces high-energy, recyclable, PFA-free battery electrodes for global battery makers. Its proprietary RaiCure platform is a solvent-free, cure-on-command coating process using energy-curable polymers instead of solvent-based thermal drying, enabling thicker electrodes (>10 mAh/cm2), higher energy density, and roughly 5x faster coating throughput at lower cost and emissions. Ateios targets medical device, IoT, mobility, and defense markets. Founded in 2017 and backed by Techstars, TitletownTech, Good Growth Capital and others, the company is a materials/hardware manufacturer and publishes no developer API, SDK, or programmatic developer platform.

providers.name: ATMI Sales
providers.description: ATMI Sales (Advanced Technical Marketing Inc.) is a manufacturers' representative and technical sales firm serving the electronics and semiconductor industry across the Pacific Northwest and Western Canada. The company connects customers with component suppliers through a research, development, and build model — identifying suitable technology solutions, building supplier relationships, and ensuring component availability and supply-chain sourcing in the regions where products are manufactured. ATMI maintains a line card of partner technologies and works with distributors to fulfill orders. This is a non-developer B2B sales and distribution company; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of sierra-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Atom Semiconductor
providers.description: Atom Semiconductor (Atom Semiconductor Technologies Limited) is a fabless mixed-signal chip design company founded in Hong Kong in October 2020, with offices in Shenzhen and Shanghai. It designs high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for consumer and industrial IoT systems across three product lines: digital sensor chips (temperature/humidity, pressure, optical), analog-to-digital converters (24-bit Sigma-Delta, high-precision SAR, and high-speed GSPS ADCs), and microprocessors. Its first product, the AS1412 24-bit Sigma-Delta ADC, shipped for customer trials in late 2021. The company raised roughly 100M yuan in a pre-A round led by Qiming Venture Partners (with Venus Medtech and Alibaba Entrepreneurs Fund) and was named to the Forbes Asia 100 To Watch 2022. It is a hardware chip designer and does not publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Axera Tech
providers.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Byanat
providers.description: Byanat is an Oman-based, award-winning AI company offering a unified platform for optimizing digital infrastructure across telecommunications networks and data centers. The platform pairs system-wide visibility with custom-tailored automation to scale operations, ensure compliance, and promote sustainability, an approach the company frames as "Infrastructure 4.0." Its product families span mobile network solutions (site management, degradation detection, auto-discovery, performance analytics), data centre solutions (predictive analytics, capacity forecasting, energy management, infrastructure monitoring), and an API and integration layer for cross-platform connectivity and AI-powered workflow automation. Byanat is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference; its API and integration capability is delivered as a managed product.

providers.name: Calxeda
providers.description: Calxeda was an Austin, Texas semiconductor startup — founded in 2008 as Smooth-Stone by Barry Evans, Larry Wikelius and David Borland — that built ARM-based EnergyCore system-on-chip server processors (ECX-1000, ECX-2000/Midway) aimed at low-power, high-density data center workloads. It raised roughly $90-103M from venture investors including Battery Ventures, and its silicon shipped in Boston Limited Viridis appliances and HP Project Moonshot systems. Calxeda ceased operations in December 2013 after a refinancing round fell through, and its ARM server IP resurfaced under Silver Lining Systems in December 2014. The company published no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts, and calxeda.com is now a parked domain listed for sale, so there is no live API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.

providers.name: CIX Technology
providers.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Coolso
providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Daqstra
providers.description: Daqstra is an AI-native operating platform for complex test infrastructure, giving aerospace, energy, and robotics teams observability and orchestration for the physical world. The platform connects data-acquisition hardware (National Instruments, PLCs, and custom equipment) at the edge, centralizes and versions test data in the cloud, and orchestrates hardware sequences and test logic as code through Python and REST APIs. Daqstra Edge streams live signals from physical hardware, Daqstra Hub (Strata Hub) organizes test-campaign data with AI-powered insight, and the Daqstra API lets engineers drive test runs programmatically instead of through manual CSV workflows. The company was founded by aerospace-propulsion and avionics engineers and is backed by Y Combinator (S26 batch).

providers.name: Epirus
providers.description: Epirus is a Torrance, California-based defense technology company building solid-state, software-defined high-power microwave (HPM) directed-energy systems for counter-electronics and counter-unmanned-aerial-systems (cUAS) missions. Its flagship product is Leonidas, a non-kinetic HPM weapon system designed to defeat single drones and large drone swarms by disabling their onboard electronics, with a growing product family that includes Leonidas IFPC-HPM (Indirect Fire Protection Capability — High-Power Microwave) for the U.S. Army, Leonidas Expeditionary (ExDECS) for the U.S. Marine Corps, Leonidas H2O for maritime interdiction, the portable Leonidas Pod, and Stryker Leonidas (with General Dynamics Land Systems). Epirus also collaborates with Anduril, Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, Kodiak AI, Peraton, and Palantir, and has received contracts from the U.S. Army, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, DARPA, ONR, and Singapore's DSTA. The company is privately held, has raised more than $550M across Series B/C/D, and operates under CMMC Level 2 certification. Its product surface is classified defense hardware and embedded firmware — there is no public developer portal, REST API, SDK, or open-source software offering.

providers.name: Fabheads
providers.description: Fabheads is a carbon fiber and composite manufacturing company (Fabheads Automation) that delivers end-to-end composite product development — design, analysis, tooling, prototyping, and production — using its own fiber-printing and automated-layup technology alongside traditional craftsmanship. It serves aerospace, mobility, marine, robotics, medical, and sports customers from aerospace-grade facilities, and publishes the C6 Slicer tool for composite fiber printing. Backed by Accel. As a hardware manufacturer it exposes no public developer API; this profile captures identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: finern
providers.description: Finern (Finern Automation) is a China-based industrial automation company that designs and builds fully automated production lines and intelligent measurement systems for manufacturing. It serves five sectors — automotive, electronics, new energy (battery/EV), healthcare/pharmaceutical equipment, and consumer goods — with automated assembly, testing, and inspection systems. The company reports 600+ personnel, 30,000+ square meters of facilities, 100+ global clients, 8 international sites, and 4 R&D centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Finern publishes a corporate marketing website but does not currently expose any public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface (no /.well-known/*, llms.txt, or OpenAPI found on probe).

providers.name: Gokin
providers.description: Gokin Solar Co., Ltd. (高景太阳能股份有限公司) is a Chinese photovoltaic manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Jiangsu, China. The company produces monocrystalline silicon ingots and wafers (N-type and P-type) and high-efficiency solar modules (GOKIN BC and FLAMINGO series), operating four major production bases with roughly 100 GW of wafer and 16 GW of module annual capacity. Ranked among the top three global silicon-wafer shippers, Gokin employs 6,000+ people, holds 500+ patents, and serves utility, commercial, and residential solar projects across 30+ countries. Backed by IDG Capital, Gokin is a solar-hardware manufacturer with a corporate marketing website and no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Gyre Energy
providers.description: Gyre Energy is a UK-based climate-tech company that reduces cooling costs for operators of cold storage facilities, data centers, and building portfolios by combining artificial intelligence with thermal energy storage. Its platform pairs Gyre AI, a digital twin that learns a facility's thermal behavior and shifts cooling cycles to run when grid energy is cheapest and greenest, with an integrated thermal energy storage "cold battery" and a real-time monitoring and controls layer that tracks temperature, energy use, and door-open events. The company reports up to 50% lower cooling expenses, 38% verified energy cost savings at its first commercial cold storage deployment, a 91% reduction in temperature excursions, and a payback period of under 1.5 years. Gyre Energy is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and, as of July 2026, secured $1.3m in funding to support a major blue-chip deployment and global scaling. It currently exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Holo
providers.description: Holo (Holo AM, operating under Greene Group Industries) is an advanced metal additive manufacturing company founded in 2017 and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its PureForm metal 3D printing platform uses digital light processing (DLP) with metal powder-filled photopolymer resins to produce high-resolution, complex metal components with features as small as 50 microns, in pure copper, stainless steels (17-4PH, 316), and in-development cobalt alloy, titanium, nickel superalloys, tool steels, and alumina. Customers submit CAD files and receive prototyped-to-production parts with roughly two-week turnaround, serving medical technology, precision micro-robotics, and general advanced manufacturing. Holo is a hardware manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Letel
providers.description: Shanghai Letel Communication Equipment (Group) Co., Ltd. (上海乐通通信设备（集团）股份有限公司) is a Chinese manufacturer of information and communication network infrastructure, founded in March 1992 and headquartered in Shanghai with over 1,500 employees and 20+ service locations nationwide. Letel builds data center physical infrastructure — cabinet micromodules, cold aisle micromodules, containerized micromodules, pallet IT cabins, and cabinets — alongside communication cabling equipment, optical communication devices, data communication equipment, broadband access equipment, and structural components for notebooks and servers. It operates through subsidiaries including Zhongle Communication Technology Co., Ltd. Letel publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; this is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: LiquidLight
providers.description: LiquidLight, Inc. (Liquid Light) was an electrochemistry company based in Monmouth Junction, New Jersey that developed and licensed process technology for converting carbon dioxide into industrial chemicals. Founded in 2009 by Kyle Teamey, Emily Cole, Andrew Bocarsly, Fouad Elnaggar and Nety Krishna around technology licensed from Princeton University, the company built a portfolio of more than 100 patents covering the electrochemical production of chemicals including monoethylene glycol (MEG), propylene and acetic acid, with MEG as its lead target market. It raised seed funding from Redpoint Ventures and a $15 million Series B in September 2014 from investors including VantagePoint Capital Partners and BP Ventures, and was also a Battery Ventures portfolio investment. Avantium acquired Liquid Light on January 10, 2017 and the company ceased operating independently. LiquidLight was a materials and process-technology company: it never published a public API, developer portal, SDKs or any machine-readable developer surface, and no company web property survives the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an accurate, non-API portfolio record.

providers.name: Mainspring Energy
providers.description: Mainspring Energy is a power generation company that designs and manufactures the Linear Generator, a fuel-flexible, dispatchable distributed power system that converts natural gas, biogas, propane, or hydrogen directly into electricity through a low-temperature, flameless reaction. The modular, factory-built systems deliver firm, flexible onsite power with near-zero NOx emissions and roughly 46% electrical efficiency across deployment scales, targeting data centers, utilities, enterprises, and industrial operations. Mainspring is a venture-backed hardware and energy-infrastructure company (backed by DCVC and General Catalyst) and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Nlight
providers.description: nLIGHT, Inc. (NASDAQ: LASR) is a US-based designer and manufacturer of high-power semiconductor and fiber lasers, optical fibers, and beam-control systems. For more than 25 years the company has served mission-critical directed-energy and defense, sensing, and advanced-manufacturing markets (cutting, welding, additive, medical, and battery production) from a vertically integrated stack spanning semiconductor chips to complete laser systems, with a portfolio of over 450 patents and design and manufacturing based in Camas, Washington. nLIGHT is a hardware and photonics company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Orbital Arc
providers.description: Orbital Arc is a Houston-based deep-tech spacecraft propulsion startup founded in 2023 by Jonathan Huffman, building Gas-Phase Field Effect Electric Propulsion (Gas FEEP) thrusters and the RIOT Drive (Relativistic Ion Thrust Drive) for satellites and in-space transportation. Its ultra-lightweight electric thrusters use solid naphthalene fuel that sublimates at room temperature instead of noble gases, targeting high specific impulse for satellite constellations. Backed by Techstars and Capital Factory, the company completed a sub-scale physics demonstration at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (TRL 3). This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Petra Power
providers.description: Petra Power is an on-site power generation company based in Solon, Ohio, and backed by Techstars, building rapidly deployable, high-efficiency generation systems positioned as "the next 100GW of on-site power." Its technology runs on natural gas, diesel, or hydrogen, claims up to 3x fuel savings versus conventional generators and turbines, and operates silently and odorlessly for use in populated areas. Target applications include data centers, critical backup power, heavy industry, and utility-scale deployment. Petra Power is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Photon Crystal Energy
providers.description: Photon Crystal Energy Technology Ltd. (广东光晶能源科技有限公司) is a China-based perovskite photovoltaic module manufacturer, founded May 2022 and headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong. The company commercializes full wet-process, full-printed perovskite PV modules for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV), photovoltaic curtain walls, rooftop distributed solar, carports and architectural solar applications. Product families include standard, semi-transparent, textured, architectural color and solar tile modules, and the firm operates a 100 MW full-printed perovskite pilot line with IEC 61215 / IEC 61730 certification milestones. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing/corporate website but no public API, SDK, or developer surface.

providers.name: PicoJool
providers.description: PicoJool is an optical connectivity company building Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers (VCSELs) and optical engines for AI and cloud data-center infrastructure. Its 50G NRZ, 100G PAM4, and 200G PAM4 VCSEL arrays target 800G and 1.6T transceivers for PCIe, Ethernet, and InfiniBand, aiming to raise bandwidth density and cut the power cost of moving data across hyperscale AI clusters. Founded in 2024 and based in Palo Alto, California, PicoJool emerged from stealth in November 2025 with $12M led by Playground Global. It is a semiconductor/photonics hardware company with no public API or developer platform; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network for portfolio and market tracking.

providers.name: Plexus
providers.description: Plexus is a global manufacturing and product development company that helps customers in highly regulated industries (Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences, Industrial, and Semiconductor Capital Equipment) design, manufacture, and service their products. Plexus does not currently publish a public developer API; this index tracks customer/supplier portals and corporate web properties.

providers.name: Quantumdiamonds
providers.description: QuantumDiamonds (QD) is a Munich-based German deep-tech company that develops diamond-based quantum sensing systems for semiconductor inspection and failure analysis. The company markets what it describes as the world's first commercially available quantum sensing system for semiconductor inspection, using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond quantum microscopy to detect defects and current-flow anomalies that traditional inspection methods miss. QuantumDiamonds is a portfolio company of the venture firm Earlybird and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a quantum hardware and instrumentation company, it does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web presence and company identity.

providers.name: Quintessent
providers.description: Quintessent is a Goleta, California deep-tech photonics company developing quantum dot laser and optical interconnect technology to scale computing and AI infrastructure. The company builds quantum dot epitaxial wafer supply chains (in partnership with IQE) and optical connectivity solutions for AI optical interconnects, targeting the bandwidth and energy-efficiency bottlenecks of next-generation data centers. Backed by Sierra Ventures, Quintessent is a hardware and semiconductor company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation.

providers.name: Rcom
providers.description: Rcom (Reliance Communications, RCOM) is an Indian telecommunications and digital infrastructure company providing enterprise connectivity, voice, and data-center services. Its portfolio spans dedicated internet access and DDoS protection, IP transit, MPLS VPN, Ethernet and leased lines, cloud networking (Cloud X Fusion / Cloud X WAN), enterprise voice (E1 PRI, SIP trunk, IP Centrex), cloud telephony and hosted contact centers, toll-free and global access numbers, audio/web conferencing, colocation and managed data-center services, and global subsea cable networks via its Global Cloud Xchange subsidiary. The company surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; enrichment confirms an enterprise service business with customer and billing portals but no public developer program, API surface, or well-known discovery documents.

providers.name: Reach Labs
providers.description: Reach Labs (operating as Reach Power Inc.) is a wireless power transmission company that delivers electrical energy through the air without physical connections, describing its mission as "doing for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented approach combines energy-transmission hardware, a custom delivery algorithm, and adaptive software controls to beam power to devices across varying distances and conditions. The company targets three primary sectors: defense and intelligence (powering sensors, autonomous vehicles, and drones in remote environments), manufacturing and logistics (energizing robotics and IoT devices in industrial settings), and public safety (enabling continuous drone operations for first responders). Reach was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable metadata surface.

providers.name: Sagence AI
providers.description: Sagence AI is a semiconductor company building analog in-memory computing hardware for AI inference. Its "analog inference machine" combines deep subthreshold computing with multi-level flash memory cells to run large AI models at a fraction of the power and cost of conventional digital GPUs, targeting datacenter and edge workloads such as generative AI, recommendation systems, real-time defect detection, and video security. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company positions its technology against offerings like Nvidia's B200, claiming large gains in performance-per-watt and cost efficiency for AI inference. Sagence AI is a hardware/silicon company and does not currently publish a developer API, SDK, or public developer portal.

providers.name: Solestial
providers.description: Solestial is a space solar energy company developing space-stable silicon photovoltaics — radiation-hardened, ultrathin flexible silicon heterojunction solar cells and modules for spacecraft. Its products are the only solar products on the market that self-cure radiation damage at operating temperatures, offering competitive performance at lower cost than III-V multijunction solar. Solestial has flight heritage across multiple spacecraft and works with customers including NASA, Boeing, and the U.S. Space Force. This is a hardware and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Substrate
providers.description: Substrate is a semiconductor manufacturing company building America's next-generation chip foundry, with the stated mission of returning the United States to dominance in advanced semiconductor fabrication. Rather than designing chips, the company is inventing manufacturing technology intended to extend Moore's Law while lowering the cost of building state-of-the-art fabs and the wafers they produce. Substrate is a hard-tech / advanced-manufacturing venture backed by General Catalyst; it is a physical-infrastructure company and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio and enriched with the provider's public identity and security surface.

providers.name: The Exploration Company
providers.description: The Exploration Company GmbH is a European space transportation startup building reusable space vehicles "for humanity." Its flagship program, Nyx, is a reusable capsule designed to carry cargo and, eventually, crew between Earth and low Earth orbit destinations such as commercial space stations, featuring orbital propulsion, autonomous docking, and re-entry recovery. The company is also developing Storm, a high-thrust reusable rocket engine (up to 180 tons of thrust) built through European partnerships toward a globally competitive launcher. Backed by Balderton Capital and a certified B Corp, it markets itself as one of the fastest-growing space startups in the world. The company operates a marketing and careers web presence but publishes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time. Surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network with verified identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Tile
providers.description: Tile is a consumer-electronics company known for its Bluetooth tracker devices, used to locate everyday items such as keys, wallets, bags, and phones through a companion mobile app and a crowd-sourced Find network. Tile was acquired by Life360 in 2021; its former site thetileapp.com now 301-redirects to life360.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Tile publishes no public developer API — this profile captures its security posture (security.txt, a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program, and probed domain security).

providers.name: VXB Aerospace
providers.description: VXB Aerospace is an Australian space technology company founded in 2022 by Alexander Ryan, developing generative design software and Hall-effect plasma propulsion for the satellite market. Its platform automates the design, manufacturability analysis, multi-physics modeling and validation of complex aerospace hardware such as propulsion systems, antennas and satellite layouts, while its ZEPHYR-35 Hall-effect thruster (Argon/Krypton/Xenon) provides in-orbit mobility, refueling, servicing and de-orbiting. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Marvell Technology
providers.description: Marvell Technology, Inc. is a Fortune 500 fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company designs and develops data infrastructure semiconductor solutions including custom ASICs, data processing units, Ethernet controllers, optical and copper PHYs, switches, and storage controllers used in data centers, enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, automotive, and consumer markets. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Marvell. Public developer documentation is gated behind a customer support portal and is not openly accessible.

providers.name: Avnet
providers.description: Avnet is a global technology distributor and solutions provider that delivers electronic components, embedded solutions, and design and supply chain services to industrial and commercial customers.

providers.name: Helion Energy
providers.description: Helion Energy is an Everett, Washington fusion power company building commercial fusion electricity generators using a pulsed, magneto-inertial field-reversed configuration (FRC) approach burning deuterium and helium-3. Helion forms two FRC plasmas at opposite ends of its machine, accelerates them toward each other, merges them, and uses pulsed magnetic compression to drive them to fusion conditions; the expanding plasma pushes against the confining magnetic field and induces current directly back into the machine's capacitor bank via Faraday's Law, recapturing electricity without a steam cycle. Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, John Slough, Chris Pihl, and George Votroubek, Helion is chaired by Sam Altman and has progressed through seven generations of prototypes (IPA, Venti, Trenta, and most recently Polaris) on its way to commercial generators. Polaris, brought online in late 2024, is the company's seventh-generation machine and the first privately developed fusion device to demonstrate measurable deuterium-tritium fusion, reaching 150 million degrees Celsius in February 2026. In May 2023, Helion signed the world's first commercial fusion power purchase agreement, committing to deliver 50 MWe to Microsoft starting in 2028, with the Orion plant planned for the Malaga, Washington area; a subsequent agreement with Nucor targets a 500-MWe facility. Helion is funded by Sam Altman, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Nucor, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and others, with a reported $5.4B valuation as of early 2025. The company's revenue model is fusion electricity sales under long-term PPAs; Helion has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source software product, and its public GitHub organization (Helion-Energy) contains only forks of plasma-physics simulation tools (WarpX, FerroX, pyamrex, maestrowf).

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: MatX
providers.description: MatX is an AI-hardware company designing specialized semiconductors optimized for large language model workloads. Its flagship MatX One chip targets high-throughput, low-latency training, inference, and reinforcement learning for large dense and Mixture-of-Experts models, storing weights in SRAM to cut latency and reaching over 2,000 output tokens per second on large models. MatX is a hardware and research company with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity, research/blog output, open-source codebases, and domain-security posture. Backed by Jane Street, Spark Capital, and Situational Awareness LP.

providers.name: Moxion Power
providers.description: Moxion Power was a Richmond, California-based mobile battery energy storage (BESS) company founded in 2020 that designed, manufactured, and deployed large-scale mobile lithium-iron-phosphate battery units (the MP-75 and related platforms) intended to displace diesel generators across construction sites, film and television production, live events, utility work, and emergency response. The company built a 40,000 square-foot factory in Richmond, raised approximately $100 million in a Series B at a reported $1.5 billion valuation led by Tamarack Global with participation from Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund and Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, and signed a multi-year fleet partnership with Sunbelt Rentals. After delivering 400+ units it announced cessation of operations on July 29, 2024, laid off its entire workforce, and filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware in August 2024 with approximately $201,980 in cash on hand and estimated liabilities of $100M–$500M. In September–October 2024, Viridi Parente acquired Moxion's Richmond facility, battery inventory, intellectual property, patents, and the Sunbelt Rentals relationship through the bankruptcy auction for approximately $7 million. Moxion Power had no public developer API, SDK, or open source release; its GitHub organization (github.com/moxion-power) contains zero public repositories. This profile is preserved for historical reference.

providers.name: Qphox
providers.description: QphoX is a Delft, Netherlands-based quantum technology company founded in 2021 and spun out of Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). It develops quantum networking hardware to tackle the scaling challenges of quantum computing, centered on its Quantum Transducer, described as the first quantum interface between single optical and single microwave photons, enabling optical interconnects between superconducting quantum processors. Alongside the transducer, QphoX offers an Optical Control System for delivering RF signals into extreme cryogenic environments and a CryoSwitch Control Module for use with Radiall's cryogenic latching actuator. The company publishes open-source Python instrument-control libraries (QCoDeS drivers) on GitHub for operating its hardware. QphoX is backed by Speedinvest. QphoX exposes no public web API or developer portal.

providers.name: Unconventional AI
providers.description: Unconventional AI (unconv.ai) is rethinking the foundations of the computer to optimize energy efficiency for AI, working to bring biology-scale efficiency to artificial intelligence through analog, dynamical-system hardware co-evolved with neural software. Founded by experts in AI systems, analog circuits, computing theory, and neuroscience, and backed by Felicis, the company publishes research including the Un-0 image-generation model built on coupled Kuramoto oscillators and an instruction set architecture for dynamical-system hardware, but does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Unconventional AI
providers.description: Unconventional AI is rethinking the foundations of compute to bring biology-scale energy efficiency to AI. The company researches dynamical systems such as coupled Kuramoto oscillators as a computing substrate that maps onto analog and physical hardware, pointing toward on the order of 1000x lower energy for AI than today's digital accelerators. Its open-source Un-0 reference implementation generates images by integrating the phase dynamics of coupled oscillators. Backed by DCVC, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Lux Capital, and Wing Venture Capital. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: atantares
providers.description: Atantares (芯宿科技) is a Chinese synthetic-biology company based in Suzhou Industrial Park that builds "silicon-based biology" — semiconductor-driven biotechnology. Its chip-based, high-throughput platform (the EcoSyn synthesizer and ECHOS MicroArray, using electrochemical oligonucleotide synthesis on CMOS/MEMS microelectrode arrays) drives low-cost, high-fidelity DNA synthesis and is expanding into RNA and protein synthesis and detection. Research-service offerings include primer/oligo synthesis, gene synthesis, gene sequencing, cloning and mutagenesis, strain-library preparation, and gene editing, built on an in-house full-workflow automation, sequence-analysis, and order-management platform. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Bellabeat
providers.description: Bellabeat is a femtech and women's wellness technology company founded in 2014 by Urska Srsen and Sandro Mur, headquartered in San Francisco, California. It designs health-tracking wearables and connected devices aimed at women, including the Leaf and Ivy wellness jewelry trackers, the Time hybrid smartwatch, and the Spring smart water bottle, paired with the Bellabeat mobile app that tracks activity, sleep, stress, meditation, menstrual cycle, and overall wellness. Bellabeat operates as a direct-to-consumer wellness brand; it does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and network provenance rather than API artifacts. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched here.

providers.name: Evonetix
providers.description: Evonetix is a Cambridge, UK deep-technology company developing a benchtop DNA synthesis platform built on semiconductor technology. Its core innovation is a silicon chip carrying thousands of independently thermally-controlled reaction sites, allowing many DNA strands to be synthesised in parallel with per-site temperature control, in-process error detection and correction, and assembly of high-fidelity genes at the desktop. The company's goal is to give synthetic biology, life-science, and drug-discovery researchers accurate, on-demand access to synthetic DNA without relying on centralised outsourced gene foundries. Evonetix was surfaced as a portfolio company of the deep-tech venture firm DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK, and its primary web domain (evonetix.com) resolves to a suspended-account placeholder page.

providers.name: Mogassam
providers.description: Mogassam is a digital dentistry company building all-in-one dental 3D printing hardware and software for chairside, single-visit treatment. Its products include the DentCase automated all-in-one 3D printer with integrated CAM, automatic washing, and post-curing, the Microdent 1 Pro printer, and the DentPrint dental 3D printing software, used to produce dentures, dental models, surgical guides, and provisional and permanent restorations. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: NVision Imaging Technologies
providers.description: NVision Imaging Technologies (now operating as NVision Quantum Technologies) is a deep-tech healthcare company that engineers quantum technology at the molecular level. Its flagship POLARIS platform delivers quantum-enhanced MRI, boosting the magnetic signal of engineered sugar molecules by over 10,000x to image disease metabolism in real time, and its PIQC platform is a quantum-computing architecture built on molecular quantum nodes native to photonic chips. The company is backed by Playground Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface; this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Orthocon
providers.description: Orthocon, now operating as Abyrx, is a surgical-therapeutics medical device company that has built a materials-science platform focused on therapeutic devices used during surgical procedures. Its portfolio centers on resorbable and hemostatic bone putties for orthopedic, trauma, spine, sports medicine, cranial, maxillofacial, and cardiothoracic applications, including AHBP (water-soluble hemostatic bone putty), the HemaSorb family (HemaSorb, HemaSorb Apply, HemaSorb Plus with HA/beta-TCP), and MONTAGE settable resorbable bone putty. The company sells directly to surgeons, hospitals, and distributors and does not operate a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or programmatic developer surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched via the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Petcube
providers.description: Petcube is a pet-technology company (a Y Combinator alum) that makes interactive Wi-Fi pet cameras and a companion mobile app for remote pet care. Its consumer hardware line includes the Petcube Cam, Bites treat-dispensing camera, and Play laser camera, offering HD video, night vision, two-way audio, motion and sound alerts, and app-controlled treat tossing and play. Petcube also sells the Care subscription (cloud video history, extended alerts) and Online Vet / Emergency Fund telehealth services. As of this enrichment pass Petcube exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented integration surface — the primary interface is the consumer iOS/Android app tied to its private cloud backend. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Shape Shapescale
providers.description: Shapescale is a consumer body-scanning company that builds ShapeScale, a home 3D body scanner and companion mobile app. The device slowly rotates around a standing user, captures a photorealistic 3D model of the body, and measures body composition, weight, and circumference metrics so users can track fitness and body changes over time. Shapescale is a Y Combinator portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer product website but no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: VINNO
providers.description: VINNO Corporation (飞依诺科技股份有限公司) is a Chinese medical device manufacturer, headquartered in Suzhou, that develops and produces digital color ultrasound (Doppler) imaging systems — cart-based, portable, and handheld/pocket devices — for clinical diagnostics and research. Product lines include the ULTIMUS and VINNO R-series ultrasound platforms plus Stream-series CPAP respiratory devices, built on proprietary soft beamforming and ultra-high-resolution micro-vascular imaging technology, with remote-diagnostic center and support services across 50+ countries. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. As of enrichment the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface (medical-device hardware manufacturer).

providers.name: Alphion
providers.description: Alphion Corporation is a broadband access equipment manufacturer that develops fiber-optic and wireless networking solutions for network operators, enterprises, and community networks. Founded in 2000 and based in Princeton Junction, New Jersey, the company builds GPON-based fiber-to-the-x (FTTx/FTTH) access systems, optical network terminals (AONT/ONT), and secure GigaWi-Fi broadband access products that deliver voice, data, video, and wireless services over passive optical networks. Alphion is a photonics and telecommunications hardware provider; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It does not currently publish a developer portal, public API, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Amca
providers.description: Amca (Advanced Manufacturing Company of America) is an El Segundo, California aerospace and defense manufacturer rebuilding America's industrial base by acquiring specialized component suppliers and expanding competition and capacity for critical parts — actuators, switches, hydraulics, pressure sensors, power electronics, and flight-control electronics. Founded in 2024 by Eli Giovanetti and Jai Malik, Amca combines design, testing, and production into a single RAPID platform across a network of AS9100D-certified factories (Electro-Mech Components, Electrocube, Aerospace Control Products, Payne Magnetics, Cal-Draulics, BC Power Systems), and serves nearly every major aerospace and defense prime and Tier 1 supplier — Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Textron, BAE Systems, and the Defense Logistics Agency. It is a hardware manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Apollo Atomics Inc
providers.description: Apollo Atomics is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26) nuclear technology company building compact, power-dense pressurized water reactors for electricity generation, industrial process heat, and data-center power. Founded by Assil Halimi and Drew Walker and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the company modifies the steam generator of proven pressurized water reactor technology to shrink the plant by roughly an order of magnitude without sacrificing power output, turning a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that can ship on a truck. Apollo has announced a research collaboration with MIT's Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering to validate its reactor design and has submitted a regulatory engagement plan to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, targeting a construction permit application in 2028. This is a hardware/energy company with no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Atlas Motion Systems
providers.description: Atlas Motion Systems (atlasmotion.com) designs and builds brushless DC (BLDC) motors and actuators for defense and robotics applications, engineered around a customer's specific program and manufactured at scale. The public web presence is a single-page marketing site (hero plus a contact page); it is a hardware company that does not publish a developer portal, public API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. This profile was seeded as a Homebrew-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable identity and live domain-security probe data only. Enrichment found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: FIMI Technology
providers.description: FIMI Technology Ltd. (Beijing FIMI Technology Co., Ltd. / Shenzhen FIMI Robot Technology Co., Ltd.) is a consumer aerial-imaging hardware manufacturer founded in May 2014 as a member of the Xiaomi ecosystem. FIMI designs and sells affordable camera drones, handheld gimbal cameras, and smartphone gimbals, with a product lineup that includes the X8 series (X8 SE, X8 Pro, X8 Tele, X8T enterprise), the compact Mini 3, the Manta VTOL fixed-wing drone, and the PALM series gimbal cameras. The company holds hundreds of patents across flight control, wireless transmission links, mechatronic design, gimbal image-stabilization, and computer vision. FIMI is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. This is a consumer-electronics company with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Ideal Power Converters
providers.description: Ideal Power Inc. (NASDAQ: IPWR), formerly Ideal Power Converters, is an Austin, Texas power semiconductor company developing bidirectional bipolar junction transistor (B-TRAN) technology for ultra-low conduction losses, bidirectional current flow, and fast fault protection and switching. Its product portfolio includes B-TRAN power switches, SymCool power modules, and B-TRAN Known Good Die, targeting data centers, energy storage systems, power grids, solid-state circuit breakers, and EV charging infrastructure. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; the company publishes a corporate and investor web presence but no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Inviscid AI
providers.description: Inviscid AI is a San Francisco-based startup (Y Combinator W2026) building physics-informed AI for real-time cooling and airflow simulation of buildings and industrial facilities. Its platform combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with physics-informed neural networks to run thermal digital twins up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD, ingesting live data from building management systems, meters, and IoT sensors to autonomously recommend HVAC setpoints and optimize airflow. Target facilities include data centers, offices, hospitals, and cold storage, where the company claims 30%+ energy savings and sub-90-day ROI. As of mid-2026 Inviscid AI is a pre-product-launch company with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending an external API.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: Mauna Kea Semiconductors
providers.description: Mauna Kea Semiconductors (mk-semi.com) is a Silicon Valley-based fabless semiconductor company founded by industry veterans to develop what it describes as the world's lowest-power Ultra-Wideband (UWB) solution for high precision location and direction-finding applications. Its UWB chips, modules, and integrated System-on-Chip solutions target smartphones, wearables, IoT devices, and automotive use cases, combining digital and analog/mixed-signal design expertise. Headquartered in Cupertino, California, with engineering operations in Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen, the company is led by CEO Dr. Yifeng Zhang and is backed by Qiming. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming; it is a hardware/silicon vendor with no public API or developer surface at this time (documentation, blog, and careers pages are marked "Coming Soon").

providers.name: MOLG
providers.description: MOLG (molg.ai) is a circular manufacturing company tackling electronic waste. It operates autonomous robotic microfactories that disassemble complex devices like laptops and servers to recover components and materials for reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. MOLG also partners with manufacturers on design-for-circularity (modular snap/press-fit/latch assembly instead of screws and adhesives) and offers OriginMark, a traceability platform for tracking devices, components, and materials across their lifecycle to calculate embodied carbon and supply-chain transparency. As of this enrichment pass MOLG publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Monumental
providers.description: Monumental builds autonomous construction robots and the software that runs them. Its robots lay bricks and blockwork on real building sites, coordinated by Monumental's software platform (Atrium) and fleet operations (Fleet). The venture-backed company operates across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and has raised multiple funding rounds (including a reported $32M raise and Series B rounds in the US and UK). Monumental was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation - this record captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Occipital
providers.description: Occipital is a computer-vision and 3D-scanning company known for the Structure Sensor depth camera and the Canvas home-scanning app, built on more than fifteen years of spatial-computing expertise. The Canvas product line (formerly canvas.io) now operates as Twindo, a spatial intelligence platform that turns iPhone/iPad LiDAR scans, floor plans, and point clouds into accurate, editable CAD and BIM files for architecture, interior design, construction, remodeling, multifamily residential, retail, hospitality, and fire-safety professionals. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes end-user scanning apps, a web viewer, and a support center, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Periodic
providers.description: Periodic (Periodic Labs) is an AI research company building "AI scientists" paired with autonomous laboratories to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences, with an early focus on materials science and higher-temperature superconductors. Their systems hypothesize, run physical experiments, and learn from the results, and they partner with industry to optimize experimental processes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and Felicis, the company is at an early stage and does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or developer platform. This profile records that honest result; it is not penalized for having no API surface.

providers.name: Pixcel
providers.description: PIXCEL Inc. is an early-stage deep-tech startup developing cutting-edge silicon photonics solutions and photonic integrated circuits (PICs) for optical communications and related systems. Based in Matawan, NJ, and co-founded by silicon photonics veteran Long Chen (previously at Cisco Systems and Acacia Communications), the company designs passive and active photonic components and collaborates with foundry partners to optimize process design kits (PDKs). PIXCEL is a hardware and semiconductor company with no public API, developer portal, or software product surface at this time; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. This profile reflects an enrichment pass that confirmed there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Pluribus Networks
providers.description: Pluribus Networks was a software-defined networking (SDN) and open-networking vendor known for its NetVisor ONE network operating system (NVOS), the Adaptive Cloud Fabric controllerless SDN fabric, the UNUM management/analytics platform, and the Freedom 9000 series switches. The company was acquired by Arista Networks in 2022; the pluribusnetworks.com domain now redirects to Arista's Pluribus support resources, and the core Pluribus product line (NVOS, UNUM, Freedom 9000) has since been moved to End-of-Sale / End-of-Life. No independent Pluribus developer portal, public REST API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK is published; support and technical documentation are provided through the Arista customer portal. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and Menlo Ventures.

providers.name: Soma Energy
providers.description: Soma Energy is an AI-powered energy intelligence platform that optimizes how power is produced, stored, and consumed. Founded by former Amazon and technology leaders, it coordinates power generation, battery storage, and large energy consumers such as data centers. Its Intelligence Platform combines three products: AI Trader, which automates energy procurement, hedging, and dispatch for independent power producers (IPPs); BESS Dispatcher, which manages battery energy storage systems; and Load Optimizer, which coordinates data-center workloads with grid conditions to cut energy costs and turn facilities into flexible grid assets. Soma Energy is an early-stage company backed by Uncork Capital. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, developer platform, or documentation.

providers.name: Team Wildfire
providers.description: Team Wildfire develops jet engine-enabled fire suppression technology built to prevent catastrophic wildfire losses. Its mobile units, the "Hurricane" and "Storm Cell", apply fire retardant at scale to deny ground to advancing wildfires. The company offers fireground services, evacuation route hardening, asset protection, prescribed fire containment, and military base protection. Team Wildfire is a physical hardware and services company backed by Techstars; it publishes a marketing and services website but no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals available for a non-API company.

providers.name: AICE
providers.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aquantia
providers.description: Aquantia Corporation was a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in San Jose, California, that designed and marketed multi-gigabit Ethernet connectivity — AQtion client network controllers, Atlantic controllers, and multi-gig PHY transceivers for enterprise, data center, automotive, and consumer networking. Aquantia was acquired by Marvell Technology in 2019; the aquantia.com domain now redirects to marvell.com. It operated no public HTTP/developer API or developer portal — its published developer surface is silicon: Linux kernel and DPDK "Atlantic" NIC drivers, firmware, and tooling in the github.com/Aquantia organization. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-lead stub; there is no API to enrich.

providers.name: Atom Computing
providers.description: Atom Computing is a Berkeley, California neutral-atom quantum computing company building large-scale, gate-based quantum computers using optically-trapped Ytterbium-171 nuclear-spin qubits. Founded in 2018 by Ben Bloom, the company became the first in the industry to exceed 1,000 qubits in a gate-based quantum computer with its second-generation platform in October 2023 (1,180 qubits across 1,225 sites). Its current commercial product, AC1000, is a universal gate-based, on-premises quantum computing system with 1,200+ physical qubits, all-to-all connectivity, mid-circuit measurement with qubit reuse and reset, real-time conditional branching, and better-than-threshold fidelities (>99.9% single-qubit, >99.6% two-qubit, >99.8% SPAM). The platform is programmable via OpenQASM and QIR (Quantum Intermediate Representation) and ships with a 20-qubit classical emulator. In January 2025 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced an on-premises 50-logical-qubit system (Magne), with additional strategic collaborations across Cisco (networked/distributed quantum, March 2026), NVIDIA NVQLink integration (March 2026), and a Letter of Intent for $100M from the U.S. Department of Commerce (May 2026). The commercial model centers on enterprise and national-lab on-premises system sales and partnerships; there is no public cloud API or self-serve developer portal — programmatic access is via the standard OpenQASM/QIR toolchains targeting customer-deployed AC1000 hardware.

providers.name: Augtera Networks
providers.description: Augtera Networks is an AI-native networking (Network AIOps) company founded in 2016 and based in Palo Alto, California. Its Network AI platform ingests telemetry from network devices, applies machine-learning anomaly detection (including gray failures), eliminates noise, performs incident root-cause identification, noiseless ticket creation, and auto-mitigation/remediation for data-center and enterprise networks. The platform exposed a Topology REST API for device discovery/lifecycle and DevOps/ITSM integration. Augtera was acquired by NVIDIA in December 2024 and folded into the NVIDIA Spectrum-X networking portfolio; its standalone augtera.com site now 301-redirects to nvidia.com, so no independent public developer/API surface remains. Added to the API Evangelist network as a bain-capital-ventures portfolio lead.

providers.name: Bouffalo Lab
providers.description: Bouffalo Lab (博流智能) is a fabless chip design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nanjing, China, focused on ultra-low-power AIoT (AI + IoT) and edge-computing system chips. Its product line centers on RISC-V based microcontrollers with integrated wireless connectivity — the BL602/BL604 (Wi-Fi 2.4G + BLE 5.0), BL702/BL704/BL706 (Zigbee 3.0 + BLE 5.0), BL606P (quad-mode dual-core Wi-Fi/BT/BLE/Zigbee), and the BL616/BL618 and BL808 families — combining wireless radios, audio/video processing, and on-device AI algorithms. The company ships the open-source BouffaloSDK (a merge of bl_mcu_sdk and bl_iot_sdk) under Apache 2.0 through its public GitHub organization, along with hardware abstraction drivers, Matter/Thread support, and NuttX RTOS ports. Bouffalo Lab is a hardware/firmware provider rather than a web-API provider; it exposes no public HTTP/REST developer API, so the enrichment pipeline captures its developer surface (GitHub SDK org) and domain security posture. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Cuspai
providers.description: CuspAI is a Cambridge, UK artificial intelligence company, founded in 2024, building generative AI for materials discovery. Its platform lets users specify desired physical and chemical properties — such as selective CO2 binding — and then generates, evaluates, and optimizes candidate molecular and material structures for applications spanning carbon capture, energy storage, catalysis, water purification, electric vehicles, and healthcare. CuspAI has raised roughly $130M (a $30M seed and a $100M Series A in September 2025) from investors including Northzone and Prosus Ventures, and maintains open-source scientific computing tooling on GitHub. As of mid-2026 the company operates a placeholder marketing site with no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Cypress
providers.description: Cypress Semiconductor Corporation was a San Jose, California semiconductor company founded in 1982, and an early Mayfield venture investment. It designed and manufactured mixed-signal, embedded, and connectivity silicon — most notably the PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth wireless combos, USB controllers (EZ-USB), NOR flash and SRAM memory, and automotive Traveo microcontrollers — supported by the ModusToolbox and PSoC Creator developer tooling and the Cypress Developer Community. Infineon Technologies AG acquired Cypress in April 2020 for approximately 9.4 billion dollars; the business, its developer community, and its GitHub repositories have since been folded into Infineon. cypress.com now redirects to infineon.com and the developer resources live at community.infineon.com. Cypress shipped hardware SDKs and embedded toolchains rather than a public web/REST API, so there is no independent HTTP API surface to catalog for this entity — this profile documents it as a historical, acquired provider.

providers.name: Harman International
providers.description: Harman International, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics, is a global leader in connected technologies for automotive, consumer, and enterprise markets, including connected car systems, audio products, professional solutions, and connected services. Harman does not currently publish a public developer portal or open APIs; integrations with Harman platforms (such as Ignite, Ready Connect, and audio brands like JBL, Harman Kardon, and AKG) are typically delivered through commercial partnerships and OEM agreements.

providers.name: INDEX Robotics
providers.description: INDEX Robotics is a South Korean humanoid robotics startup based in Seongnam (Bundang) building high-precision actuators and upper-body humanoid robots for high-mix, low-volume industrial work. Its core products are the IA Series, a family of high-precision actuators purpose-built for humanoid joints, and INDEX01, a compact upper-body humanoid prototype that deliberately foregoes a mobile base so it can slot into constrained factory workspaces for logistics handling, machining support, and precision assembly. The company treats joint precision, responsiveness under sustained repetitive motion, and long-run performance consistency as the core unsolved problems in humanoid commercialization. In February 2026 INDEX Robotics closed a $1M (KRW 1.5B) seed round led by Futureplay with Bass Ventures and 500 Global co-investing. This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Jewelbots
providers.description: Jewelbots makes smart, codable friendship bracelets designed to teach kids (primarily tween girls) to code. The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

providers.name: Misfit
providers.description: Misfit is a consumer wearables brand — fitness trackers and smartwatches such as the Misfit Shine, Flash, Ray and Vapor — founded in 2011 by Sonny Vu, John Sculley and Sridhar Iyengar and backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, GGV Capital and Xiaomi before being acquired by Fossil Group in 2015. Misfit ran a developer program (the Misfit Cloud API, Device SDK and Scientific Library) at build.misfit.com with 30+ launch partners. Fossil discontinued the Misfit backend, Cloud API and companion app in spring 2023, so the hosted API and all misfit.com domains are now unreachable. The only surviving developer surface is the official Misfit-Developers GitHub organization and its unmaintained iOS SDKs on CocoaPods.

providers.name: NVE Corporation
providers.description: NVE Corporation (nve.com, NASDAQ: NVEC) is a leader in the practical commercialization of spintronics, a nanotechnology that relies on electron spin rather than electron charge to acquire, store, and transmit information. NVE designs and manufactures spintronic GMR and TMR magnetic sensors (analog, angle/rotation, current, gear-tooth, and medical sensors), digital signal isolators (CAN, RS-422/485, PLC, battery-management, and power interfaces), and power-management ICs. Its developer surface is hardware-oriented: PDF datasheets, application notes, reference designs, magnetic-field calculators/web apps, a YouTube channel, and Arduino/embedded sample code on GitHub. NVE publishes no software/web API, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or developer API platform.

providers.name: onsemi
providers.description: ON Semiconductor (now branded as onsemi) is a global supplier of semiconductor-based solutions for power efficiency, image sensing, and signal processing in automotive, industrial, and other applications. No public APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: Planqc
providers.description: planqc GmbH is a German quantum computing company building neutral-atom quantum computers, using individual atoms trapped in optical lattices as qubits on what it describes as the most promising path to fault-tolerant, scalable systems. Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, the company delivers full-stack quantum computing — hardware, control software, and applications — including its MAQCS (Multicore Atomic Quantum Computing System) line for enterprise and scientific customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and financial services. planqc operates from Garching and Ulm in Germany and Innsbruck in Austria, and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic cloud-access surface; access is arranged directly through the company. This profile is a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network, enriched with verified public identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Primesense
providers.description: PrimeSense was an Israeli fabless semiconductor and 3D-sensing company, best known for co-developing the depth-sensing technology behind Microsoft's Kinect and for sponsoring the open-source OpenNI (Open Natural Interaction) framework and its NiTE middleware for skeleton tracking and gesture recognition. The company shipped the PrimeSensor reference design and PS1080 system-on-chip for structured-light depth cameras. Apple acquired PrimeSense in November 2013 for roughly $360M; the OpenNI project and openni.org were subsequently wound down (openni.org now redirects to apple.com) and the company's developer program, website, and API/docs hosts are no longer online. Only legacy Apache-2.0 source repositories (the OpenNI sensor driver and NiTE controls) remain public on GitHub. There is no live web/REST API surface for PrimeSense.

providers.name: PsiQuantum
providers.description: PsiQuantum is a Palo Alto, California photonic quantum computing company founded in 2016 by Jeremy O'Brien, Terry Rudolph, Pete Shadbolt, and Mark Thompson, building utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers based on single-photon qubits at telecom wavelength. Its Omega chipset — a silicon photonic system integrating on-chip single-photon sources, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, barium-titanate optical switches, and low-loss fiber couplers — is manufactured on 300mm wafers at GlobalFoundries' flagship fab in Malta, NY, leveraging mature semiconductor processes rather than exotic cryogenic fabrication. The company is constructing two utility- scale, million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum computing sites: one at Moreton Bay, Queensland, Australia (in partnership with the Australian and Queensland governments) and one at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago, Illinois (with additional R&D at PsiLabs in Daresbury, UK and assembly at PsiFactory in Milpitas, CA). PsiQuantum exposes a developer surface aimed at fault-tolerant quantum algorithm researchers: Construct, an enterprise platform for FTQC algorithm development, resource analysis, and training; Circuit Designer, a free web tool for prototyping and visualizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits; Circuit Hub, a shared library of `.circuit` files; and two open-source Python projects on GitHub — Bartiq, a symbolic quantum resource estimator that compiles subroutine-level costs to global T-gate, Toffoli, qubit, and circuit-volume estimates, and QREF, an open JSON-Schema-based format for representing quantum algorithms as hierarchical DAGs with a Pydantic validation library and a `qref-render` visualization tool. NVIDIA's CUDA-Q is integrated into Construct for accelerated simulation. PsiQuantum does not currently publish a commercial cloud-access REST API, OpenAPI specification, or a general-purpose quantum-execution SDK comparable to those of gate-model quantum cloud providers — its public developer artifacts are confined to FTQC resource-estimation tooling and algorithm-design surfaces — and there is no public pricing or self-serve tier for the underlying quantum hardware.

providers.name: StratoScale
providers.description: Stratoscale was an Israeli software-defined data center company founded in 2013 in Herzliya by Ariel Maislos and backed by Battery Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Intel Capital, Cisco, Qualcomm Ventures and SanDisk ($70M raised). Its flagship product, Stratoscale Symphony (announced December 2015), delivered AWS-compatible cloud infrastructure on commodity x86 hardware — an API-driven, hyperconverged platform exposing EC2-, S3-, EBS-, EFS-, RDS-, ELB- and EMR-compatible services plus Kubernetes and Docker, alongside OpenStack and vCenter compatibility for hybrid and multi-cloud operations. The company ceased operations at the end of 2019 due to insufficient funding; there is no longer a live developer portal, documentation site, or reachable API surface. Its public GitHub organization (open-source Go/go-swagger tooling) remains available.

providers.name: Sygaldry
providers.description: Sygaldry Technologies builds quantum-accelerated AI servers — augmenting classical data-center infrastructure with quantum processors purpose-built for AI to deliver exponential speedups on specific training and inference tasks. Founded in 2024 in Ann Arbor, Michigan by Chad Rigetti (founder of Rigetti Computing), Idalia Friedson, and Michael Keiser, the company combines multiple qubit types within a single fault-tolerant architecture to accelerate model training, fine-tuning, and token generation while cutting compute cost and energy use. A Y Combinator Spring 2025 company, Sygaldry has raised $139M ($34M seed led by Initialized Capital and a $105M Series A led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, with Bloomberg Beta among its investors). Sygaldry currently publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network discovery.

providers.name: Tabular
providers.description: Tabular was an independent, managed cloud data platform and storage engine built on Apache Iceberg, founded in 2021 by Ryan Blue, Daniel Weeks, and Jason Reid — two of the original creators of Apache Iceberg and a former head of Data Engineering at Netflix. Its central product was a managed Iceberg catalog exposed over the open Apache Iceberg REST Catalog protocol (an OpenAPI-defined common API), giving any compute engine vendor-neutral access to a single copy of data. Databricks agreed to acquire Tabular in June 2024 and closed the deal that month; the founders joined Databricks and the standalone product was wound down. As of this enrichment pass the tabular.io domain no longer resolves and the tabular-io GitHub organization has no public repositories, so there is no live first-party API surface to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Upverter
providers.description: Upverter is a browser-based, collaborative electronic design automation (EDA) platform for schematic capture and PCB layout, founded in Toronto in 2010 (Y Combinator W11) and acquired by Altium in 2017. Surfaced as a Version One Ventures portfolio company. As of the July 2026 enrichment probe the upverter.com platform returns HTTP 502 on every path, its docs/blog/status subdomains no longer resolve, and no public API surface remains; the GitHub organization is dormant since 2019.

providers.name: Vaire Computing
providers.description: Vaire Computing is a deep-tech semiconductor startup building reversible computing chips for near-zero energy computing. Its reversible logic gates recover and recycle the energy of computation instead of dissipating it as heat, aiming to decouple energy consumption from growth in computing power. The company was co-founded by Rodolfo Rosini (CEO) and Dr Hannah Earley (CTO), is backed by Seedcamp, 7percent Ventures, and Lifeline Ventures, and publishes technology and software whitepapers. Vaire currently publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Voltron Data
