providers.description: Voltron Data is a Mountain View-based data infrastructure company (founded 2021) behind Theseus, a GPU-accelerated, composable distributed SQL query engine for petabyte-scale analytics and AI pipelines, distributed embedded through partners rather than as a self-serve public API. The company is a major steward of the open-source composable data stack — Apache Arrow, Ibis, Substrait, Arrow Flight SQL, and ADBC — acquired Claypot AI in January 2024, and is backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Walden Catalyst, with an Accenture investment in 2025. As of 2026-07-21 the company website (voltrondata.com) is unreachable — the domain is registered but its DNS zone is lame-delegated — leaving the GitHub organization as the live public surface; no public API, SDK packages, or developer portal are published.

providers.name: XING Mobility
providers.description: XING Mobility (行競科技) is a Taiwan-based battery technology company building immersion-cooled lithium battery systems under the IMMERSIO brand, including cell-to-pack (CTP) battery platforms, battery backup units (BBU) for AI data centers, and the automotive-grade XBE energy storage series, serving electric mobility, energy storage (ESS), marine, and data center markets from its Taoyuan City headquarters. A 500 Global portfolio company, XING Mobility publishes no public developer API or API documentation as of July 2026.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Alsym Energy
providers.description: Alsym Energy is a Malden, Massachusetts battery technology company founded in 2015 by Mukesh Chatter, Rahul Mukherjee, and Kripa Varanasi to develop low-cost, high-performance rechargeable batteries that are free of lithium and cobalt. Its Na-Series is a line of non-flammable, non-toxic sodium-ion batteries aimed at grid and utility-scale energy storage, data-center backup, and industrial applications where safety and supply-chain resilience matter. The company uses a proprietary AI/computational-materials platform to accelerate battery chemistry development, and has raised roughly $111M+ including a $78M round in 2024 led by Tata Limited and General Catalyst. Alsym is a hardware/energy-infrastructure manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Altair Semiconductor
providers.description: Altair Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power, highly integrated cellular IoT chipsets. Its core products are the ALT1250 (a dual-mode LTE-M / NB-IoT modem and SoC with integrated iSIM, MCU and GNSS) and the ALT1350 (a next-generation 5G LPWA SoC that combines LTE-M/NB-IoT, unlicensed-spectrum and satellite NTN connectivity), used in smart meters, asset trackers, wearables, sensors and vehicle telematics. Altair was acquired by Sony in 2016, operated as Sony's cellular IoT unit, and in 2026 was spun back out as an independent company with $50M in funding led by Pitango. This is a hardware/semiconductor provider: it ships chipsets, evaluation kits and datasheets rather than a public developer API, so it carries no OpenAPI, SDK, MCP or developer-portal surface to enrich.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Architect Labs
providers.description: Architect Labs is an AI lab building an AI system that explores, designs, and provably verifies custom silicon for the world's most demanding AI and compute workloads. The company is developing a platform that automates the chip-design and verification workflow, aiming to let AI model developers, robotics startups, and neocloud operators generate and verify custom chips without deep hardware-engineering expertise. Architect Labs raised a $24M seed round led by Kindred Ventures, with participation from investors including Aravind Srinivas and Lukasz Kaiser, and is scheduled to appear at DAC 2026. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site (about, blog, careers) but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Arlo Industries
providers.description: Arlo Industries is a San Francisco defense hardware company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building a passive sensing network for detecting and tracking drones and aerial threats without traditional radar. Its product, Mentat, uses a distributed mesh architecture of low-cost sensors that cooperatively detect and track targets in 3D while remaining invisible to the threats they monitor. The company frames its approach around "asymmetric economics" — sensor deployment cost grows linearly while tracking accuracy grows exponentially — making the system more scalable than conventional radar installations. Arlo has demonstrated its technology with Ukrainian military operators on active frontlines and maintains partnerships across the US, Ukraine, and Northern Europe. As an early-stage hardware startup it publishes no public API, developer program, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Aspinity
providers.description: Aspinity is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania semiconductor company that develops analog machine learning (AnalogML) technology combining ultra-low-power analog signal processing with machine learning for always-on, battery-operated edge AI event detection and classification. Its analogML processors the AML100 and next-generation AML200 deliver TOPS-level inference in a microwatt power footprint, targeting automotive vehicle-security monitoring, smart-home sensing such as glass-break and water-leak detection, and IoT applications including voice and keyword detection and vibration monitoring. Aspinity is a hardware and semiconductor provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Attotude
providers.description: AttoTude is a semiconductor and data-center infrastructure company building the first wired terahertz (THz) interconnect for AI and hyperscale networking. Its platform pairs the AttoEngine, an ASIC-based THz radio built on standard CMOS manufacturing, with AttoWire, a low-loss dielectric waveguide that carries 200/400/800 Gbit/s per lane over reaches up to roughly 40 meters, delivering the bandwidth density of optics without the cost, power, and complexity of photonics. Founded to relieve the interconnect bottleneck in everything-to-everything AI clusters, the company has raised roughly $143M across seed, Series A, Series B, and Series C rounds. This is a hardware company with no public API, developer portal, or SDK; the profile below is enriched only with the identity and domain-security facts the pipeline could verify.

providers.name: Cambrio
providers.description: Cambrio is a manufacturing software company, now a Sandvik-owned brand, that develops CAD/CAM software for CNC programming and digital manufacturing. Its portfolio spans GibbsCAM for CNC milling and turning, SigmaNEST for nesting and material optimization, and Cimatron for integrated tooling and mold design. Cambrio serves the automotive, aerospace, medical, electronics, and general manufacturing industries. It was a Battery Ventures portfolio company before being acquired by Sandvik AB in 2021. Cambrio is desktop/on-premises manufacturing software and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Colony Capital (DigitalBridge Group)
providers.description: Colony Capital was a diversified real estate and hospitality investment firm founded by Tom Barrack in 1991. In June 2021 the company rebranded as DigitalBridge Group, Inc. (NYSE: DBRG) — completing a multi-year pivot from traditional real estate to pure-play digital infrastructure investing. The Boca Raton, FL-based alternative asset manager now operates exclusively across five digital infrastructure categories: data centers, macro cell towers, fiber networks, small cells, and edge infrastructure. DigitalBridge manages approximately $119B in assets across 45+ portfolio companies including Vantage Data Centers, DataBank, Switch, Vertical Bridge, Zayo Group, GD Towers, Boingo Wireless, AtlasEdge, Scala Data Centers, Yondr Group, and ExteNet Systems. In December 2025 SoftBank Group announced a definitive agreement to acquire DigitalBridge for approximately $4 billion, with the deal expected to close in the second half of 2026. DigitalBridge itself publishes no developer API, SDK, or public OpenAPI surface — it is a holding company whose programmable surface lives inside its individual portfolio companies (e.g., Zayo, DataBank, Switch), each of which is profiled separately in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Constelli
providers.description: Constelli (Constelli Signals Private Limited) is a Hyderabad, India based defence and aerospace signal-processing company founded in 2017 by Satya Gopal Panigrahi and Avinash Chenreddy. It designs and manufactures radar systems, radar target and echo simulators, deployable drone-based radar payloads, high-performance radar processors, and IRIG-standard digital telemetry receivers for ground, onboard, and satellite telemetry. Its products serve electronic warfare and defence R&D programs globally, including India's Ministry of Defence and DRDO. Constelli raised a $20M Series A led by General Catalyst (with Pravega Ventures and 360 One). It is a hardware/systems company and does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Daivin
providers.description: DAIVIN! is a deep-tech hardware company (Y Combinator Winter 2026, based in San Francisco and Finland) building tankless diving technology. Its core product, SPRING, is marketed as the "world's first tankless diving technology": instead of carrying heavy pressurized oxygen tanks, a diver wears a lightweight vest of electrolyzers and a battery belt that use electricity to split water on demand into breathable oxygen (O2) and hydrogen (H2), targeting depths up to 200 meters / 650 ft. Founder Leo Kankkunen frames breathing as "fundamentally an energy problem," and the company envisions applications beyond recreational and professional diving across space exploration, high-altitude rescue, hospitals, and aircraft. Added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital portfolio lead surfaced via y-combinator. Daivin runs a conceptual marketing website (Wix) and a news blog; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or other machine-readable developer surface, so no API artifacts apply to this provider.

providers.name: EdgeQ
providers.description: EdgeQ is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, building a converged "Base Station-on-a-Chip" that integrates 5G, 6G, non-terrestrial network (NTN), custom waveform, CPU, and antenna-controller functions into a single software-defined silicon platform. Its programmable baseband targets small cells, private enterprise 5G, open RAN, satellite (LEO/MEO) communications, and AI-enabled physical devices. EdgeQ is a hardware and silicon provider surfaced as a portfolio company of Threshold Ventures; it publishes a corporate site, a 5G engineering blog, newsroom, and careers, but exposes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Enfabrica
providers.description: Enfabrica is a semiconductor company building networking silicon and systems for large-scale AI and accelerated-computing infrastructure. Its ACF-S ("Accelerated Compute Fabric") SuperNIC targets maximum throughput with fault-tolerant, multipath connectivity across AI clusters, and its EMFASYS elastic memory fabric system provides memory offload for AI inference workloads. Enfabrica is backed by Spark Capital. The company publishes a technical blog and company news, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security signals rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Fourier
providers.description: Fourier is an energy technology company building on-site, on-demand hydrogen production systems. Its core product is a modular, scalable device that generates hydrogen where it is needed, removing the transport and storage barriers of conventional hydrogen supply. Fourier targets three application areas: long-duration distributed storage for renewable energy, alternative fuels for heavy transportation, and cleaner feedstock for chemical and manufacturing industries. The company commercially launched its onsite hydrogen system in late 2025 and raised an $18.5M Series A led by Paramark Ventures and General Catalyst. Fourier is a hardware and infrastructure company and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other software developer surface.

providers.name: Kets
providers.description: KETS Quantum Security is a Bristol, UK deep-tech company (incorporated 2016) building chip-based quantum-safe encryption and networking hardware. Its product line spans Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNG), and the KETS KORE sub-system, delivering security grounded in the laws of physics rather than computational complexity. KETS technology hardens telecommunications networks, satellite and aerospace communications (including Airbus collaborations), data-center backups, and critical infrastructure control systems against the emerging threat of quantum computing. Backed by European quantum-specialist venture investors including Speedinvest and supported by multiple UK government funding awards, KETS is a hardware and photonics company; it does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: LINSOL Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: LINSOL Co.,Ltd. (린솔) is a safety-technology company headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, founded as an in-house venture spun out of Hanwha Aerospace. LINSOL adapts acoustic detection techniques originally developed for defense landmine applications into commercial real-time hazard, accident, and environmental detection. Its product line includes Karang F (driving-environment detection), Karang S (precision acoustic signal transmission), SkyShield (fall detection), BR, Acoustic Eye (aerial security), and Safety Nova (smart integrated safety platform), sold into industrial safety, ESG, and defense security use cases. The company operates a Daejeon headquarters and research center plus a Goheung branch. LINSOL ships hardware and integrated platforms; as of a 2026-07-19 probe it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: MITO Material Solutions
providers.description: MITO Material Solutions (MITO Materials) is a specialty chemical company that develops patented hybrid additive technology to strengthen composite and thermoplastic materials. Its platform functionalizes graphene and biomaterials to improve strength, durability, flexibility, and sustainability without requiring changes to a manufacturer's existing process. Core products include the MITO hybrid additive platform, MITO E-GO, MITO E-GO Res-1, and MITO ACRE, serving the sports and recreation, transportation, automotive, and infrastructure industries. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass, MITO publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Mycotech
providers.description: MYCL (Mycotech Lab) is an Indonesian biomaterials company, founded in 2015 and based in Bandung, that cultivates mushroom mycelium on agricultural waste to produce sustainable, carbon-sequestering alternatives to animal leather, plastics, and construction materials. Its flagship product is Mylea, a mycelium-based leather-like material, alongside Biobo binder board, MYCL Composite for architecture and interior design, and Mylea Sea, a seaweed-based biopolymer. A certified B Corp and Good Design Award winner backed by 500 Global and the Unreasonable Group, MYCL sells physical materials and finished goods rather than software; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Mythic
providers.description: Mythic is a high-performance analog computing company building Analog Processing Units (APUs) for energy-efficient AI inference. Its compute-in-memory architecture stores AI model parameters directly in the processor to eliminate the memory bottleneck of traditional digital designs, targeting data center, automotive, robotics, edge, and defense workloads with claims of dramatically lower energy use and cost versus GPUs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and Threshold Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Mythic publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Nabhdrishti Aerospace
providers.description: Nabhdrishti Aerospace is a Bangalore-based deep-tech startup building India's first fuel-flex micro gas turbine for aviation and power generation. Its ND 400 engine is a 400 N single-core micro gas turbine designed for UAVs, hybrid-electric aircraft, and small aircraft as well as oil & gas, manufacturing, and vehicle range-extender power generation, running on conventional fuels, biofuels, and hydrogen with an innovative recuperator design that targets greater than 15% efficiency at under half the cost of competing turbines. Backed by Accel, the company raised USD 3M and operates from the IISc Bangalore IHUB. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks its public web presence.

providers.name: NuScale Power
providers.description: NuScale Power is a Portland, Oregon-based small modular reactor (SMR) company developing the NuScale Power Module (NPM), a 77 MWe pressurized light-water reactor that is the first — and to date one of only two — SMR designs to receive design approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Originally certified in 2020 at 50 MWe and uprated to 77 MWe under the US460 Standard Design Approval issued by the NRC on May 29, 2025, the NPM is delivered as a factory-fabricated, rail-shippable cylindrical containment vessel using passive natural-circulation safety features. Its commercial offering, the VOYGR SMR power plant, is sold in 4-, 6-, and 12-module configurations (308, 462, and 924 MWe respectively) and is targeted at utilities, data centers, hydrogen production, district heating, desalination, and industrial process heat. NuScale traces its origins to Oregon State University research begun in 2000 and was formally founded in 2007; Fluor Corporation became majority investor in 2011. The company went public on the NYSE in 2022 (ticker SMR) through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp., becoming the first publicly traded pure-play SMR vendor. NuScale partners exclusively with ENTRA1 Energy for global commercialization and operates Energy Exploration (E2) Centers — full control-room simulators hosted at Oregon State University, Texas A&M, the University of Idaho, and SNU in South Korea — for operator and regulator training. The high-profile Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS) Carbon Free Power Project at Idaho National Laboratory was terminated in November 2023 after costs rose from $58 to $89/MWh and subscription targets fell short, leaving NuScale without a first-of-a-kind US deployment and prompting a focus on data-center, industrial, and international (Romania RoPower, Poland KGHM, Ghana, Standard Power) opportunities. NuScale's revenue model is power-module sales/leasing, EPC services, and plant lifecycle services — there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release. NPM design data, topical reports, and safety analysis are conveyed through NRC docket filings and topical reports rather than a developer portal.

providers.name: Pacific Fusion
providers.description: Pacific Fusion is a fusion energy company based in Fremont, California developing commercial fusion power using pulsed magnetic inertial fusion. Its modular system pairs a fast electric pulser, a meter-scale fusion chamber, and centimeter-scale fuel targets to pursue net facility gain with practical, affordable manufacturing. Building on breakthroughs from US National Laboratories (Lawrence Livermore, Sandia) and partners such as General Atomics, the company aims to deliver limitless, clean, on-demand power. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, this profile has been enriched through the API Evangelist network. Pacific Fusion is a hardware and energy company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Parasma
providers.description: Parasma is a San Francisco based biological compute startup building algorithms and hardware that train living human brain cells (cortical neurons on a chip) to perform computation for AI workloads. Founded in 2026 by Sean Cole and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch), the company grew out of research that taught a clump of lab-grown human neurons to play Doom, coverage of which appeared in Nature, The Economist, Scientific American, The Guardian and elsewhere. Parasma currently operates as an early-stage research company with a marketing and news website; it does not yet publish a public API, SDK, developer portal, or other machine-readable developer surface. This profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company lead so any future developer platform can be captured when it ships.

providers.name: Quantum Systems
providers.description: Quantum-Systems GmbH is a Gilching/Munich, Germany-based dual-use drone manufacturer founded in 2015 by former Bundeswehr helicopter pilot Florian Seibel. The company designs, builds, and operates small electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for reconnaissance, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition (RSTA), surveying, and mapping. Its flagship platforms include the Trinity Pro (mapping/surveying VTOL with up to 90-minute endurance), the Vector tactical reconnaissance drone (the de facto main small UAS supplier to the German Bundeswehr and, with 619+ systems delivered as of April 2025, one of the most-used Western reconnaissance drones in Ukraine), the Reliant long-range Group 2 ISR/RSTA platform built for the U.S. market with 10+ hours endurance and hot-swappable MOD-compliant payload bays (EO/IR, SIGINT, EW, CRPA), and the Ukraine-manufactured Sparta drone carrier that delivers two FPV drones to a 200 km combat radius. All platforms are operated through QBase 3D, Quantum-Systems' proprietary Windows-based mission planning, control, and post-processing software with integrated ESRI terrain data and direct export to Pix4D, Agisoft, Propeller, and Trimble Business Center. The Vector tactical line is built on Auterion's flight stack. Backed by HV Capital, DTCP, Thiel Capital, Project A, Airbus Ventures, and Omnes Capital, the company reached unicorn status in May 2025 as "Europe's first dual-use unicorn." Quantum-Systems supplies the militaries of Germany, the United States, Ukraine, Australia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Romania, and Spain. There is no public developer API, REST endpoint, SDK, or open-source release for QBase 3D or any Quantum-Systems platform; integration with Pix4D/Agisoft/Propeller/Trimble is via standard photogrammetry file exchange (GeoTIFF, RAW imagery, flight logs), not a programmable API.

providers.name: Quintessent Communications
providers.description: Quintessent is a deep-tech photonics startup based in Goleta, California, developing optical connectivity solutions that address the communication bottlenecks in large-scale computing and AI infrastructure. The company builds chip-to-chip optical interconnect technology grounded in quantum-dot laser epitaxy, and has established supply chains for quantum-dot epitaxial wafers used in AI optical interconnects. Quintessent is a hardware and semiconductor photonics company rather than a software/API provider; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface. Backed by Battery Ventures, Entrada Ventures, Foothill Ventures, and Sierra Ventures, with research funding from DARPA, ARPA-E, and the NSF, the company was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and profiled here for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Related Companies
providers.description: Related Companies is a privately held, fully integrated real estate firm founded by Stephen Ross in 1972 as an affordable-housing developer and now active across luxury residential, affordable housing, retail, office, hospitality, data centers, and city-scale mixed-use development. Related is the developer of Hudson Yards in New York City, The Grand LA, Time Warner Center (now Deutsche Bank Center), The 78 in Chicago, and operates regional platforms including Related Beal, Related Midwest, Related California, Related Ross, and Related Argent in the UK. The firm owns and manages roughly 55,000 affordable and workforce housing units and has stated it has never converted a single affordable unit to market rate. Stephen Ross also owns a majority stake in Equinox Holdings (Equinox fitness clubs, Equinox Hotels, SoulCycle, Blink Fitness) and the Miami Dolphins / Hard Rock Stadium.

providers.name: Standard Kernel
providers.description: Standard Kernel Co. is an AI infrastructure company building a system that automatically generates optimized low-level kernel code — the programs that execute computations on GPUs and TPUs. It aims to eliminate the kernel-engineering bottleneck across the AI stack by combining LLMs with program analysis to produce hardware kernels (matmul, attention, fused feed-forward networks) that match or exceed hand-tuned libraries such as cuBLAS and FlashAttention3, including reported results at 99–116% of cuBLAS on H100 BF16 matmul. Backed by a $20M seed round with participation from General Catalyst, the company is early-stage and does not yet publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: Starcloud
providers.description: Starcloud is developing orbital data centers that run AI and high-performance compute in space. The company aims to deploy hyperscale, gigawatt-scale infrastructure in orbit, using continuous solar energy without batteries and radiative cooling into the vacuum to lower cost, scale beyond terrestrial siting and permitting limits, and deploy rapidly. Backed by Nvidia, Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, NFX and others, Starcloud is building a roadmap of Starcloud-1 through Starcloud-4 satellite compute platforms. As of this profile the company exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a space-compute infrastructure company and lead for future enrichment.

providers.name: TAE Technologies
providers.description: TAE Technologies (formerly Tri Alpha Energy) is a Foothill Ranch, California fusion energy company founded in 1998, pursuing commercial fusion power using aneutronic hydrogen-boron (p-B11) fuel in an advanced beam-driven field-reversed configuration (FRC). Because the p-B11 reaction is aneutronic, TAE's approach produces virtually no neutron flux or on-site radioactive waste compared with conventional deuterium-tritium concepts. The company has built a progression of plasma machines — Sewer Pipe, CBFR-SPS, C-2, C-2U, and C-2W ("Norman") — and is constructing Copernicus in Irvine, California to demonstrate net energy gain, with Da Vinci planned as the grid-connected power-plant demonstration. TAE has raised more than USD 1.2 billion from investors including Google, Chevron, NEA, Goldman Sachs, Vulcan, Venrock, Wellcome Trust, and the Kuwait Investment Authority, and runs research collaborations with Japan's National Institute for Fusion Science (NIFS). Two operating subsidiaries commercialize spin-off technology: TAE Life Sciences develops accelerator-based Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) systems for cancer treatment, and TAE Power Solutions builds modular, software-controlled power-management systems for e-mobility and battery applications. TAE is a private hardware and deep-science company; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or public open-source code repository.

providers.name: Thrive Agritech
providers.description: Thrive Agritech is a horticultural lighting company that designs and manufactures high-efficiency LED grow lights and related power systems for commercial indoor farming, greenhouses, and vertical farming operations. Its product line includes fixtures such as Strata, Boost XE, and a 1050W LED grow light, along with a Remote Power System, backed by lighting design services, rebate assistance, and multi-year warranties. The company positions itself around energy efficiency, ROI, and long-term grower partnerships rather than a developer or API offering. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile was enriched by probing the public web surface; no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification was found.

providers.name: Velaura
providers.description: Velaura AI, Inc. (formerly Auradine) is a Santa Clara, California deep-tech company delivering proven, breakthrough, ultra-low-power compute for cloud, edge, and physical AI applications. Its Titan Core silicon design and IP platform helps AI compute platforms cut power for arithmetic operations while maintaining performance, and its Teraflux line covers high-efficiency Bitcoin mining hardware, ASICs, containers, and fleet-management software. Founded in 2022 by veterans from Qualcomm, Marvell, NVIDIA, Intel, Apple, Google, and Palo Alto Networks, Velaura is backed by Mayfield, Celesta Capital, Mara, StepStone, Maverick Capital, and Premji Invest. As a semiconductor and infrastructure company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Volt14
providers.description: Volt14 Solutions Pte Ltd is a Singapore-based deep-tech startup developing silicon-majority anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. Its fully integrated, tunable, and ready-to-use anodes replace conventional graphite to deliver large gains in energy density and lower normalized cell cost, while remaining compatible with existing battery cell manufacturing infrastructure. Target application markets include electric vehicles, consumer electronics, appliances, and power tools. The company is a materials-science and battery-technology producer; it publishes a corporate and careers website but exposes no public developer or API product surface. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Zetwerk
providers.description: Zetwerk is a global contract-manufacturing and B2B supply-chain company that connects original equipment manufacturers with a vetted network of manufacturing partners across processes including CNC machining, die casting, forging, injection molding, and sheet-metal stamping. It serves industries such as aerospace and defense, automotive, consumer electronics, renewable energy, and industrial equipment, offering production sourcing, quoting, and program management. Backed by Accel, D1 Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Zetwerk operates as a manufacturing services marketplace rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: 21Vianet
providers.description: 21Vianet (VNET Group, Inc.) is the largest carrier-neutral internet and data center services provider in China, operating more than 50 data centers across over 20 cities with tens of thousands of cabinets and multi-terabit network port capacity. The company delivers hosting, managed hosting, interconnectivity, cloud, and hybrid IT infrastructure services to enterprise customers, and is the exclusive operator of Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform in mainland China through its Blue Cloud subsidiary. 21Vianet trades on Nasdaq under the ticker VNET. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; 21Vianet does not publish a public first-party developer API program, so most API artifacts are legitimately not applicable.

providers.name: 3com
providers.description: 3Com Corporation was a networking-technology pioneer founded in 1979 by Robert Metcalfe, the co-inventor of Ethernet, and colleagues; its name derived from "Computer, Communication, and Compatibility." 3Com built Ethernet network interface cards, switches, routers, and enterprise networking and security hardware, and at one point owned the Palm handheld computing business. An early Mayfield Fund portfolio investment (seed participation in 1981, alongside NEA, Venrock, and Sequoia), 3Com later operated the 3Com, H3C, and TippingPoint brands before being acquired by Hewlett-Packard in 2010 for roughly $2.7 billion, after which the standalone brand was wound down. This record is a historical company profile; 3Com no longer operates an independent developer portal, public API, or live product surface (the 3com.com domain now serves a placeholder page).

providers.name: 6thSense
providers.description: 6thSense is a physical-AI hardware company building the touch layer for dexterous robots. It designs and manufactures wearable tactile-sensing data gloves that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and 3D hand pose — alongside custom tactile skin molded to robot hands. Its capture stack synchronizes eight aligned modalities (tactile and pressure proxies, egocentric video, depth/RGB-D, hand pose, motion and IMU dynamics, wrist and scene cameras, dense labels and commentary, and success/failure outcomes) into model-ready demonstration datasets used to train the next generation of dexterous, manipulation-capable robots. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (S26).

providers.name: 9 Mothers Corporation
providers.description: 9 Mothers Corporation is a defense technology company founded in 2024 and based in Austin, Texas, building AI-powered counter-drone (C-sUAS) point defense systems for the FPV drone era. Its flagship product, EDDA, is a small, low-power, autonomous-capable point-defense turret that engages Group 1 suicide drones at 10-100+ meter range to protect soldiers, vehicles, and critical assets. A Y Combinator Spring 2026 company with reported sales to the U.S. Department of War, its roadmap includes Vor (passive acoustic sensor), Atla (belt-fed shotgun system), and Gleipnir (counter-drone for larger platforms). This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Advanced Analogic Technologies (AnalogicTech)
providers.description: Advanced Analogic Technologies Incorporated (AnalogicTech, formerly NASDAQ: AATI) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1997 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, with design centers in Santa Clara and Shanghai. The company designed total power-management solutions built on proprietary analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and discrete power MOSFETs, shipping a portfolio of more than 500 power-management application-specific standard products (ASSPs) and general-purpose analog ICs across four application areas: display and lighting, voltage regulation and DC/DC conversion, interface and power management, and battery management, primarily for mobile and portable consumer electronics. Advanced Analogic Technologies was acquired by Skyworks Solutions, Inc. in January 2011 and no longer operates as an independent company; it is a hardware semiconductor manufacturer with no public web API, developer platform, or API artifacts. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a company record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Advanced Metal Research
providers.description: Advanced Metal Research is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in Los Angeles building machine intelligence for American welding. The company develops American-made robotic welding cells that pair computer vision with real-time seam tracking and post-weld inspection, turning welding from a scarce manual craft into a closed-loop manufacturing system that learns from every weld as it happens. Founded in 2025 by Julian Fried, Stephen Lin, and Angus Muffatti, it targets the projected shortage of skilled welding professionals across US industrial manufacturing. The company is early-stage and hardware-focused; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Advent Solar
providers.description: Advent Solar was a silicon photovoltaic company founded in 2002 and headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico, that designed and manufactured crystalline-silicon (c-Si) solar cells and modules, pioneering emitter-wrap-through cell architectures and streamlined back-contact module assembly. Backed by Battery Ventures, EnerTech Capital, @Ventures and others across roughly $109M in venture funding (including a $70M Series D in 2007), the company's assets and intellectual property were acquired by Applied Materials in late 2009 / 2010. As a physical solar-hardware manufacturer that is no longer operating independently, Advent Solar exposes no public API, developer portal, or software surface; this profile is retained as a network identity record with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: airquality
providers.description: AirQuality (爱优特) is a Shanghai-based manufacturer of high-efficiency electrostatic air purification and disinfection products, including central air filtration systems, commercial kitchen exhaust (hood) cleaners, odor-elimination units, and smart air-quality detection systems for schools, hospitals, offices, shopping malls, and hotels. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is a hardware/manufacturing business that publishes a consumer website and online shop but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so most enrichment artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Akash Systems
providers.description: Akash Systems is an Oakland, California deep-tech semiconductor company that pioneers Diamond Cooling thermal-management technology, integrating synthetic diamond directly with semiconductors such as Gallium Nitride (GaN) to remove heat up to five times faster than copper. Its Chip-on-Diamond and diamond-cooled server products target AI and data-center compute, while its GaN power amplifiers and satellite radios serve space communications, radar, cellular, and automotive/EV markets. Akash Systems is a hardware and materials company with no public developer API or documentation surface; it was surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Aliena
providers.description: Aliena is a Singapore-based space-technology company, incorporated in 2018, that designs and manufactures compact electric propulsion systems for small satellites. Its MUSIC plasma thruster line delivers high thrust-to-power ratios at very low power budgets with high specific impulse, enabling small satellites to operate and sustain very low Earth orbit (VLEO) for high-resolution remote sensing. Aliena is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Allevi
providers.description: Allevi is a bioprinting company that designs and manufactures 3D bioprinters, bioinks, and accompanying software for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and life-sciences research. Its desktop bioprinters and biomaterials let researchers fabricate living tissue constructs for drug discovery, disease modeling, and organ-on-chip work. Allevi was acquired by 3D Systems and operates as part of its regenerative medicine portfolio. The company publishes bioprinting protocols, application notes, webinars, and white papers, but exposes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Alpha Technologies
providers.description: Alpha Technologies is a power-systems manufacturer providing AC, DC, and renewable powering solutions for the telecom, cable-broadband, traffic, security, industrial, and alternative-energy industries. Its product line spans uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), standby and non-standby power systems, batteries, enclosures, network/fiber powering gear, and renewable-energy products. Founded in the 1980s and now part of EnerSys, Alpha operates as a hardware and stored-energy solutions provider rather than a public API platform; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an Accel-associated portfolio lead and carries no public developer or API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Amalfi Semiconductor
providers.description: Amalfi Semiconductor was a fabless developer of high-performance CMOS radio frequency (RF) and mixed-signal semiconductors for cellular handsets. Its proprietary CMOS-based AdaptiveRF architecture delivered power amplifiers that extended battery life and talk time while reducing the size and cost of front-end cellular handset designs, shipping over 100 million CMOS power amplifiers. Battery Ventures led the company's $24M Series C in 2009, with further investment in 2012 alongside DCM and Globespan Capital Partners. Amalfi Semiconductor was acquired by RF Micro Devices (now part of Qorvo) in November 2012 for $47.5M in cash. The company is defunct as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; this profile is retained for network and portfolio-graph completeness rather than API enrichment.

providers.name: Amber Wave
providers.description: AmberWave, Inc. (formerly AmberWave Systems Corporation) is a Lowell, Massachusetts deep-technology company that researches, develops, and licenses semiconductor and photovoltaic materials technology. It originated strained-silicon and aspect-ratio-trapping techniques from MIT and Bell Labs research, and today develops Ultra-Thin Silicon (UTSi) flexible solar cells and modules that weigh roughly 90% less than conventional panels, targeting lightweight commercial rooftops, off-grid power, building integration, vehicle, and aerospace applications. AmberWave is a Battery Ventures portfolio company. It publishes a corporate website but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so there are no machine-readable API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: AMCC
providers.description: AMCC (Applied Micro Circuits Corporation, also known as AppliedMicro or APM) was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 1979 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It designed network and embedded Power ISA processors, ARMv8-A server processors (the X-Gene line), and optical transport, connectivity, and storage silicon for telecommunications, data center, and industrial markets. Backed by Matrix Partners, U.S. Venture Partners, and other venture investors, AMCC traded on NASDAQ under the ticker AMCC. It was acquired by MACOM Technology Solutions (NASDAQ: MTSI) in January 2017 and no longer operates as an independent company. As a fabless chip designer with no public developer platform, AMCC exposes no APIs, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is retained as a historical company record and Matrix Partners portfolio lead.

providers.name: AMCC (Applied Micro Circuits Corporation)
providers.description: Applied Micro Circuits Corporation (AMCC) was a California-based semiconductor company founded in 1979, originally producing application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for the military market before diversifying into commercial mixed-signal, networking, storage, and embedded processor products. AMCC went public on NASDAQ in 1997, acquired MMC Networks in 2000, and bought IBM's PowerPC 400 processor line in 2004. Under the AppliedMicro brand it later developed the X-Gene ARM 64-bit server-on-chip family. AMCC ceased to exist as an independent entity when MACOM completed its acquisition on January 26, 2017; the X-Gene compute business was subsequently spun out to form Ampere Computing. As a fabless silicon/hardware company (now defunct), AMCC published no public developer API surface, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: AMP Fund
providers.description: AMP (AMP PBC) is a public benefit corporation founded in 2025 by Anjney Midha, a former Andreessen Horowitz general partner, to build an independent "AI grid" — a pooled compute utility for frontier AI research teams. Rather than operating as a cloud provider or a conventional venture firm, AMP acts as an independent system operator: data center operators and labs contribute underutilized GPU capacity to a shared network, and member research teams draw base-load and burst compute from that pool at rates intended to sit below the volatile spot market. AMP pairs capital with compute, having raised roughly $1.3 billion for its first fund, and its PBC charter is structured so leadership can supply compute at cost without shareholder challenge. It has also committed a Public Wealth Fund of up to $500 million through 2030 toward education, workforce readiness, healthcare access, and economic resilience in communities affected by the AI transition. AMP publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Amphiform
providers.description: Amphiform is an energy technology company redefining the future of energy by developing new materials and manufacturing processes that create clean, abundant, and dense energy sources. Rather than scaling existing technologies, Amphiform engineers entirely new materials using precise manufacturing tools to address energy demands for decarbonization, computing, and space exploration. A General Catalyst portfolio company in the energy-infrastructure sector, it is pre-product and does not currently publish any public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Anobit Technologies
providers.description: Anobit Technologies was an Israeli fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2006, that developed flash-memory Memory Signal Processing (MSP) controller technology to extend the endurance, reliability, and performance of consumer-grade NAND flash used in SSDs and mobile devices. Backed by Battery Ventures among others, Anobit was acquired by Apple in early 2012 and no longer operates as an independent company. It has no public developer surface, API program, or live web presence, and remains in the API Evangelist network only as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Apex Space
providers.description: Apex Space (Apex) is a Los Angeles based satellite manufacturing company that builds productized, configurable spacecraft bus platforms for proliferated constellations across LEO, MEO, and GEO orbital regimes. Apex offers three product lines: Aries (small satellites up to 150 kg payload), Nova (medium satellites up to 300 kg payload), and Comet (large satellites up to 3,000 kg payload), and operates Factory One, a high-rate manufacturing facility in Los Angeles with the capacity to produce more than 200 satellites annually. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Apex does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; customers configure satellite platforms through the on-site Configurator and direct sales inquiries.

providers.name: Apigy
providers.description: Apigy, Inc. is the company behind Lockitron, an early keyless smart-lock startup that let people lock, unlock, and share access to their doors from a smartphone. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and known for a large 2012 crowdfunding campaign, Apigy built connected door-lock hardware and companion mobile apps before the Lockitron product line was wound down. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; its public website (lockitron.com) is currently unreachable and no active developer or API surface could be located.

providers.name: AppAssure Software (Dell)
providers.description: AppAssure Software was a data-protection vendor (backup, replication, and recovery for physical, virtual, and cloud systems) funded by Bain Capital Ventures before Dell acquired it in 2012. Its flagship AppAssure 5 platform shipped a bundled service-management REST API for programmatically driving backup, replication, and recovery from the Management Console. The product line has since been retired and folded into what is now Quest Rapid Recovery; there is no active public developer portal, hosted API host, or machine-readable specification. This profile is retained for network completeness and lineage rather than as a live, integrable API surface.

providers.name: Arcturus
providers.description: Arcturus (Arcturus Technologies) is a Los Angeles advanced-materials company founded by Amir Mashal that infuses carbon nanomaterials into metals to create a new class of conductors, using lasers to embed carbon into copper and dramatically improve its electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance. Positioned in frontier climate/energy tech, its drop-in materials target motor windings, bus bars, heat sinks, data-center infrastructure, electric motors, drones, robotics, and — over time — transmission lines and grid infrastructure. The company emerged from stealth in June 2026 with an $8M seed round led by Initialized Capital, with 1517, Breakthrough Energy Discovery, Toyota Ventures, and Wireframe Ventures participating. This is a deep-tech hardware/materials company with no public API or developer program; the profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Arilinc
providers.description: Aril Inc. (Arilinc) is a fabless semiconductor company in Los Gatos, California designing efficient AI processors and memory technology for edge inference. Its two core products are the Aril Standard Cell Memory, a patented on-chip memory offering roughly 40% lower active power and 3.6x smaller area, and a scalable RISC-V-based AI Processor Engine delivering hundreds of TOPS of inference per block with integrated vector and matrix engines. The company targets robotics, industrial automation, drones, defense and aerospace, autonomous vehicles, and edge vision systems where power efficiency is critical. Founded by a team of engineers who have collectively shipped 20M+ processors and worked on silicon for Cisco, Intel, AMD, and Google. Arilinc sells custom silicon and IP to hardware makers rather than a public developer API; it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Ascend Communications
providers.description: Ascend Communications, Inc. was an Alameda, California manufacturer of wide area networking equipment, founded in 1988 and taken public in 1994. It developed, manufactured and sold WAN access solutions — remote-access concentrators, ISDN and frame relay gear, and the MAX family of access servers — to telecommunications carriers, Internet service providers and corporate customers worldwide, becoming a leading supplier during the dial-up internet build-out of the 1990s. On January 13, 1999 Lucent Technologies announced a definitive agreement to merge with Ascend in a stock deal valued at roughly $20.3 billion, and the merger completed on June 24, 1999, when Ascend became a wholly owned subsidiary of Lucent. The company has not operated independently since. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company; it predates the public web API era and publishes no developer surface today.

providers.name: Asetek
providers.description: Asetek designs and builds liquid cooling and thermal-management technology. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Aalborg, Denmark, the company pioneered all-in-one (AIO) closed-loop liquid coolers for enthusiast and gaming PCs and supplies OEM cooling to major PC and workstation brands. Its data-center and high-performance-computing business delivers direct-to-chip liquid cooling for servers and racks, and its Asetek SimSports division makes premium sim-racing hardware such as force-feedback wheelbases and load-cell pedals. Asetek is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and enriched with what is publicly verifiable (domain-security posture).

providers.name: asgoodasnew
providers.description: asgoodasnew is a German e-commerce retailer of refurbished and pre-owned consumer electronics, including smartphones, tablets, laptops, cameras, and related accessories, sold with warranty through its online store at asgoodasnew.de (asgoodasnew.com redirects there). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Probing the public surface found no developer portal, API documentation, or API host — this is a consumer-facing storefront with no public API program at this time. The profile is retained as a portfolio lead; only mechanical domain-security signals for the web host could be captured.

providers.name: Atrisa
providers.description: Atrisa (formerly Refortifai) is a Y Combinator (P26) startup building AI agents for analog circuit design. The product is a chat-based assistant engineer that lets hardware and analog design teams ask it, in natural language, to create a design, debug a circuit, or run simulations. Atrisa is designed to fit into existing workflows: teams bring their own toolkit, PDKs (process design kits), and design documents, which Atrisa reads, understands, and adopts to produce schematic-level outputs and iterate on analog designs. As an early-stage company it currently ships a hosted web application rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public surface pending any future API release.

providers.name: Avanex
providers.description: Avanex Corporation was a fiber-optic components manufacturer founded in 1997 and headquartered in Fremont, California, backed by Mayfield along with Crosspoint Venture Partners, JAFCO America and Sequoia Capital. Avanex designed and built photonic processors, optical components, modules and subsystems used to raise the speed and capacity of fiber-optic communication networks, and went public on NASDAQ in February 2000 raising $216 million. In April 2009 Avanex merged with Bookham Technology to form Oclaro, and Oclaro was in turn acquired by Lumentum in December 2018. Avanex is no longer an operating company: it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API of any kind, and the avanex.com domain is now a parked GoDaddy for-sale listing. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lineage record only.

providers.name: Avegant
providers.description: Avegant is an augmented reality display technology company that develops light engine technology bringing high-performance visuals to lightweight AR glasses designed for everyday wear. Its flagship product, the AG-30L2 LED light engine, is described as the world's smallest LED light engine for augmented reality. Avegant is a venture-backed hardware company (a portfolio company of 500 Global) focused on the optical and display components that power the next generation of AR eyewear rather than on a public developer platform. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Avere Systems
providers.description: Avere Systems was a Pittsburgh-based enterprise storage company building hybrid cloud NAS technology, best known for its FXT Series Edge filers and the vFXT virtual appliance that accelerated and tiered file workloads across on-premises NAS and public cloud object storage. The company was acquired by Microsoft in January 2018 and folded into Microsoft Azure, where the technology lives on as Avere vFXT for Azure. Avere Systems no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal or public API of its own; its former domain (averesystems.com) now 301-redirects to Microsoft's Avere landing page.

providers.name: Avnera
providers.description: Avnera Corporation was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon, that designed low-power analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits and audio system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for wireless headphones, headsets, soundbars, speakers, and gaming audio devices. Backed by venture investors including Redpoint Ventures, Avnera was acquired by Skyworks Solutions in 2017 and now operates as part of Skyworks. It maintains no independent developer program or public API surface; the avnera.com domain resolves to a parked/inactive page with no product site.

providers.name: Awavesemi
providers.description: Awavesemi (Awave Semiconductor) is a semiconductor company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass, its domain awavesemi.com issues a 301 redirect to https://www.qualcomm.com/data-center, indicating the company and its data-center silicon effort have been absorbed into Qualcomm. Awavesemi publishes no independent developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or MCP surface — it is a hardware/silicon company, not an API provider, so the enrichment pipeline finds no API artifacts to harvest beyond domain-level security posture.

providers.name: Baya Systems
providers.description: Baya Systems is a semiconductor IP company accelerating intelligent compute with chiplets. Backed by Matrix Partners and Intel Capital and based in Santa Clara, California (with offices in Austin, Texas and Bengaluru, India), Baya provides the WeaverPro software platform and the WeaveIP unified fabric and cache IP portfolio. Together they let system architects analyze, design and post-silicon tune optimal single-die or multi-die, chiplet-ready Network-on-Chip (NoC) interconnect systems, with multi-level coherency and multicast for AI acceleration scaling into petabytes per second across hyperscale, enterprise, AI, automotive, GPU and IoT markets. Baya Systems does not publish a public developer API, portal or SDK at this time; this API Evangelist network profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Bear Flag Robotics
providers.description: Bear Flag Robotics is an autonomous-tractor company that retrofits existing farm tractors with sensors, onboard compute, and path-planning software to enable driverless field operations such as tillage and row-crop work. Founded in 2017 and backed by Y Combinator and True Ventures, the company was acquired by John Deere in August 2021 and now advances Deere's autonomy roadmap. It is a hardware and agricultural-robotics business with no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or GitHub surface; its website redirects to John Deere.

providers.name: Bedrock Materials
providers.description: Bedrock Materials was a Chicago-based deep-tech startup founded in 2023 by Spencer Gore (CEO, previously Tesla and Enovix) and Rafael Vila (CTO, Stanford battery scientist) to manufacture engineered sodium-ion cathode active materials as a low-cost, easy-to-source alternative to lithium-ion — built from abundant sodium, manganese, iron and aluminum, and designed to drop into existing lithium-ion cell manufacturing lines for low-voltage, starter-lighting-ignition, micromobility and industrial-traction applications. It raised a $9M seed round led by Trucks Venture Capital with Refactor Capital and Version One Ventures. In April 2025 the company wound down and returned the majority of that seed capital to its investors: CEO Spencer Gore concluded that sodium-ion could not be produced cheaply enough to beat lithium iron phosphate (LFP) after lithium oversupply collapsed prices, and that energy-density gains carried steep trade-offs. Bedrock Materials was a materials-science manufacturer and never operated a developer program, public API, or developer portal; both bedrockmaterials.com and its former bedrock.inc website are now parked/for-sale domains with no company content. This profile is retained as a verified-defunct record in the API Evangelist network — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Beyond Reach Labs
providers.description: Beyond Reach Labs is a Brooklyn, New York aerospace company building deployable solar arrays and thermal radiators for spacecraft that expand from compact launch sizes to enormous structures in orbit. Its patented geometry-changing panels grow from the size of a dining table to a football field once deployed, giving satellites, orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts up to 10x more usable power without adding launch mass or volume. Founded by two aerospace engineers, the company is targeting its first in-space demonstration in Q2 2027 and is a Y Combinator portfolio company. Beyond Reach Labs is a hardware manufacturer and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Bilimber Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Bilimber Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based private company (exempt private company limited by shares) incorporated on 2020-11-17, operating in research and experimental development on electronics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (an early/seed-stage investor alongside a Hong Kong government program) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface -- the bilimber.com domain is currently unregistered and does not resolve -- so no first-party API artifacts could be searched, derived, or generated. This profile remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: Bitcasa
providers.description: Bitcasa, Inc. was an American cloud storage company (founded 2011 in St. Louis, Missouri; later based in Mountain View, California) known for its converged/infinite storage model and, for developers, the CloudFS API — a white-label cloud-storage platform that let third-party applications integrate file management, secure sharing, media transcoding, instant streaming, and zero-knowledge client-side encryption. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), CrunchFund, Pelion Venture Partners, Horizons Ventures, Samsung Ventures, and First Round Capital, Bitcasa wound down its consumer Bitcasa Drive service in 2016 and shut down all services in 2017. The company is defunct and the bitcasa.com domain is now parked, so no live developer surface, API documentation, or specifications remain to enrich.

providers.name: Bracket Computing
providers.description: Bracket Computing was a cloud computing and enterprise security company founded in 2011 by Tom Gillis and Jason Lango (both formerly of IronPort Systems) and based in Mountain View, California. It built a cloud workload-isolation platform that extended encryption, integrity protection, and micro-segmentation across heterogeneous public and private cloud environments. The company raised roughly $130 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Fidelity, Goldman Sachs, and Sutter Hill Ventures before VMware acquired its intellectual property and key engineers on May 1, 2018, folding the technology into the VMware NSX networking and security portfolio. Bracket Computing no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; its primary domain now resolves to a parked domain-for-sale page.

providers.name: Bridgeco
providers.description: BridgeCo Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 that built networked-audio silicon and software for consumer electronics. Its JukeBlox platform — a system-on-a-chip paired with a software development kit — let wireless speakers, A/V receivers, home-theater systems and docking stations stream music from tablets, smartphones and PCs, and was designed into products from Pioneer, Philips, Denon, Marantz, JBL and Harman/Kardon. Earlybird Venture Capital was the company's first institutional investor in 2000. BridgeCo was acquired by Standard Microsystems Corporation (SMSC) on 19 May 2011 in a deal worth up to $67.5 million, and SMSC was in turn acquired by Microchip Technology on 2 August 2012, where the JukeBlox wireless-audio line was folded into Microchip's portfolio. BridgeCo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation or public API; the bridgeco.com domain today is an unrelated domain-for-sale parking page.

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: Britesemi
providers.description: Britesemi (Brite Semiconductor / 灿芯半导体（上海）股份有限公司, Shanghai, stock ticker 688691) is a one-stop custom chip and silicon IP supplier. It provides ASIC design services spanning chip specification definition, SoC and mixed-signal design architecture, backend design, and final product delivery, alongside a family of proprietary YouIP interface IP cores (YouDDR, YouSerdes, YouUSB, YouMIPI, YouPCIe, YouONFI, YouIO, YouRF, YouADC). This is a semiconductor / ASIC design-services business, not a public web-API provider: enrichment found no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of norwest-venture-partners.

providers.name: Bumblebee Spaces
providers.description: Bumblebee Spaces is a San Francisco smart-home robotics company that builds app-controlled motorized storage systems for compact urban living. Its ceiling-mounted robotic units lift beds, closets, and storage bins up and out of the way, reclaiming floor space in small apartments, while a built-in camera and mobile app track and retrieve stored belongings on demand. The company sells and installs hardware plus a companion consumer mobile application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Canaan Partners, the profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: CAD Solutions
providers.description: CAD Solutions, Inc. is a historical Battery Ventures portfolio company that appears in the firm's all-companies list. Research during the API Evangelist enrichment pass found no operating business, no developer surface, and no live web presence behind the name - public records indicate the company was acquired by microCAD Solutions on 1995-05-29, and the closest matching domain, cadsolutions.com, now resolves to a GoDaddy parked "for sale" page rather than a company site. The many unrelated "CAD Solutions" businesses currently trading under similar names (CAD Solutions LLC, CAD Solutions Inc of Dassault partner fame, CADD Solutions, CAD-E Solutions) are separate entities and are not this Battery portfolio record. This profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead with no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Calista Technologies
providers.description: Calista Technologies was a desktop and GPU virtualization startup founded in 2006 in San Jose, California by Neal Margulis, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Greylock, and Western Technology Investment. Its software improved the user experience of 3-D and multimedia delivery for virtualized desktop deployments and server-hosted applications running on Windows Server Terminal Services (Remote Desktop). Microsoft acquired the company in 2008 and folded its GPU-virtualization technology into RemoteFX. The company is defunct and publishes no live developer, documentation, or API surface; its former domain (calistatechnologies.com) is now a parked domain listed for sale.

providers.name: Cambridge Aerospace
providers.description: Cambridge Aerospace is a UK-based defense technology company, incorporated in September 2024, developing scalable interceptor missiles and sovereign air-and-missile-defense systems for European nations. Its first product, Skyhammer, is a tube-launched subsonic interceptor with a Cambridge-developed radar seeker, positioned as an affordable, mass-producible counter to drones and cruise missiles (often likened to an Iron Dome-style layered air defense). The company operates in the aerospace and defense/security sector and is backed by a venture syndicate including Accel, Lakestar, Lux Capital, Spark Capital, and the D3 fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel; it is a hardware-first defense company with no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Cavium
providers.description: Cavium, Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 and headquartered in San Jose, California, that designed multicore processors and networking silicon for enterprise, data center, cloud, and service-provider infrastructure. Its product families included OCTEON multicore MIPS and ARM network and security processors, ThunderX ARM-based server SoCs, Nitrox security processors, LiquidIO intelligent adapters and smart NICs, and the FastLinQ Ethernet and Xpliant switch lines it gained through its 2016 acquisition of QLogic. Cavium was a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: CAVM) before being acquired by Marvell Technology Group in July 2018 for roughly 6 billion US dollars. Its technology now ships as part of Marvell's networking and infrastructure processor portfolio. As a silicon and hardware vendor, Cavium never operated a public developer API program or web API surface.

providers.name: Cencorp
providers.description: Cencorp (Zhuhai) Industrial Technology Co., Ltd. is a process-automation equipment manufacturer that designs and builds high-end laser processing, dispensing, automated optical inspection (AOI), and system-integration & automation systems for the consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor, and new-energy industries. Formed in 2020 and combining the acquired Finland-based Cencorp automation business with operations headquartered in Zhuhai, China, the company runs 12 offices worldwide with 400+ R&D engineers and 300+ patents, and is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this is a physical automation-equipment business.

providers.name: Chariot Defense
providers.description: Chariot Defense is a San Francisco-area defense technology company building high-voltage, hybrid-electric power systems for the modern battlefield. Its AMPHORA family (the 24 VDC / 5 kW A24 and the 400 VDC / 35 kW A400) and the upcoming VANGUARD platform deliver quiet, high-density, transportable power that replaces loud, fuel-hungry diesel generators, cutting energy signature and fuel use while powering distributed systems such as drones, sensors, electronic warfare, command and control, additive manufacturing, and directed-energy weapons. Founded in 2022 by Adam Warmoth, the company has raised $41M (a $34M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz plus an $8M seed) and its systems are fielded by the U.S. Army and the Defense Innovation Unit. This is a hardware/defense company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Cinta Networks
providers.description: Cinta Networks, Incorporated was a venture-backed optical networking equipment startup of the dot-com era, funded in part by Battery Ventures and led by CEO John Vaughan. The company built the patented WAVEJunction product family, an architecture that integrated DWDM optical transport with optical switching in a single network element for metro, regional, and long-haul carrier networks, claiming capital-expense savings of more than 50 percent and operational savings of over 70 percent through modular, port-at-a-time growth, universal transponder cards, and dynamic wavelength reconfiguration across ring and mesh topologies. Public activity is visible from roughly 2000 to 2002, including a January 2002 WAVEJunction field-trial agreement with Pacific LightNet and a component supply arrangement with ADC. Cinta Networks appears to have ceased operations in the post-telecom-bust period: archived captures of cintanetworks.com show the site replaced by a parked domain-search page by 2004, and the domain no longer resolves in DNS as of July 2026. Cinta was a hardware manufacturer and never published a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record.

providers.name: Circularity Fuels
providers.description: Circularity Fuels builds AI-controlled, mass-manufacturable reactors that turn waste carbon and cheap renewable power into drop-in hydrocarbons, starting with affordable sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Its Ouro Reactor reforms waste carbon (methane and CO2 off-gassed by dairy farms, agricultural plants, and industrial facilities) into clean syngas, and its Aion Reactor uses next-generation Fischer-Tropsch synthesis to assemble that syngas into liquid fuels. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. It is a hardware and process company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Citadel
providers.description: Citadel (also branded Citadel Defense / Drone Citadel) is a counter-unmanned-aircraft-system (C-UAS) company founded in 2016 that built an automated, modular drone-defense solution using proprietary machine-learning algorithms to detect, classify, and defeat unauthorized drones. It raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series A in 2017 and was subsequently acquired by BlueHalo. The company operates no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, and its standalone domains (citadeldefense.com, dronecitadel.com) are now parked or no longer resolve.

providers.name: Cloudsimple
providers.description: CloudSimple was an enterprise software company that ran secure, dedicated VMware workloads (VMware Cloud Foundation - vSphere, vSAN, NSX) as a managed service on public clouds, originally partnering with Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. Google Cloud acquired CloudSimple in November 2019 and folded the technology into Google Cloud VMware Engine; the standalone company, product, and developer surface no longer exist. The former domain (cloudsimple.com) resolves to a Google-owned IP but serves no live website, documentation, or API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and Redpoint Ventures and remains in the API Evangelist network as a historical / defunct-provider record; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Clusterk
providers.description: ClusterK was a cloud cost-optimization startup founded in 2013 in Palo Alto, California by Dmitry Pushkarev. Its software let AWS users run production and batch workloads on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances at up to 90% savings versus on-demand pricing, by predicting spot-market prices and continuously rebalancing capacity across instance types. ClusterK shipped two products: ClusterK Balancer, which arbitraged the AWS Spot Market for cost savings, and ClusterK Cirrus, a cloud-native HPC grid scheduler. The company was backed by DCVC (Data Collective), Rally Ventures, and the Mayo Clinic Business Accelerator, raising roughly $1.2M. Amazon acquired ClusterK in April 2015 and absorbed the team and technology into AWS; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

providers.name: Coho Data
providers.description: Coho Data was a scale-out enterprise storage startup based in Sunnyvale, California, founded in 2011 (originally as Convergent.io) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz among others. It built a software-defined storage platform that combined commodity flash and software-defined networking to deliver scalable NFS/object storage for private clouds.
